## #1379: the run reports its walk and the wizard draws it (Opus implementer, 2026-10-20)

- **Reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus: sign-off on the contract amendment.**
  *Fork:* sign off on `Sink::walked` and the three `SyncProgress` fields as booked in
  `docs/contract/10.8/1379-the-run-reports-its-walk.md`, or hold the PR. *Ruling:* signed off.
  *Reasoning:* both are additive. The `Sink` method has a do-nothing default, so no existing sink
  or adapter changes; the fields are absent on the wire when nobody reports, so no reader of
  `SyncProgress` changes. It is the surface #1378 decided on (Björn, 2026-10-20) and #1380–#1384
  build on it as written. *Reversing:* drop the method and the fields; the follow-ups would have to
  be re-cut.
- **The field names.** *Fork:* the ticket describes the fields as "done, total, unit"; the parent
  spec names them `walked`, `of`, `unit`. *Ruling:* `walked`, `of`, `unit`. *Reasoning:* the
  ticket describes, the spec names, and the five follow-ups were cut from the spec. The `Sink`
  method's arguments keep the spec's `done`, `of`, `unit`. *Reversing:* a rename across the
  engine, the mirror and the wizard, before any follow-up lands.
- **Absent or `null`.** *Fork:* `Option` fields serialised as `null` (as `message` is), or skipped
  when `None` and optional in TypeScript. *Ruling:* skipped (`skip_serializing_if`,
  `#[serde(default)]`, `#[ts(optional)]`). *Reasoning:* the ticket's first criterion says
  "absent"; an optional field leaves every hand-written `SyncProgress` literal in the frontend
  (tests, fakes) valid. *Reversing:* three attribute lines and a regenerated mirror.
- **Which throttle a reading rides.** *Fork:* the item path's time clock only (250 ms), or that
  and its every-250-items count. *Ruling:* the clock only. The first reading goes out at once,
  since the clock starts one throttle in the past. *Reasoning:* the count rule exists so a burst of
  items between ticks is not lost; a reading is a single latest value that the next tick or the
  final `fetching` sample carries anyway, and a unit is often hundreds of requests, so a reading
  every 250 units would rarely fire. *Reversing:* one condition in `Counting::walked`.
- **What the wizard does with a message that has no reading.** *Ruling:* keeps the last reading
  until a new sync starts. *Reasoning:* only the engine's decorator sends readings; the scheduler's
  `started` and ending messages never do, and a failure panel should still say how far the walk
  got. *Reversing:* one `if` in `FirstRun.svelte`.
- **A total of zero.** *Ruling:* the bar stays indeterminate (`of > 0` to draw a maximum).
  *Reasoning:* `<progress max="0">` is invalid and falls back to 1. *Reversing:* one comparison.
- **Number format.** *Fork:* the ticket's sample reading "1,240 items · 83 s", or the wizard's
  existing "40 items · 0.9 s". *Ruling:* the existing format, with the walk in plain digits:
  "120 of 300 repositories · 0 items · 8.3 s". *Reasoning:* the sample illustrates the order of
  the parts; changing how items and seconds print is not this ticket's work and would move
  assertions it does not own. *Reversing:* a formatter in the reading line.
- **What the mock counts.** *Ruling:* every item it pushes, the opt-in tombstone included; a run
  already at the current cursor pushes nothing and reports nothing. *Reversing:* one line.
- **No screenshot.** The fake IPC answers `sync_now_with_progress` with a run id and sends no
  progress message, so `just shot` cannot draw the bar mid-run. Teaching the fake to stream is out
  of scope; the component test witnesses the drawing.
- **Merge-manager on Opus: the sign-off ruling stands.** *Fork:* confirm the implementer's
  sign-off on the amendment or hold the PR. *Ruling:* confirmed. *Reasoning:* the deep pass found
  the §10.8 entry matches the diff. `walked` has a do-nothing default; the one wrapping sink
  (`Counting`) forwards it, and no other decorator sits between an adapter and the engine's sink.
  The fields are absent on the wire when nothing reports, and the names are the ones the parent
  spec and #1380–#1384 use. Björn said on 2026-10-20 that Opus may amend without him.
  *Reversing:* as above.
- **Merge-manager: the two reviewer suggestions stay unapplied** (one reading type in place of three
  fields; one shared test sink in place of four copies). *Ruling:* unapplied. *Reasoning:* the
  ticket and the parent spec name three `Option` fields on `SyncProgress`, and the follow-ups are
  cut against that shape. The test sinks are local to their crates' test binaries. *Reversing:* a
  refactor after #1384 lands.

## #1382 — TeamCity reports its walk

- **What the incremental walk counts.** *Fork:* the builds the run listed (in-flight plus finished,
  deduplicated by id, in or out of scope), or only those it emits. *Ruling:* the listed ones, unit
  `builds`; the full sync reports `build configurations`. *Reasoning:* the ticket says "against the
  count it listed", and a run whose listed builds are all out of scope must still move the bar.
  *Reversing:* the `observed` count in `sync.rs`.
- **Empty listing.** *Ruling:* an incremental run that lists nothing reports one closing `0 of 0
  builds`, like Gitea's empty selection. *Reversing:* one `if`.
- **Where the reading sits.** *Ruling:* the incremental readings go in the scope-and-map loop, not
  the emit loop, because the emit loop also pushes configurations the count does not cover.
  *Reversing:* move the calls.
## #1380: a WASM adapter reports its walk, `knobas:adapter@1.3.0` (Opus implementer, 2026-10-20)

- **Where the function goes.** *Fork:* a function on the existing `sink` interface, or an
  interface of its own looked up as optional, as `downloads` and `query` were. *Ruling:* on `sink`,
  as the spec and the ticket name it. *Reasoning:* `downloads` and `query` are exports, which the
  host has to look up on the component; `walked` is an import the host provides. A 1.0.0 to 1.2.0
  component's `sink` import names only `item`, and wasmtime links it against the 1.3.0 instance,
  which provides more: `walk.rs` witnesses the 1.0.0 build installing and syncing.
  *Reversing:* move the function to its own interface and bump the minor again.
- **A reading the host cannot use.** *Ruling:* a call outside a sync, or after the sink refused
  an item, is dropped without an error. *Reasoning:* the function cannot fail (it returns nothing,
  as `Sink::walked` does), and after a refusal the run is over; reporting it would draw progress
  on a failed run. *Reversing:* one `if` in `sink::Host::walked`.
- **What the fixture counts.** *Fork:* its position in the whole corpus, or the items this run
  hands. *Ruling:* the items this run hands, from 0, so a sync from cursor `"3"` reads 0 to 2 of 2
  and one from `"5"` reads `0 of 0`. *Reasoning:* the bar shows this run's walk, as the mock's and
  Gitea's do. *Reversing:* one offset in the fixture's `sync`.
- **Where the reading is witnessed.** *Ruling:* the host's tests sync through
  `knobas_sync::progress::Observed`, the engine's real decorator, which makes `knobas-sync` a
  dev-dependency of `knobas-wasm-host`. *Reasoning:* the criterion is "arrives at the engine's
  progress sink"; a recording `Sink` alone would stop one hop short. No cycle: `knobas-sync` does
  not depend on the host. *Reversing:* drop the dev-dependency and assert on the recording sink.
- **The sync channel's capacity.** *Fork:* keep the pump's channel of one, or let readings queue
  beside the one item in flight. *Ruling:* one item plus 16 readings (`READINGS_IN_FLIGHT`); the
  item still waits on its answer, so a refused item still stops the sync where it stood.
  *Reasoning:* with a channel of one, each reading made the next item wait for the pump, and every
  wait hands the thread to whatever else runs on it. `knobas-app`'s
  `a_run_past_its_deadline_ends_failed_naming_it_and_its_neighbour_syncs` then failed 7 of 13
  runs on this branch (the healthy neighbour, sharing the thread with a spinning component, passed
  its 1 s deadline), where the base passed 5 of 5; with the readings queued it passed 6 of 6.
  *Reversing:* one constant.
- **Reserved steps.** None in this ticket; the contract sign-off is the parent's (#1379's ruling).
- **Merge-manager on Opus: sign-off on the WIT amendment.** *Fork:* treat the 1.3.0 minor as
  covered by #1379's sign-off, or rule it here. *Ruling:* signed off, here. *Reasoning:* the
  amendment is its own frozen-surface change (ADR-0028: a minor is a §10.8 entry), so it gets its
  own line. The deep pass found it additive and matching the diff: one function on `sink`, which
  an earlier component's narrower `sink` import does not name and still links against; the
  version gate moved by one minor and still refuses 1.4.0 and 2.0.0. Björn said on 2026-10-20
  that Opus may amend without him. *Reversing:* drop the function and the minor.
- **Merge-manager: the failure guard gets a witness.** *Fork:* leave "dropped after a refusal"
  unwitnessed, as the PR said no mutant could reach it, or add a test. *Ruling:* added
  `walk::a_reading_after_the_sink_refused_an_item_is_dropped` (the `swallow_sink` fixture into a
  sink that refuses the second item and records readings); removing the guard fails it.
  *Reasoning:* the amendment states the behaviour, so a test should hold it. *Reversing:* delete
  the test.
- **Merge-manager: the amendment names its witness.** *Ruling:* it now says the earlier-minor link
  is witnessed for 1.0.0 and inferred for 1.1.0 and 1.2.0, whose `sink` is the same as 1.0.0's.
  *Reasoning:* the entry claimed 1.0.0 to 1.2.0 without saying which one a test holds.
  *Reversing:* the sentence.

## #1381: Jira and Confluence report their walk (Sonnet implementer, Opus merge-manager, 2026-10-20)

- **Where the Confluence reading is pinned.** *Fork:* the ticket asks for a test "in the
  Confluence crate's integration binary", and the crate has none: it has never had a mock
  (ADR-0013), its API trait is crate-private, and `tests/live_confluence_seeded.rs` is its one
  test file. *Ruling:* two unit tests in `src/sync.rs` over the existing `Fake` (with and without
  `totalSize`, over 2-result pages, an idle run included), a wire-name test in `src/model.rs`, and
  a `--ignored` live test that `just atlassian-live` runs. *Reasoning:* a `tests/it` binary would
  need a stub HTTP server the crate has no dependency for, to re-test what the `Fake` stands in
  for. *Reversing:* low; the tests move when a binary exists.
- **What the numerator counts.** *Ruling:* issues (Jira) and pages (Confluence) the walk got
  through, delivered or skipped as already delivered, so the overlap window of an incremental run
  moves the bar and an idle run ends it at its own total. A reading comes before each unit and one
  after the last. Jira's `of` never reads below `done`, because the live `total` can shrink under a
  run. Confluence's `of` is the latest page's `totalSize`, and `None` when no page carried one. The
  mention walk, a second pass over a different query, reports nothing. *Reasoning:* the bar is
  for the main walk; a second `pages` count would reset it. *Reversing:* one line per adapter.
- **Merge-manager on Opus: both rulings confirmed.** *Reasoning:* the unit tests drive the real
  `SyncRun` over several result pages and pin 0..=N of N, `None` without a total, and the idle
  run; that is the criterion's intent. They cannot pin the server's meaning of `totalSize`, and the
  live test could not either, because the default `page_size` (50) put all seven seeded pages in
  one result page, where the whole count and this page's count agree, and the clamp to `done`
  would have hidden the difference by the last reading. *Fix:* the live test now walks 2-result
  pages and asserts the whole series 0..=N of N, so a per-page `totalSize` fails it on the first
  reading. *Reversing:* none needed.
- **Merge-manager: the positions sweep stays unreported.** *Fork:* an incremental run sweeps every
  page's position (#1138) before the reported walk, so an idle run on a large space shows no
  reading during that sweep. *Ruling:* left as is, backlog follow-up #1389. *Reasoning:* the
  ticket names one unit, the CQL result's pages, and its idle criterion is met. The sweep reads
  200 results a request with a light expand, about 30 requests for 6,000 pages. Giving it its own
  reading would mean a second `pages` count that resets the bar. *Reversing:* a reading in
  `positions_sweep`.

## #1383 — Uptime Kuma reports its walk

- **Which session the test fakes.** *Fork:* the ticket says "fake socket session", but `Source::sync` reads
  one `GET /metrics`; the socket session carries writes only. *Ruling:* the test runs against the
  existing wiremock `/metrics` fake in the Kuma crate's `it` binary. *Reasoning:* the ticket's
  wording misnames the read path; its intent (N is the monitor list the run read) is met, and
  there is no socket read to fake. No follow-up: nothing in code or docs is left to change once
  the ticket closes. *Reversing:* none, the reading sits in `sync`.
- **Idle run.** *Fork:* an unchanged document emits nothing; report the walk or stay silent.
  *Ruling:* it reports 0 to N `monitors`, then returns the cursor byte for byte. Tombstones are
  not counted. *Reasoning:* the ticket's second criterion asks for exactly this, and a tombstone is
  a monitor gone from the list, not one of its N. *Reversing:* gate the walk on `!unchanged`.
- **Merge-manager: one walk for both paths.** *Fork:* the idle path reported 0..N in a loop of its
  own. *Ruling:* one loop reports the walk and gates only the emission on an unchanged cursor; the
  test now also pins each reading arriving before its monitor. *Reasoning:* the walk is the same
  either way, and two loops could drift. *Reversing:* split the loop again.
- **Merge-manager: the copied `Walking` test sink.** *Ruling:* kept, as #1379 ruled; the refactor
  to one shared sink is #1391 (`backlog`). *Reversing:* none.
## #1389: Confluence's positions sweep reports its walk (Opus implementer, 2026-10-20)

- **How the sweep reads without resetting the bar.** *Fork:* the engine keeps only the latest
  `Sink::walked` reading and the wizard draws `walked`/`of`/`unit` as given (`Counting` in
  `crates/knobas-sync/src/progress.rs`, `FirstRun.svelte`), so any reading the sweep gives is
  replaced by the walk's first. A sweep counting its own `pages` to N, then the walk starting
  again at "0 of k pages", empties a full bar. A distinct unit ("page places") does the same and
  also ends an idle run on the window's small count. *Ruling:* one walk of `pages`. The sweep
  reports a reading before each row, over the sweep result's `totalSize`. The page walk counts on
  from the rows swept and adds them to its own total: "s + w of s + N". The count only moves
  forward and the unit stays the same. When the walk starts, the total grows by the window's size,
  so the bar dips by k/(s+k), which is small next to the sweep. *Reasoning:* this is the only
  shape that keeps one bar moving forward without touching `Sink`, the engine, the wizard or the
  §10.8 entry. Both passes read pages, so "pages" is still true, although a page in the window
  counts twice. An idle run now ends at "s + k of s + k pages" instead of "k of k". The mention
  walk and the re-read of moved pages still report nothing. This carries out the reversal the
  #1381 merge-manager named ("a reading in `positions_sweep`"). *Reversing:* drop the sweep's reading
  and the `swept_rows` offset in `SyncRun::run`; one function each.
## #1384: the source's settings page shows the walk during a scheduled run (Opus implementer, 2026-10-20)

- **Reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus: sign-off on the §10.8 entry.** *Ruling:*
  signed off. `docs/contract/10.8/1384-watch-sync-joins-the-run-in-flight.md` books one command,
  appended to the handler list, its TypeScript function in the existing `sources` barrel, and the
  fake's answer; nothing else frozen moves. *Reasoning:* the command is additive and the entry
  matches the diff. Björn said on 2026-10-20 that Opus may amend without him. *Reversing:* remove
  the command, its function and the entry.
- **Where the join lives.** *Fork:* call `Scheduler::trigger` with a sink (it joins a run in
  flight) or add a method that only joins. *Ruling:* `Scheduler::watch(source_id, sink) ->
  Option<i64>`, which takes the `runs` lock and calls `Watchers::attach`. *Reasoning:* `trigger`
  starts a run on an idle source, and the ticket says an idle source answers nothing; opening a
  settings page must not sync. `watch` leaves the first-sync claim alone, since watching is not
  asking about the first sync. *Reversing:* one method.
- **No detach command.** *Fork:* add `unwatch_sync` so a page that leaves takes its channel out of
  the run, or let the channel ride to the run's ending. *Ruling:* no command; the page aborts a
  signal it handed the port, which swaps the channel's `onmessage` for a no-op so the page that
  left is no longer reachable through Tauri's callback table, and the backend sink stays enrolled
  until the run ends. *Reasoning:* the enrolment is bounded by the run, `ChannelSink` already ignores a
  closed channel, and a second command is a second frozen surface for a few hundred bytes per
  message until the run ends. *Reversing:* one command plus a remove on `Watchers`.
- **Which statuses attach.** *Ruling:* the page attaches when its status says running, keyed on
  the status's run id, and skips a second attach while it is already watching or asking. A local
  *Sync now* marks the source running with no run id; if `watch_sync` lands before the trigger and
  answers `null`, the `sync:state` that follows (with the id) attaches. When the status goes idle
  the page drops the channel and the reading, whether or not the channel's ending arrived first.
  *Reasoning:* the two statuses of one run should attach once, and a lost ending should not leave
  a stale bar. *Reversing:* the effect in `TfSourcePage.svelte`.
- **The reading's form.** *Fork:* the wizard's `<phase> · … · 83.0 s` or the ticket's
  `120 of 300 repositories · 1,240 items · 83 s`. *Ruling:* the ticket's, with en-GB grouping as
  the page's run rows use and whole seconds (`runProgressWords` in `settings.ts`). *Reasoning:*
  the ticket quotes the line. *Reversing:* one function.
- **The Sync runs row fills in on the channel's ending too.** *Ruling:* the ending re-reads the
  runs, alongside the existing re-read on the terminal `sync:state`. *Reasoning:* the component
  test feeds the channel only, and the ending is the run's own word that it is over.
  *Reversing:* drop `ended` from the runs effect.
- **The fake IPC.** *Ruling:* `watch_sync` answers `null`; no fixture source runs, and the fake
  bridge sends nothing on a channel, so `just shot` cannot draw the page mid-run. The look is
  handed to the milestone review. *Reversing:* a running fixture source plus channel delivery in
  `fake-tauri.ts`.

### #1384: merge-manager on Opus, 2026-10-20

- **Reserved for Björn, the §10.8 sign-off: the implementer's ruling confirmed.** *Reasoning:* the
  deep pass found the entry true to the diff line by line: the signature, the append at the foot of
  the handler list, `Scheduler::watch` under the claims lock through `Watchers::attach`, `null` for
  an idle or unknown source, the first-sync claim untouched, `not_ready` as the only error, no
  generated type, the fake's `null`. *Reversing:* as the implementer's ruling.
- **No detach command: confirmed.** *Reasoning:* the enrolment ends with the run, and a second
  command would freeze a second surface for nothing a person sees. *Reversing:* as above.
- **A watch whose answer comes back after the status named a new run asks again.** *Fork:* leave
  the effect's skip ("already asking") as it was, or re-check the status when the answer lands.
  *Ruling:* re-check. A local *Sync now* marks the source running with no id and the page asks at
  once; if `watch_sync` reaches the scheduler before the trigger it answers `null`, and when the
  `sync:state` carrying the id arrives before that answer, the effect skipped it and nothing
  attached for the whole run. Now the page asks again when the status names a run the ask did not
  know, and only then, so a status lagging an ended run cannot loop. Witnessed by "a watch that
  finds nothing while the run's id arrives asks again for that run (#1384)", red before the fix.
  *Reversing:* the re-check in `watch()` in `TfSourcePage.svelte`.

## #1391 -- one walk-recording test sink

- **Fork:** the copies differ: most keep `items` as a `Vec`, three count them in a `usize`, the Kuma one also records how many readings had arrived at each item. *Ruling:* one `knobas_source::contract::Walking` with all three fields (`items`, `readings`, `readings_before_item`); the counting callers read `items.len()`. *Reasoning:* the superset costs nothing where unused and keeps every assertion as it was. *Reversing:* split the struct; one file plus the callers.
- **Fork:** `Handed` and `RefusesTheSecond` in `crates/knobas-wasm-host/tests/it/walk.rs` also implement `walked`. *Ruling:* left as they are. *Reasoning:* `Handed` records items and readings as one merged, formatted list (and the second wraps it with a refusal); that is a different record, not a copy. *Reversing:* none needed.
- **Fork (merge-manager, Opus):** the four live suites' own files changed (their inline sinks replaced) and none was run. *Ruling:* no live re-run. *Reasoning:* the sink only observes; the assertions on `readings` are untouched and the item counts became `items.len()` / `!items.is_empty()` of the same values, so nothing a suite witnesses changed, and no adapter, engine or `knobas-source` trait code changed. *Reversing:* run `just gitea-live` (and the JVM suites) on `main`.
- **Merge-manager confirms** both rulings above: the superset struct (only Kuma reads `readings_before_item`, and its test still witnesses the order) and leaving `Handed` / `RefusesTheSecond` alone.

## Grilling of 2026-10-21 (Björn + Claude, `/grill-with-docs` on #1403, #1416, #1427, #1464): what #881 left behind

Four journey-audit findings of 2026-10-20 share one root: #881 retired the rooms UI and left features
whose only surface was a room. Each is ruled restore, trim or retire below; the spec and ticket cuts
follow through to-spec and to-tickets. The glossary's **Context** and **Job** entries carry the
vocabulary half of #1427.

### #1403 — the credential expiry countdown: restore

- **Drawn again, on the source's page and on the Sources row.** *Fork:* draw `expiryNote`, or rule
  that the inbox's credential-expiry item replaces it and strike spec §3's countdown. *Ruling:* draw
  it. The source's page shows "expires in N days" on the Token or Password row of Connection (the
  row's label is the noun), plain over 14 days, amber under, red "expired"; the Sources list row shows
  "Credential expires in N days" in its state column only while amber or expired. *Reasoning:* the
  inbox item says something is wrong soon and opens this page, which today shows no date; the date
  comes from the source itself (`secret_expires_at`, never typed), the function and the fixture exist,
  so this is wiring. *Reversing:* delete two call sites.
- **The function drops the word PAT; spec §3 says credential.** *Reasoning:* #1405 already found a
  token source told to re-enter a password; the noun belongs to the row, not the function.
  *Reversing:* low.
- **The fixture's expiry date becomes relative to today.** The stored 2026-08-30 is past, so a
  screenshot would read "expired" and never show the countdown. *Reversing:* n/a.

### #1416 — the Tab chain: trimmed to two rows

- **The chain on an entity row is *Link to <job>* then *Start timer on <title>*.** *Fork:* restore
  everything spec §4 lists (Change status › Comment › Link to… › Add to context › Start timer › Start
  work › Open), trim, or leave Start timer alone. *Ruling:* trim. Change status, Comment, Start work
  and the "Do it here" rows (Start/Stop timer on the current ticket, Comment on it) are retired:
  the job page owns them and ⌘T owns the timer. *Add to context* dies with the Context ruling
  (nothing is added to a context by hand). No *Open* row: `chainFor` never drew one and Enter opens.
  Spec §4's three rows, the Launcher.svelte header and the roadmap's M2 line are rewritten to match.
  *Reasoning:* the launcher's job is finding; acting on a ticket is the job page's job; the one
  action about the *pair* (result + current job) has no other home. *Reversing:* the rows are still
  in `chainFor`'s shape; restoring one is a prop and a row.
- ***Link to <job>* opens the job's link dialog with the result preset as the other end**, closing
  the launcher; it does not write the link directly as the rooms shell did. *Reasoning:* one place
  picks relations; the launcher never writes a link the reader did not name. *Reversing:* low.
- **"The job" is the breadcrumb's job**: a job page or a view opened from one ('PAY-231 › Time'); no
  row on Tickets, Inbox or Settings. Not the newest open job. *Reasoning:* a guessed job writes links
  to the wrong ticket in silence. *Reversing:* low.

### #1427 — contexts: kept as the job's hidden working set, given a lifecycle; ad-hoc retired

- **The stored context stays.** *Fork:* keep it as the working set behind a job, or retire ticket
  contexts and route alerts, open jobs and proposals off the ticket and its links directly.
  *Ruling:* keep. *Reasoning:* ADR-0008's membership and #446's alert rule are built and
  load-bearing; what was missing was a lifecycle and honest glossary wording. The glossary's Job
  entry said a job "needs no stored context" while `job-reader.svelte.ts` promoted one on every
  open; the entry is corrected, not the code. *Reversing:* a backend rewrite of the Alert rule and
  ADR-0008's reach.
- **Archived follows the ticket's status, and only that.** `archived_at` is set exactly while the
  status is in the source's declared done-like set and cleared when it leaves, maintained by the
  sync run as the status lands. Opening the job never touches it. `promote` returns an archived
  context for a done ticket rather than making a second; a context first made for a done ticket is
  born archived; a one-time pass archives existing contexts whose ticket is already done. *Fork
  rejected:* reviving on reopen (nothing would ever re-archive a done ticket someone glanced at) and
  a manual *Put away* (a second place to forget). *Reasoning:* done in the source is the fact the
  inbox should follow; a reopened done job is reading, not working; leaving Done in the source is how
  reopening work already happens. *Reversing:* the sync hook and the promote branch.
- **Done-like is a `done_statuses` name list beside `blocked_statuses`**, matched the same way; Jira
  claims Done, Closed and Resolved; a workflow spelling it otherwise never archives, which is today's
  behaviour; a per-instance list is a setting the day one is asked for. One §10.8 entry (ADR-0007).
  *Fork rejected:* a declared path to Jira's status category. *Reasoning:* the shape the descriptor
  already has; absence is the safe miss. *Reversing:* add the path later as a second signal.
- **Ad-hoc contexts are retired.** *Fork:* *New ad-hoc job…* under *Not a ticket* and in ⌘K plus a
  job page with no ticket card, or retire. *Ruling:* retire: the *Not a ticket* group, R-3.11, the
  Job entry's ad-hoc sentence and the 2026-10-15 ruling "where an ad-hoc context goes" go; ad-hoc
  time is the ⌘T label timer; `create_context` stays an uncalled command under #881's ruling until a
  cleanup pass. *Reasoning:* a job is the working view of a ticket, and no `#/job/<ctx id>` route was
  ever built; an ad-hoc job would be a page whose every section is empty. *Reversing:* the command
  exists; the UI is new work.
- **The sixth built-in is renamed 'Open alerts on my jobs'**, description "Assets a job you have not
  finished holds, with a monitor in trouble"; the predicate (unarchived contexts) is unchanged and
  the fixture stops dropping the context clause. *Reasoning:* with the lifecycle above the list says
  something true about the reader's open work, and it shares the alert rule's predicate.
  *Reversing:* a string.
- **No ADR.** ADR-0008 carries the membership trade-off; this is lifecycle and wording, recorded
  here and in the glossary.

### #1464 — notes: a minimal read-only page while they are shown

- **`#/note/<id>` exists only while notes are shown.** *Fork:* a read-only page, the capture window
  reused as reader and editor, or retire (notes out of search even when shown, the switch governing
  the capture shortcut only). *Ruling:* the page: title, the body as pre-wrapped text with `[[refs]]`
  as links to the entity's address, the born links, and *Delete* behind a confirm; no edit, no
  Markdown dependency. *Reasoning:* D10 says hide, not break — a switch that puts notes back in search
  must lead to the note; retiring leaves capture producing notes nobody can read; the capture window
  as a second surface, and a dependency, are the wrong size for a page that lives one release.
  *Reversing:* delete the page; #1085's address stands.
- **Addresses.** While hidden the address redirects to Settings › Notes and capture as #1085 ruled;
  while shown, `itemHash`, the capture window's *Open in knobas* and the `capture:open-note` listener
  all go to the page. *Reversing:* `tf/address.ts`.
- **After *Delete*** the reader returns where they came from, else to Settings › Notes, with a toast
  "Deleted <title>" and no undo: the `deleted` activity line is final. *Reversing:* low.
- **A protocol note opens Time › Standup at its date**, recognised by the backend's own
  "Standup YYYY-MM-DD" title rule moved to one shared place; no stored marker. *Reasoning:* one rule
  already names protocols, and that tab is where they are drawn and edited. *Reversing:* low.
- **The switch's promise is reworded** in R-13a.6 and D10: "On, notes are back in search and open on
  their own page, and the capture shortcut works again". *Reversing:* a string.

## #1402: boot screen on the design system (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **No `.tf` wrapper.** *Fork:* wrap the boot screen in `.tf`, or reach `.tf-btn` without it.
  *Ruling:* without it. `.tf-btn` is unscoped in `css/chrome.css` and the tokens are on `:root`;
  the component sets what `.tf` would have given (paper, ink, the 2px `--focus` ring at offset 2).
  *Reasoning:* `App.test.svelte.ts` waits for `.tf` in the document to mean "the shell drew"; a
  boot screen carrying it would let those waits pass during boot. *Reversing:* add the class and an
  override of its grid; the App tests then need another marker.
- **All three sentences in `--ink-2`, the version line too.** *Fork:* the ticket allows "the fainter
  ink token" for the version line. *Ruling:* `--ink-2`. *Reasoning:* the design system has no text
  ink fainter than `--ink-2`; `--muted` is a state tone ("unknown, no data") and the spec forbids a
  lighter grey for text. *Reversing:* one declaration.
- **The failure message's mono and error ink are the component's own classes.** *Fork:* keep the
  bare `.mono`/`.fail` classes `unported.css` styles globally, or name the component's own.
  *Ruling:* `boot-mono` (JetBrains Mono at .9em, as `.tf-mono`) and `boot-fail` (`--err`), scoped.
  *Reasoning:* a bare name the unported sheet defines leaks its rule onto the element (the wall
  `tf.css`'s header describes), so the boot screen now reads nothing from that sheet, and the
  sheet's header stops naming it. The two scoped rules restate `.tf .tf-mono` and `.tf
  :focus-visible`, which is the price of not wrapping in `.tf`. *Reversing:* low.

## #1377 — where the Gitea token probe lives

Ruled 2026-10-21 (delegated by Björn at triage).

- **Pick (a): `./seed --env` probes the token on every call.** *Fork:* (a) `--env` probes, or (b) only
  the recipes that hand the token to a test probe, through a shared helper. *Ruling:* (a), reusing
  `gitea-token.sh`'s probe (now `gitea_token_status`, which `gitea_seed_token` also calls) through
  `gitea_token_require`. A non-200 answer, or none, exits `--env` non-zero before it prints a line,
  naming the token, the status and `./seed`. *Reasoning:* `responsiveness-probe`, `gitea-live` and
  every other consumer are covered in one place; the cost is one `GET /api/v1/user` per eval. It
  reverses no earlier ruling; it applies #552 ("the seed owes the red") without re-minting from a print.
  *Reversing:* low: delete the call in `print_env`, and add the helper to the two recipes.
- **`eval "$(./seed --env)"` swallows the exit status**, so the `responsiveness-probe` recipe and
  `live_session` now capture the output first (`seed_env=$(...) || exit 1`) and eval that. *Reversing:* low.
- **A Gitea that does not answer is refused too** (HTTP 000), as the ticket says "anything but 200".
- **Corrected reading of the `gitea-live` dead-token criterion (#1509, Sonnet implementer, 2026-10-21).**
  The criterion cannot pass as worded: `live_session` runs `./seed-gitea.sh` before `./seed --env`,
  which re-mints a refused token (seen on PR #1508), so `just gitea-live` with a dead recorded token
  passes. The `--env` probe guards only a token that dies between seed and eval. *Ruling:* the
  criterion is read that way; no code change, and the closed issue's body stays as it is.
  *Reversing:* none needed.

## #1400: the first-run wizard in tf.css, with TfAddSource (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **One PR for #1399, #1400 and #1401** (delegated). *Ruling:* one PR, as all three briefs
  recommend when all three are dispatched. *Reasoning:* the port rewrites the markup #1399's
  button and #1401's strings sit in, so the wizard is ported once. *Reversing:* none needed; the
  three `Closes` lines are separate.
- **Where the wizard draws.** *Fork:* mount it inside `TfShell` (a page under the top bar) or keep
  it taking the whole window as its own `.tf` root. *Ruling:* its own root, `.tf tf-fr-root` with a
  `tf-full` view inside, and no top or status bar. *Reasoning:* the ticket keeps the wizard's
  behaviour, and `App.test` holds that the wizard takes the window. The shell's `Esc` ladder is
  then not mounted, so the wizard closes the topmost dialog on `Esc` itself (rung 1 only), as the

- **Its rules** go in a new part, `lib/tf/css/first-run.css`, imported last in `tf.css`, every class
  `tf-fr-*`. *Reversing:* one file.
- **The rooms `AddSource` and its suite are deleted.** Nothing else mounted it, as the ticket says.

## #1407: the item page draws a custom role's source actions (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

Ruled 2026-10-21 (delegated by Björn at triage).

- **Dialog shape: lifted, not copied.** *Fork:* lift the pull request page's action dialog into a
  shared entity action dialog, or copy it under the item page. *Ruling:* lifted:
  `tf/pr/TfPrAction.svelte` is now `tf/TfEntityAction.svelte`, its `prId` prop `entityId`, and both
  pages open it. Its classes (`tf-pr-dialog`, `tf-pra`) went with it unchanged, so the pull request
  page's tests pass untouched. *Reasoning:* one dialog in ADR-0020's vocabulary, as #1194's ruling
  asks ("the view that offers one draws its dialog in ADR-0020's action vocabulary, as every
  action's is"); a copy would drift on the first fix. *Reversing:* low: move the file back.
- **Witness: both fixtures.** *Fork:* the WASM fixture and the dev fake each gain one source action,
  or the dev fake only. *Ruling:* both. The WASM fixture declares `source_actions: ["book_repair"]`,
  and the battery then requires `write_ops: ["source_action"]` and `Capability::Write` beside it
  (clauses 5 and 11), so it declares those too. A survey's view offers *Book repair…* with one
  required field, *Day*; `write` answers a receipt for `book_repair` on a survey and changes nothing,
  and refuses every other write with a protocol error. The dev fake's demo commit (`mock:9f2c1ab`,
  the route the ticket's screenshot names; the fake has no custom-role item) offers *Add note…*.
  *Reasoning:* the WASM fixture is what the custom role is tested with, so the host's battery now
  probes clause 11 on it, and `reads.rs` holds the view's action and the write it performs. All
  existing fields, no §10.8 entry. *Reversing:* low: empty the three descriptor fields and the view's
  `actions`.
- **Every action in the view is drawn, not only `source_action` ones.** *Fork:* filter the toolbar to
  `write_op === "source_action"`, as the pull request page does for its own list, or draw every
  action. *Ruling:* every action, in the view's order, through the shared dialog. *Reasoning:* the
  ticket says "draws them as the page's toolbar"; on a custom role's view every write is a source
  action anyway, and an op the shell cannot build gets the dialog's existing *Could not queue* toast.
  A disabled action is drawn `aria-disabled` with its reason as the title and opens nothing, as on
  the pull request page. *Reversing:* low: one filter.
- **Button words, dialog heading and toast.** The button is the label without its ellipsis
  (`actionName`), as the pull request page draws a source action; the dialog's heading is *<action>
  on <item title>*, and the toast *Queued: <action, lower case> on <item title>.* *Reversing:* low.
- **The write choke-point lint counts an external adapter's guest as implementing the trait**
  (merge-manager on Opus). *Fork:* the gate's `write_choke_point` scan flagged
  `knobas-wasm-fixture/src/lib.rs`, whose `write` now parses its op as a `WriteOp`. Parse it as
  untyped JSON so the file never names the op, or widen the lint. *Ruling:* widened:
  `implements_the_trait` also accepts `impl GuestAdapter for`, with a rule assertion beside the
  Jira one. *Reasoning:* the lint's category 3 is "anything that implements the trait": the host's
  `impl Source` forwards every write to the guest's `write` (ADR-0028), so the guest is
  `Source::write`, not a second path, and a WASM component cannot reach a source except through
  that host. Spelling the op as untyped JSON to slip past the scan would trade a compile-time
  check for a run-time one, which the lint's own file argues against. *Reversing:* low: drop
  the clause and parse a `serde_json::Value` in the fixture.

## #1408: the item page draws the shell's breadcrumb (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

Ruled 2026-10-21 (delegated by Björn at triage).

- **#1201's "no breadcrumb" is reversed in favour of R-1.6.** *Fork:* reverse #1201's implementer
  ruling ("No navigation entry, no breadcrumb … Reversing: low"), or keep it and argue R-1.6 does not
  cover a custom role's view. *Ruling:* reversed. *Reasoning:* R-1.6 is the maintainer's requirement
  and says *every* full view opened from a job; #1201 gave no reason the item page is exempt, and
  the proposals view's exemption rested on prototype-6 drawing it without one, which has no item
  page to point at. The rest of #1201's ruling stands: no navigation entry, and Esc's rung is
  unchanged.
- **The crumb's name is the kind's label.** *Fork:* the kind's label or the item's title. *Ruling:*
  the kind's label (`kind_info.label`, else the kind's id, as the header's sub-line already reads
  it); the title stays the page's `h1`. *Reasoning:* every other crumb names a view, not a record;
  a title would also say the same thing twice, one line apart.
- **One crumb, drawn by the item page.** *Fork:* widen `TfPage`'s crumbs guard to the item route, or
  let the item page draw the same crumb. *Ruling:* the crumb is now one component, `tf/TfCrumbs.svelte`,
  which `TfPage` draws for its full views and the item page draws itself; the item's page entry hands
  it `job`. *Reasoning:* the name is the kind's label, which only the item page's own read
  (`get_entity`) knows, so the frame cannot name it without a second read. *Reversing:* low.
- **Before the read answers, no crumb; a failed read names it *Item*.** *Reasoning:* drawing a
  placeholder name that flips to the kind's label a moment later is a flicker; a page that could not
  read its item still needs the *Back Esc* hint. *Reversing:* low.

## #1411: the launcher's selected row stays on screen (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **What an option's id is keyed on.** *Fork:* the row's id or its index in the flat list.
  *Ruling:* the index, `<$props.id()>-opt-<n>` for results and `-chain-<n>` for the Tab chain.
  *Reasoning:* the index is what `session.selected` already is, so the listbox names the option
  without a lookup, and a row id such as `confluence:ENG:SEPA design` contains a space, which is not
  valid in an element id. *Reversing:* one helper in `Launcher.svelte`.
- **A hover also scrolls.** *Fork:* scroll only on the arrow keys, or on every change of the
  selected row. *Ruling:* every change, as the ticket says. A hovered row is already on screen, so
  `block: "nearest"` leaves it in place; a row cut off at the edge moves just far enough to show in
  full. The ticket's "hover stays as it is" is about which row hover selects, and that is unchanged.
  *Reversing:* gate the effect on a keyboard flag.
- **When the listbox names nothing.** *Fork:* the ticket says the attribute is absent "with nothing
  selected", but the session always holds an index. *Ruling:* `aria-activedescendant` is absent when
  there is no current row, when a failed read draws its reason in place of rows, and while the
  current saved list is being renamed. *Reasoning:* in each of those states no option element exists
  for the index, and naming a missing id is worse than naming none. A list being renamed is drawn as
  a text field. *Reversing:* one `$derived` in `Launcher.svelte`.

## #1412: Rename focuses the name field (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Effect or action.** *Fork:* a bound input focused from an `$effect`, or a `use:` action.
  *Ruling:* a `use:takeFocus` action that calls `focus()` and `select()` on the input as it mounts,
  in place of `autofocus`. *Reasoning:* the ticket allows either. The input exists only while it is
  being renamed, so mounting it and starting the rename are the same moment, and an action needs no
  binding or effect. *Reversing:* swap the action for a bound input and an `$effect`.

  focus a clicked button, so `autofocus` never fires. Filed as #1511 and left unfixed here, as the
  ticket says.

  onto `TfDialog`, as `TfLinkTo` is. *Ruling:* keep the dialog's form, footer and layer
  registration, and draw the picker inside it; `TfLinkTo` is unchanged. *Reasoning:* the brief
  forbids changing `TfLinkTo`, and the form's submit, *Delete block* and the refusal line would
  all move for no change the reader sees. *Reversing:* low.

  *Undo* cancels a write that never happened, as recommended (the #835 pattern). The block leaves
  the day at once. The timer outlives the view, so leaving the Day tab keeps the delete; closing
  the window inside those seconds loses it, and the block is simply there next time, as #835's
  merge-manager ruling has it for proposals. A held delete the backend refuses brings the block
  back with the refusal as an error toast. *Reasoning:* re-creating through `create_block` would

  script. *Ruling:* measure: a canvas draws the label in the strip label's face (600 at `--t-2xs`,
  mono for a key, sans for a label), the strip's width comes from a `ResizeObserver` (window
  resizes where there is none), and `fitLabel` keeps the longest head that fits with "…", dropping
  a trailing space, or drops the label when not one character and the ellipsis fit. The nested
  `<svg>` that clipped a label (the #827 ruling's) is gone. *Reasoning:* a test can witness what
  script decides; jsdom draws no ellipsis. *Reversing:* one component.

  and target ("13:10 to 13:58, Standup and planning"). *Reasoning:* the brief says the title keeps
  the full label, and a shortened or dropped label leaves the title as the only place it is whole.

  08–18 reads whole" depends on the window's width: in the 1440 px shot the 48-minute block reads
  "Standup and p…". "A block widened to 20:00 by an evening timer does not shorten labels it did
  not shorten before" cannot hold for a label that just fits, because a wider window makes every
  block narrower. What holds is that every label is fitted to its block's current width and never
  cut without "…". *Reversing:* n/a.

  brief asked.
- **The held delete is its own few lines, not `review/decisions.svelte.ts`.** *Fork:* reuse the
  Proposed links view's module, or hold the delete in `TfDay`. *Ruling:* in `TfDay`, with its own

  entries; the Day needs one timer and a hidden id. *Reversing:* extract a shared hold if a third

## #1413: Save as list is offered only where the backend can save (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **`>` and `?` under the new sentence.** *Fork:* the ticket gives `NotASearch` the sentence
  *`t` is not a search.*, but `NotASearch` is also what `> palette` and `?` get from `saved::plan`,
  and they would then be told about a `t` they never typed. *Ruling:* `Refusal::NotASearch` carries
  the prefix it refused, and `Refusal::on_create` names it: *`t` is not a search.*, *`>` is not a
  search.*, *`?` is not a search.* (*That prefix is not a search.* for the others, listed without a
  wildcard so a new prefix is a compile error there). `Refusal::description()` ignores the field and its text is unchanged. *Reasoning:*
  the `t` sentence is the one the ticket specifies, and following it literally for `>` and `?` would
  repeat the bug the ticket fixes (a sentence that does not fit the case). The box never offers the
  control on `>` or `?`, so only a direct caller ever sees those two. *Reversing:* drop the field
  and use one sentence.
- **The other refusals' wording.** *Ruling:* the rail's reason is kept word for word and
  capitalised, ending with a full stop and without the delete sentence (*The launcher refuses the
  saved query: …*), as the ticket says. *Reasoning:* "keep their reason sentence". The box has
  already refused these queries on the keystroke, so the save path cannot reach them from the UI.
  *Reversing:* one match arm.
- **An answer to the previous query.** `canSave` needs *a* response, as the ticket says, not a
  response to the text now in the box. In the 90 ms after a keystroke the control can still show
  under the previous answer. A click in that window is refused by the backend with the new
  sentence, which no longer misleads. Not gated on `pending` (*reversing:* one more condition).
- **The IPC-seam test.** `creating_refuses_a_query_it_cannot_run_and_never_shadows_a_built_in`
  (knobas-app) asserted that `create`'s refusal carried *Needs attention*. That is the behaviour
  this ticket removes. The test now asserts that the refusal carries neither the heading nor
  "Delete it", and that every refusal is distinct.

## #1418: the launcher board previews the inbox and gives today's time (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Build or strike** (delegated). *Ruling:* build, as recommended. Both reads already exist in the
  shell.
- **Data path** (delegated). *Ruling:* shell props, as recommended. `App.svelte` hands the launcher
  `inbox` (the live inbox store's `count` and its stream's items) and `today` (the Day tab's figures,
  read on each opening). `LauncherHome` and `launcher_home` are unchanged: no §10.8 entry and no
  sign-off. *Reversing:* move both onto `LauncherHome` with a §10.8 entry.
- **Shape** (delegated). *Ruling:* the inbox count and the newest three items, and time as the Day
  view's *tracked* and *to log*, in `hm` form (`2h 10m tracked`, `1h 5m to log`), as recommended.
- **No second copy of the Day read.** *Ruling:* `TfDay.svelte`'s read (`day_blocks` plus
  `ad_hoc_block` per unlogged block) moves to `tf/time/day-read.ts` as `readDay`. The Day tab and
  the shell's `readTodayFigures` both call it, and the figures come from `day-view.ts`'s
  `dayRows`/`dayFigures`, running timer included, as on the Day tab. A failed read leaves the time
  block off the board rather than showing zeros.
- **Rows or pictures.** *Fork:* the criteria say *pressing* opens. The launcher is driven from the
  keyboard. *Ruling:* the inbox lines and the day are rows of the board's one flat list (`rows.ts`
  kinds `inbox` and `today`), after the smart lists and before the recent items, so `↑`/`↓` reach
  them and `Enter` opens them. Neither has a `Tab` chain. *Reasoning:* a launcher-board block the

  is the item's view, the source's settings for a credential expiry, or Monitors for an alert. A line

- **When a block is absent.** Inbox: when the count is 0. Time: when today's tracked minutes are 0
  (to-log time is part of tracked time, so it is 0 then as well).
- **Order.** Lists, inbox, today, the source strip, recent, which is spec §4's order with the strip
  left where it was.

## #1430 — how the top bar fits at 1100 px: CSS only, or a *More* menu

Ruled 2026-10-21 by the implementer (Sonnet), delegated by Björn at triage.

**The fork:** CSS only (drop the search field's minimum width, tighter item padding, hide the counts
below a breakpoint), or a *More* menu that collapses the nav's tail (a new component).

**Ruling:** CSS only, in `narrow.css`, for 901 to 1240 px. The search field loses its minimum width,
its "Search" word and its `⌘K` hint (the magnifier stays, ⌘K still works), nav items take 7 px side
padding, the nav's count badges hide, and the timer chip's target caps at 12ch (22ch everywhere else).

**Reasoning:** with a timer on a long label at 1100 px, the first three cuts alone still lost *Proposed
links* and *Time*; the tighter chip cap is what made it fit, so it is part of the band. Everything
stays reachable and no component is added. Hiding counts costs the Inbox and Monitors badges between
901 and 1240 px; the pages carry the same numbers. At 1440 px and above nothing changes.

**Cost of reversing:** replace the band with a *More* component; one stylesheet block and one test.

## #1423: on a Jira view the preview and the list read the ticket's status (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

Ruled 2026-10-21 (delegated by Björn at triage).

- **The shape is (a): `MiniBoardCard` gains `status`.** *Fork:* (a) the card carries its own
  status, or (b) `MiniBoardColumn` gains `name` with `status` null on a column of several statuses.
  *Ruling:* (a), the recommended pick. *Reasoning:* the card is what the preview, the list and the
  button read, and the #1200 ruling has the shell read only `MiniBoardCard`; (b) would still leave
  the shell to find each card's status by looking up the column it came from, which is the lookup
  that broke. A saved view's `MiniBoardColumn.status` stays the view column's name, as the header
  draws it, and its doc says so. *Reversing:* low: one additive field (§10.8 entry
  `1423-miniboardcard-carries-its-status.md`).
- **A column is done by what it lists, else by its cards.** *Fork:* the done cap by "every card on
  it is done", by the view's `statuses`, or by either. *Ruling:* where the view's column lists
  statuses (a Jira view's, or a view's own columns), the column is done when every listed status is;
  a column that lists none (the board's own, one per status) is done when it has cards and every
  card's status is. "Done" is still the status spelled *done* in any case (`isDone`); knobas syncs
  no status categories (#1208's *knobas does not sync status categories*). *Reasoning:* the list is
  what the column is; the cards on it at one moment are a sample, and a column named *Done* that
  gathers *In Review* must not drop to three because its review tickets are elsewhere. *Reversing:* low.
- **The list's Status sort follows the statuses as the board first meets them.** *Fork:* sort by the
  column a card stands in, or by its own status. *Ruling:* by its own status, in the order the board
  first draws each, column by column (`statusOrder`). *Reasoning:* the cell shows the card's status,
  so sorting by a column name the row no longer shows would read as unsorted. *Reversing:* low.
- **The view editor's list preview reads the card's status too.** *Fork:* leave the editor's preview
  as it was, or read the card there too. *Ruling:* the card. *Reasoning:* it sits on the Tickets page
  and read the same column name; the ticket says nothing on the page reads a column name as a
  status. *Reversing:* low.
- **The fixture needed no change.** `jira-board-21` already holds PAY-233 (To Do, Mara's) under
  *Ready* and five Done tickets under *Shipped*.
- **Björn's sign-off before merge: reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus.** The §10.8
  entry is one additive field on a read type, the pick Björn recommended at triage; signed off.

## #1476: two sources holding one ticket key are told apart (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

Ruled 2026-10-21 (delegated by Björn at triage). The ruling applies to #1455 (a space key two
sources hold) too.

- **Addressing: the entity-id job address, the bare key the fallback.** *Fork:* `#/job/<key>` with a
  disambiguated `#/job/<source>/<key>`, or jobs moved to the entity id. *Ruling:* keep `#/job/<key>`
  for a key one source holds; a key several sources hold opens at `#/job/<source>:<key>` (the entity
  id), which the shell conventions already read ("An address holding an entity id
  (`#/job/jira:PAY-231`) is read as one"). *Reasoning:* the recommended pick's intent with the
  spelling the route already has: `#/job/<source>/<key>` would collide with `#/job/<key>/<tab>`
  (`#/job/PAY-231/map`), so it would need a route grammar change; the colon form needs none, and no
  §10.8 entry. A bare key two sources hold opens the first listed source's ticket and the job card
  says *In <source> · also in <other>* with a link to the other's address, so it is never silent.
  *Reversing:* low: one address rule (`ticketAddress`, `entityAddress`'s `shared`).
- **When to draw the source: only when the key is not unique where it is drawn.** *Fork:* only then,
  or always. *Ruling:* only then, the recommended pick. The board and the list count the cards read
  (a capped read does not see a twin past its cap, so that card draws no source and opens by key,
  where the job card names the other); the launcher counts the rows of the answer or the recent
  items, per kind; the job card reads every listed source under the key. *Reversing:* low.
- **What names the source.** *Fork:* the display name or the monogram. *Ruling:* the board card,
  the list row and the job card draw its display name (the source list's, through
  `sourceRoles.nameOf`, and the detail's `source.display_name`). The launcher row names it by id,
  before the sync age (`jira · synced 25 min ago`), as its complaint line already does.
  *Reasoning:* the launcher's health rows carry no display name (§2.2), and a monogram of two
  letters tells `jira` from `jira-ops` no better than the id. *Reversing:* low.
- **An entity's one stable address stays its entity id.** `CONTEXT.md`'s *Entity* has exactly one
  stable in-app address; for a ticket that is `#/job/<source>:<key>`, which always opens it.
  `#/job/<key>` is the short form a person reads, kept where it names one ticket (R-1.2).
- **The fixture's second source is the Jira source it already lists.** *Ruling:* `Tidewater Jira`
  now holds PAY-231, PAY-228 and OPS-77 as the mock does. *Reasoning:* it already claims the ticket
  system; a sixth source would change every count the sources view draws.
- **Björn's sign-off before merge: reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus.** No IPC type,
  route grammar or §10.8 surface changes for this ticket; nothing to sign off beyond the rulings above.

## #1504: the note page and protocol addresses (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **The hidden redirect lives in the page, not in the address.** *Fork:* make `entityAddress`
  read the notes switch, or let every producer emit `#/note/<id>` and have the page send the
  reader on. *Ruling:* the page reads `capture_shortcut` first and replaces the address with
  `#/settings/notes` while notes hide. *Reasoning:* `entityAddress` stays pure and has one answer;
  an old bookmark, a link panel and the capture window land right in both states. A setting that
  cannot be read does not hide a note the reader asked for. *Reversing:* `tf/note/TfNote.svelte`.
- **The protocol rule runs in two places that share one function.** `standup/protocol.ts`
  `protocolDayOf` reads `Standup YYYY-MM-DD` (a date the calendar has, as a `NaiveDate` must be).
  `itemHash` uses it when a producer holds the title (a launcher hit, a recent row, a digest line,
  the note page's own refs and links); the note page uses it after its read for producers that
  hold only the id (*Open in knobas*, a link panel). Both replace, not push. *Reversing:* low.
- **What the page draws.** A resolved ref is a link reading its target's title; an unresolved one
  stays the text as written; a withdrawn target is named, struck, not linked. A link row reads
  "Captured in", "Related to" (`readingFor`) and its other end; a context end (`ctx`) is named, not
  linked, since #1427 ruled no page for a context; a withdrawn end likewise. A note `get_note`
  calls `not_found` reads the shell's *Nothing lives at …*. *Reversing:* low.
- **"Came from" is `history.length > 1`.** After *Delete*, the page goes back when the window has
  an address to go back to, else replaces with `#/settings/notes`. *Reasoning:* the shell keeps no
  history of its own; a forward entry can make the length overcount, and the miss lands on a page
  that exists. *Reversing:* low.
- **`#/time/standup/<date>` reads that day's digest as well as its protocol,** and the Time header
  names the day. A segment that is not a date is today's Standup. The tab is keyed by the date, so
  another date is a fresh mount. *Reversing:* low.
- **Delete is sent at once, not held.** *Fork:* the shell conventions' *Writes and undo* hold an
  irreversible write for the toast's 6.5 s with *Undo*; the ticket asks for a confirm and a toast
  with no undo. *Ruling:* the ticket's, recorded as a line under *Writes and undo*. *Reasoning:*
  #1464's ruling makes the `deleted` activity line final, and the confirm is the reader's chance
  to stop. *Reversing:* hold the call behind the toast as `TfDay`'s delete does.
- **Fixture.** `note:retry-backoff` is seeded so the page has a note under `?fake-notes-shown`,
  and `delete_note` is answered (it was out of the walk's reach while notes were hidden).
  *Reversing:* fixture only.
## #1500: the Tab chain is Link to the breadcrumb's job, then Start timer (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Where "the breadcrumb's job" comes from.** *Fork:* the launcher reads the address itself, or the
  shell says which job its breadcrumb names. *Ruling:* the shell. `TfShell.svelte` reports it to a
  window singleton beside `currentJob` (`tf/job/current.svelte.ts`, `breadcrumbJob`): the job page's
  job, or the last job on a view or an item page opened from it, with the entity id `navJobId`
  resolved. *Reasoning:* only the shell knows the last job opened and its entity id; the launcher
  stays a component that is handed its second end. *Reversing:* one `$effect` and a prop.
- **Inbox and Settings.** Both start their breadcrumb at the last job ('PAY-231 › Inbox'). The
  ticket and the 2026-10-21 ruling on #1416 name them as job-less, so they offer the timer row
  alone. Not a fork; recorded because the breadcrumb alone would say otherwise.
- **From a view opened from the job.** *Fork:* draw the job's link dialog over the view (Time,
  Dependencies), or open the job page and its dialog there. *Ruling:* open the job page. The
  launcher asks through `linkRequest`, `App.svelte` moves to `#/job/<key>` when that job is not on
  screen, and the job page takes the request once its ticket has drawn. *Reasoning:* the dialog is
  the job page's, and the Connections drawer there shows the link the moment it is made; one
  mechanism serves both cases; Back returns to the view. *Reversing:* mount `TfLinkTo` in the
  shell's dialogs for a view, and keep the request for the job page.
- **A request nobody took.** The shell drops it the moment the reader lands on any page but a job
  page (found in review): otherwise a reader who left before the job drew would get the dialog
  unasked on their next visit. *Reversing:* one `$effect`.
- **The Connections drawer opens under the dialog.** *Ruling:* yes, so confirming leaves the reader
  looking at the new link, as *Link to…* from the drawer does. *Reversing:* drop `drawer = true`.
- **The launcher's props.** `openEntity` and `onlink` keep their names, re-documented as the
  breadcrumb's job; `onlink` gains the result's kind, since the dialog draws the preset's kind.
  *Reversing:* a rename.
- **The fake.** `create_link` under `?fake-ipc` refused any end outside the corpus, so a `list:`
  result (an estate asset) could not be linked and the screenshot route ended in an error. The
  fixture now resolves an estate asset as a link end, in `create_link` and in the drawer's rows.
  Fixture-only; the real graph already holds assets as entities.
- **Where the shell-level test lives.** It mounts `App.svelte` over the whole fake bridge, and
  `house-rules.test.ts` lets only `lib/shell/dev/` import the harness, so the file is
  `lib/shell/dev/launcher-chain.test.svelte.ts`.

## #1525: the shell remembers the address a job was opened at (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Fork:** what the shell remembers of the last job. *Ruling:* `{ key, segment }`, as the ticket
  suggested: `key` is what the chip, the Job tab and *Back to* name; `segment` is the address it was
  opened at (`PAY-231`, or `tide:PAY-231` when two sources hold the key, #1476). The chip, the Job
  tab and `Esc` link `jobHash(segment)`; `navJobId` resolves the segment, so an id reads as itself.
  *Reasoning:* the key alone cannot tell two sources' PAY-231 apart; the segment can, and a bare key
  still reads as it did. *Reversing:* low, one field.
- **Fork:** how pages get the segment. *Ruling:* a second context field `jobAt` beside `job`, which
  stays the key; the six components that draw the chip (TfCrumbs, Settings, Docs, Builds, Pr, Repo,
  and Item through TfCrumbs) take an optional `jobAt` that falls back to the key. *Fork rejected:*
  turning `job` into the object everywhere, which reaches about a dozen pages and their tests and every logic
  read of the key (branch names, *This job*, monitors), and collides with the launcher bundle
  (#1500) running beside this. *Reversing:* fold `jobAt` into `job` later; mechanical.
- **Fork:** the Job tab while only the timer names the job. *Ruling:* it links the timer's ticket by
  its entity id, not its bare key, so a timer on the second source's PAY-231 opens that one. The
  address reads `#/job/jira%3APAY-231` even for a key only one source holds. *Reversing:* one
  `$derived`.
- **Fork:** a stale `navJobId` across two jobs with one key. *Ruling:* when the segment changes the
  id is cleared before the read, so *Add to* and ⌘T never answer with the other source's ticket
  while the new one is read. *Reversing:* one line.
- **Left as it was:** Builds' and Docs' *This job* scope and Docs' *Link to <job>* still resolve the
  key under every source (they take `job`, the key). Filed as #1537.

## #1438: one toast for every queued write, naming a failing sign-in (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **The tail: #860's wording wins over #841's (delegated by Björn at triage, recommended pick).**
  *Fork:* keep "Sends with the next sync" (#841's PR toasts, the shell conventions' *Writes and
  undo* line) or drop it (#860–#862's Docs ruling). *Ruling:* dropped everywhere. A write toast
  reads "Queued: <what>." with *Show queue*, plus "<Source> sign-in is failing, so it waits
  there." (R-15.1) when the source's credential is rejected or missing. This **reverses #841's
  toast line** and the conventions line, which now says the same. *Reasoning:* `submit_write`
  queues and flushes the source at once (`knobas-sync` `write_queue::submit` → `flush_source`, which
  reads no `enabled`), so the write is out in a second; the audit saw a move reach Jira with sync
  paused. The only case where a write waits is the one the toast now names. *Reversing:* the
  `queuedText` line in `shell/queued-toast.ts`.
- **Pausing does not hold writes, and the pause toast says so (delegated, recommended pick).**
  *Fork:* build a hold on pause in the backend, or say what is true. *Ruling:* no backend hold;
  the source page's switch toasts "Paused. Nothing syncs until you turn it on; writes you make
  still go." The recommended wording was "writes still go"; *you make* is added because a write
  that was already waiting when the source was turned off does hold (CONTEXT.md *Held write*,
  migration 0012: its target leaves the view, and the scheduler never retries a disabled source),
  so the bare phrase would overclaim. *Reversing:* the string in `TfSourcePage.svelte`, or a hold
  in `flush_source` and the old words back.
- **Credential health comes from the shell's live store, not the page's own read.** *Fork:* each
  page passes its own "sign-in fails" flag (Builds had `stale?.fix != null`), or the helper reads
  `shell/health.svelte`'s `health`. *Ruling:* the store, keyed by the write's source id. *Reasoning:*
  it is the store the status bar draws, it is live on `source:health`, and one reading means the
  toast never disagrees with the bar. *Reversing:* a `failing` argument on `toastQueued`.
- **"Sign-in is failing" means `unauthorized` or `missing_secret`.** *Fork:* those two, or every
  actionable state (`isActionable`, which adds `unreachable`). *Ruling:* the two, as one total
  table `signInFails` beside `isActionable` in `shell/health.svelte.ts`, which Builds' `staleLine`
  and the job's stale builds line now read too. *Reasoning:* an unreachable server is retried on
  its own and an untested (`unknown`) credential is not failing. *Reversing:* low.
- **The caller names the source.** *Fork:* a module store of source names, or each caller passes
  `{ id, display_name }` (the shape of `SourceRef`). *Ruling:* the caller, because no store holds
  source names: the job, PR, item and repository pages pass their detail's `source`
  (the repository page hands it down to Branches, Compare, New branch and the commit dialog);
  Builds its pipeline's `source_id`/`source_name`; Docs its page's; *Create monitor* the target
  the reader picked (`TfCreateMonitor`'s `oncreated` now carries it); Monitors its `sourceNames`;
  the inbox reads `list_sources` after the re-run is queued. A worklog carries no source, so its
  toast names none. *Reversing:* low.
- **Every write toast routes through the helper, not only the ticket's list.** *Fork:* the
  ticket's named callers only, or every write toast. *Ruling:* every one: Docs' three and
  Monitors' *Pause*/*Resume*/*Create monitor* ("<label> queued for <name>" before) and the
  worklog too, so "Queued: <what>." with *Show queue* holds on every page. The inbox reads
  "Queued: re-run Payout_IntegrationTests #1187.", the row's title rather than prototype-6's
  "#1187". The old `AssetsView` (the asset tree, kept unchanged) keeps its own monitor toast.
  *Reversing:* low.
- **`queuedRunText` became `queuedRunWhat`.** *Fork:* keep Builds' own text function with the
  tail, or reduce it to the *what*. *Ruling:* the *what*; Builds' run toast keeps its words ("Queued: run
  <pipeline>. <summary>.") and its tail now comes from the helper. *Reversing:* low.

## #1441: what a queued merge or state change holds back on the PR page (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **A source-blocked Merge… is `aria-disabled` yet still opens its dialog.** *Fork:* the ticket
  asks Merge… to honour the source's `disabled` as `aria-disabled`, and every other held button on
  the page opens nothing; but #843 has the blocked dialog name each reason the source gives, which
  the tooltip carries only as one sentence. *Ruling:* `aria-disabled` and the source's title, primary
  styling kept, and a press opens the dialog, whose *Merge* stays disabled. Held by a queued write,
  Merge… loses primary styling and a press opens nothing, as the ticket says. *Reasoning:* the
  criterion asks for the attribute only, and the reasons box is the one place the source's reasons
  are listed. An `aria-disabled` control stays focusable so it can explain itself, and here the
  explanation is the dialog. *Reversing:* one guard in the button's `onclick`.
- **A queued close or reopen holds the state-change button whatever it reads.** *Fork:* the ticket
  says "the opposite state change"; before the sync the source still offers *Close* after a queued
  close, so a second close could be queued. *Ruling:* `close queued` or `reopen queued` holds *Merge…*
  and the *Close*/*Reopen* button, both before the sync (the same change again) and after it (the
  opposite one). *Edit* and *Update branch* stay live then. *Reasoning:* a duplicate close is the same
  refused-write case as a duplicate merge. *Reversing:* drop the state chips from `close`/`reopen` in
  `TfPr.svelte`'s `HOLDS`. A landed close keeps *Reopen* held until the session ends, because nothing
  drops the page's chips once the source's read shows them; #1542 has that.
- **A source's own actions (#1194) are never held.** *Fork:* the ticket names Close/Reopen, Edit and
  Update branch only. *Ruling:* a source action stays as the source draws it. *Reasoning:* the shell
  never reads their op (ADR-0029), so it cannot know which a merge makes stale. *Reversing:* look up
  a source action's key (`source:<id>`) by its prefix in `heldBy`.
- **A queued hold names itself before the source's reason.** When both apply, the title is the chip
  (`merge queued`), since it is the newer fact. *Reversing:* swap the `??` order.

## #1440: a branch or commit row opens its repository page (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **How a branch or commit finds its repository** (delegated by Björn at triage). *Fork:* (a) parse
  the id in the shell, (b) keep `#/branch/<id>` and `#/commit/<id>` and give them a page that reads
  the entity's declared parent and redirects, (c) widen `itemHash` to take the row's parent.
  *Ruling:* (b). `tf/code-row/` reads `get_entity`, then the repositories of the entity's own
  source (`list_entities`, as the pull request page reads its header's), takes the one whose title
  is the row's `path` (`repoOfRow` in `tf/repo/repo.ts`, ADR-0018), and replaces the address with
  the Branches tab (`repoHash(…, "branches")`, R-8.1) or the commit's page (`commitHash`, R-8.7).
  *Reasoning:* no caller changes, no id parsing (ADR-0020), and the window-address callers, which
  hold only kind and id, land right too. It costs one round trip and a frame of empty page.
  *Reversing:* low, `itemHash` and the two heads in `route.ts`.
- **Whether `#/branch/<id>` and `#/commit/<id>` stay valid addresses** (delegated). *Ruling:* they
  stay, so #816's ruling on the address stands as it was written; what changes is what they draw.
  *Reversing:* low.
- **What a miss draws.** A branch or commit with no declared parent (ADR-0007), or one naming a
  repository the mirror does not hold in that source, draws *<title> is not under a repository in
  the mirror.* with *Go to Code*, under the Code breadcrumb. An id the mirror does not hold reads
  the shell's *Nothing lives at …*, as the note page does. *Reversing:* low.
- **The two heads are the foreground.** *Ruling:* `branch` and `commit` join `ENTITY_HEADS`, so the
  entity is in front while its page reads or names the miss; the redirect then puts the repository
  in front. *Reasoning:* `foreground.ts` admits a head once a page draws it, and the miss page names
  that entity. *Reversing:* low.
- **Fixture.** The fake's branch `feat/PAY-231-idempotent-retry` and commit `mock:9f2c1ab` gain the
  parent path Gitea declares (`tidewater/payout-service`), so `?fake-ipc` witnesses the redirect.
  *Reversing:* fixture only.
## #1442: the Open in component remembers the root it just saved (Sonnet implementer, 2026-10-21)

**The fork:** keep the saved root in `TfOpenIn`, or make every parent re-read the checkout.

**Ruling:** `TfOpenIn` keeps the root *Set and clone* saved (`savedRoot`) and uses it in `clone()`, in the dialog's done handler (so the stop toast names the root) and in the Clone tooltip. The `checkout` prop's `clones_root` is the fallback. No `clones_root` IPC read.

- **The box row.** The bar left of the input stays as the only loading sign, in `--ink`, dimmed to
  `--rule` while a query is in flight (amber is the timer's, and the design system keeps yellow for
  the card). The footnote, ⌘K and the × stay; the × is the pointer's way out beside the dim.
- **Rows.** Kind monogram (Archivo 11 px in a hairline frame), the kind word, the title with the key
  and the path, and the provenance as the source column, 12 px `--ink-2`, as prototype-6's `.kind`
  and `.src`. The monogram is drawn inline rather than through `shell/Monogram.svelte`, which still
  draws the asset tree's with `unported.css`'s `.mg`. The state chip is the shell's `.tf-chip` in the
  adapter's tone. The excerpt's hit is `--mark` behind ink, not amber text.
- **Mono.** Only the key and the path of a result row, as the ticket's criterion says. The `?`
  card's tokens, the miss's raw link, the *Nothing matches* echo and `--demo` are Archivo (bold
  where they stood out before). *Reversing:* one selector each.
- **Palette labels.** The `>` palette's label column is 240 px, not 160: *Settings › Checkouts and
  Open in…* (#1417) wrapped at 160. The #1414 layout test reads the new width.
- **Specificity.** `.tf button, .tf input { font: inherit; color: inherit }` beats a single class,
  so every launcher rule on a button or an input names `.tf` as well.
- **`TfDialog` and `Tab`.** The trap now leaves a `Tab` whose default a field already prevented:
  the box takes `Tab` (and Shift+Tab) for the action chain, and the trap would otherwise move focus
  from the box to the dialog's last control on Shift+Tab. Every other dialog is unchanged (none
  prevents `Tab`).
- **No focus ring on the box.** The design system draws a 2 px `--focus` ring on whatever has focus;
  the ticket asks for prototype-6's input with no rectangular focus box. *Ruling:* the ticket's,
  for this one field: it holds focus for as long as the launcher is open (rows are walked with the
  arrows, never focused), and the ink bar beside it and the text caret mark it. Every other control
  in the launcher keeps the ring. *Reversing:* drop one rule.
- **What the shell's dialog adds.** On `TfDialog` the launcher registers on the shell's layer

## #1451: the run Overview's *Create ticket* stays deferred (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Build R-9.11's *Create ticket* (LOW) now, or keep #853's deferral.** *Ruling:* keep the
  deferral, the recommended pick; #1451 stays open under `backlog`. Reverses no earlier ruling: it

  The other two still hold. The ticket asks for the run and the ticket to be linked, and the
  shell has no such link: `create_action_item_ticket` and `action_item_ticket` bind the new
  ticket to a note, and the raw `CreateTicket` op links nothing. A link from a run means a new
  command and a relation from the run entity (or a migration), which is a frozen-surface touch:
  a §10.8 entry and Björn's sign-off. Leaving the link out (the run address only in the body)
  would fail the ticket's own criterion that the run page draws the linked ticket. A LOW item
