  run-to-ticket link) for whoever picks it up from `backlog`.

### #1451, 2026-10-22: built after all (Opus implementer)

- **Build R-9.11's *Create ticket* now, or keep the deferral.** *Ruling:* build it. This reverses
  #853's "*Create ticket* (LOW) is not drawn" and the ruling above (#1548, 2026-10-21). Two things
  changed. First, Björn asked the loop on 2026-10-22 to work through the backlog, and this is its
  oldest item, so "higher-priority work is waiting" no longer holds. Second, #1548 overestimated
  the link's cost. It assumed a new command and a relation, or a migration. In fact
  `submit_write`'s `link_to` (#984), with the intent held on the queued row (#1050), already
  draws a link on arrival for a new branch, pull request or page. Extending it to a `CreateTicket`
  takes one `delivery()` arm and one look-up arm. There is no new command, migration, relation or
  DTO. The sign-off it needs is ruled below. *Reversing:* moderate; drop `TfRunTicket` from the
  problem block and the `CreateTicket` arms. The shared dialog can stay.
- **Reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus: sign-off on the frozen-surface touch.**
  *Ruling:* signed off, as `docs/contract/10.8/1451-create-ticket-links-on-arrival.md` records it:
  `WriteOp::CreateTicket`'s `delivery()` gains `link: Some(ArrivalLink::Related)`, and
  `submit_write` accepts a `CreateTicket` with `link_to`. It widens an existing argument and adds
  nothing to the wire, and every op that took `link_to` before keeps its behaviour, pinned by
  the existing `link_on_arrival_ipc.rs` cases. *Reversing:* low; two match arms and the entry.
- **How the filed ticket is found** (the run-to-ticket link's shape, delegated). *Ruling:* a
  confirmed `related` link from the ticket to the run. The ticket is the newest live ticket in the
  write's source with exactly the filed title, among tickets the source last changed no earlier
  than five minutes before the write was queued. *Reasoning:* Jira's create receipt names no key,
  so the title is the address, as it is for Standup's action item. The time bound keeps out the
  likeliest wrong match: the same failing test filed from an earlier run under the same title. The
  five minutes allow for skew between this machine's clock and the source's. *Cost:* a
  same-titled ticket edited inside that window could be taken. Closing that gap would need the Jira
  adapter to put the key in its receipt, which its own comment rules out. *Reversing:* low; one
  query.
- **Which project the ticket goes in** (delegated). *Ruling:* a picker over `list_projects`, empty
  until chosen. No pipeline has a configured project to default to. *Reversing:* low.
- **Generalise Standup's dialog or write a second one** (delegated). *Ruling:* generalise it, the
  recommended pick: `tf/TfCreateTicket.svelte` is the shell's one create-ticket dialog. Standup
  uses it with the action item's words as the note. The run page uses it with title and body
  fields (`words`). Standup's behaviour and tests are unchanged. *Reversing:* low.
- **What the problem block draws once a ticket exists.** *Ruling:* each ticket linked to the run is
  drawn in place of *Create ticket* (`Ticket <KEY>`, opening its job, the title as its tip). While
  a ticket filed here is queued, *Ticket queued* is drawn instead. Neither offers a second
  *Create ticket*, as Standup's action item does not (#1433). While the mark is drawn, the page
  reads the run's links again whenever any source's sync ends, because it is the ticket's source,
  not the pipeline's, that brings the ticket in. *Reversing:* low.
- **The prefill.** *Ruling:* the title is `<first failed test> fails in <pipeline> #<number>`. The
  body is the failure heading, the details as the source wrote them, `At <path>:<line>` where the
  details give one, and `<pipeline> #<number> on <branch>: <the run's URL at the source>`, so the
  ticket can be read without knobas. The type is `Task`, as Standup's. *Reversing:* low; one pure
  function (`ticketDraftOf`).

### #1451, 2026-10-22: review (Opus merge-manager, PR #1750)

- **Finding the filed ticket by its title, while Jira's create answers its key.** *Ruling:*
  accepted for this PR. The title match is the wrong long-term design, and #1754
  (`ready-for-agent`) replaces it. The implementer's premise is half right. Jira's REST v2
  `POST /rest/api/2/issue` does answer `{id, key, self}`, and `knobas-source-jira`'s
  `write::create_ticket` reads `key` and refuses a create without one. The adapter's
  `CreateTicket` arm then drops it (`WriteReceipt::none()`, on #280's reasoning). So it is the
  receipt that names no key, not Jira. A comment in the adapter does not rule out putting the key
  in the receipt, and `docs::created_page` (#1121) already resolves an arrival from
  `write_queue.remote_id`. *Reasoning for merging anyway:* (1) Standup's action item
  (`standup.rs` `ticket_titled`) has matched by title, unbounded, since #779. This PR's match is
  bounded, so it adds no new kind of risk. (2) The prefilled title carries the run number
  (`… fails in <pipeline> #<n>`), so an earlier run's ticket does not share it. The realistic
  collision is the same run filed twice, or a reader-edited generic title. Either way the link goes
  to a sibling ticket, never to another run's. The implementer's "same failing test filed from an
  earlier run" is therefore not the likeliest case; the bound guards the edited title. (3) Fixing it
  properly spans two adapters: Gitea's receipt is an issue number, not its entity's local part
  `owner/repo/issues/<n>`. It also changes Standup's path. That is a ticket's scope, with its own
  §10.8 entry and `just jira-live`, not a merge-manager fix. *Cost of reversing:* low; #1754
  replaces one query in each place.
- **`CreateTicket`'s delivery class (ADR-0012).** *Ruling:* unchanged and correct. The arm
  sets only `link: Some(ArrivalLink::Related)` over `conservative`. `resend_harmless` stays `false`
  and `can_leave_unclaimed` stays `true`, and only `knobas-app`'s `arrival_linkable` and
  `link_on_arrival` read `link`. A create is still not resend-harmless. *Cost of reversing:* n/a.
- **Reserved for Björn (the frozen-surface sign-off), ruled by implementer on Opus: reviewed.**
  *Ruling:* upheld. The §10.8 entry matches the diff (the `delivery()` arm, the `link_on_arrival`
  arm, the refusal's wording, the `entity.ts` doc), and nothing on the wire changes. *Cost of
  reversing:* low.
- **The new ticket-first convention.** *Ruling:* kept as a real convention, since it says where
  any future create-ticket site goes. Reworded so that Standup, which files through
  `create_action_item_ticket` and not `link_to`, is not left non-conforming. *Cost of
  reversing:* trivial.

## #1424: what the job and Docs draw of a queued write, and how it goes (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Delegated by Björn at triage, ruled by implementer on Opus: the section echo.** *Fork:* the queued
  text in place of the old, or under the heading beside it. *Ruling:* in place of the old, muted, with
  a dashed rule and *queued* by the heading. *Reasoning:* the triage's recommendation; two texts in one
  section ask the reader which one holds. *Reversing:* draw `TfDocBlocks` above `.tf-sec-queued` in
  `TfDocBody.svelte`.
- **Delegated by Björn at triage, ruled by implementer on Opus: *Edit section* while a save is queued.**
  *Ruling:* it starts from the queued text. *Reasoning:* the triage's recommendation; the live pass's
  second save started from the old text and lost the first edit's words. A second save still carries
  the version the page was read at, so once the first lands the source refuses it as stale; that
  refusal now drops the echo and offers *Edit and resend*. *Reversing:* one `??` in `TfDocBody`'s `open`.
- **One shared module, not a shape copied per surface.** *Ruling:* `tf/queued.svelte.ts`, keyed by
  entity and write id, used by the job, Docs and the pull request page; the repository page keeps
  `repo/queued.svelte.ts`, whose marks read a listing and a blob, not a write id. *Reasoning:* the
  drop-on-read rule and the held-or-refused path are the same on every surface. *Reversing:* medium.
- **The follow lives in the module, not on the page.** *Fork:* the inbox stops its follows on unmount.
  *Ruling:* a mark's follow outlives its page, so a write held after the reader moved on still drops
  its echo and toasts. *Edit and resend* asks the module (`askAgain`), navigates to the page, and the
  page takes the request when it draws (`takeAgain`). *Reversing:* stop the follows on unmount.
- **A move's mark goes once the mirrored status moved from where the move found it**, not only when it
  equals the picked status, as the ticket's criterion says ("until the detail's status moves"). A mark
  dropped stays dropped, so a ticket moved back by somebody else does not draw the old move again. The
  same holds for a section edit (the page's version) and the pull request's state (#1542).
- ***Edit and resend* on a held move focuses the Status select on the job's Work tab.** *Fork:* a
  select has no typed text to put back; selecting the refused status without queuing it would draw a
  status that is neither mirrored nor queued. *Ruling:* focus the select, showing the mirrored status.
  *Reversing:* set the select's value in `TfJobCard`'s take effect.
- **The toast names the write as the queue toast does:** *Move of PAY-231 to In Review*, *Comment on
  PAY-231*, *Edit of “Context” on SEPA payout retry design*, *Comment on <page>*, *Page <title>*,
  followed by `toastStopped`'s *was held* / *was refused* and the queue's detail.
- **A comment's mark goes when a read holds its words**, compared with runs of white space collapsed
  (`sameWords`): Jira and Confluence hand back the text with their own line breaks. A Docs comment's
  words are its blocks' (`blockWords`).
- **A queued page is keyed by its parent page and drawn at the end of the parent's fold**, which it
  opens; it goes once a tree read holds a page of that title under that parent.
- **Not built: a re-read on sync.** The job, Docs and the pull request page read once per opening, as
  before; a mark goes on the next read after the sync. A write withdrawn in the queue panel leaves the
  open rows the way a sent one does, so its mark stays until the session ends. *Reversing:* a
  `sync:state` listener per page, or a `withdrawn` state on the follow.

## #1542: the pull request page's queued chips go once the view reads them (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **A *merge*, *close* or *reopen* chip goes once the view's *State* moved from what it read when the
  write was queued** (`merged`, `closed`, `open` from `knobas-source-gitea`'s `view/pr.rs`), and the
  holds it drives go with it. *edit*, *update*, *review* and a source action's chip have no state to
  read and keep the session lifetime, as the ticket says. *Reversing:* `STATE_READ` in `TfPr.svelte`.
- **The chips are followed too.** *Fork:* the ticket asks only for drop-on-read. *Ruling:* a chip whose
  write is held or refused goes, with its holds, and a toast says why; its dialogs are not reopened, so
  it offers no *Edit and resend*. The pull request's comment does: the box gets its words back.
  *Reasoning:* a refused merge otherwise holds every toolbar button for the session, the same defect.
  *Reversing:* drop `following` from `marked` in `TfPr.svelte`.
- **The dialogs' `onqueued` passes the queued write** (`TfEntityAction`, `TfPrMerge`, `TfPrReview`),
  so a chip carries its write id. `TfItem`'s use of `TfEntityAction` ignores the argument.

## #1454: *Export as Markdown* never replaces a file in Downloads (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

Ruled 2026-10-21 (delegated by Björn at triage).

- **Where the export lands: bare `~/Downloads`, a taken name numbered ` (1)`, ` (2)`.** *Fork:*
  bare `~/Downloads` with the downloads module's numbering, or a knobas-owned
  `~/Downloads/knobas-docs` folder as the notes export has. *Ruling:* bare `~/Downloads`, the
  recommended pick. *Reasoning:* it is what ruling #854–#856 already says for every download ("a
  taken name gets ` (1)`, ` (2)`"), the toast's *Saved <name> to ~/Downloads* stays true, and a
  page exported for someone else lands where a browser download would. No earlier ruling reversed.
  *Reversing:* low: pass `folder.join("knobas-docs")` in the command.
- **One free-name rule for both writers.** *Fork:* make `numbered` visible to the docs module and
  loop there, or lift the downloads sink's create-new loop into `downloads::create_free` and call
  it from both. *Ruling:* the shared function. *Reasoning:* the name is claimed with `create_new`,
  so a file that appears between the check and the write is still never opened, and the rule
  (`name`, then ` (1)` to ` (999)`) is spelled once; `numbered` and its test are unchanged. A write
  that fails after the name was claimed removes the empty file, as a failed download does.
  *Reversing:* low.

## #1455: a docs space two sources hold is addressed with its source (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

Ruled 2026-10-21 (delegated by Björn at triage), following #1476's ruling above, which named #1455.

- **Addressing: the address grows a source, in the entity-id spelling.** *Fork:* the breadcrumb
  picks the space in place and the address stays, or the address names the source. *Ruling:* the
  address, as `#/docs/space/<source>:<key>` where another source holds the key, and
  `#/docs/space/<key>` otherwise. *Reasoning:* #1476 ruled the same class for a ticket key and said
  its ruling applies here; one rule for both (the source before the first `:`, written only where
  the key is not unique) keeps a second addressing shape out of the app. The in-place pick would
  have left the address itself still opening the other source's space when copied or reopened.
  Requirements §10's header and its opening paragraph name the new address. *Reversing:* low: the
  breadcrumb's `spaceHash` and the split in `placeOf`.
- **Encoding the source.** *Sub-fork:* how `source_id` sits in the segment. *Ruling:* `<source>:<key>`
  in the one segment, `encodeURIComponent`d (`wiki%3AENG`), split at the first `:`. A source id
  holds no `:` (an entity id is split at its first one), so the split is exact. A segment whose
  prefix names no space with that key is read again as a bare key, so a key that holds a `:`
  still opens by its bare address. *Reversing:* low: one split, one fallback `find`.
- **A bare key two sources hold.** *Sub-fork:* open the first or refuse. *Ruling:* open the first
  listed source's space, as before and as #1476 does for a job. The breadcrumb never hands out that
  address for a shared key, so it is reached only by hand or an old bookmark. *Reversing:* low: one
  `find` in `pageToOpen`.
- **No route grammar or §10.8 change.** The route keeps `space` and the segment after it whole;
  `#/docs/space/<source>/<key>` would have needed a third segment. `foreground` reads a docs space
  as nothing, with or without the source.
## #1457: the asset editor's *Needed by* reads `depends_on_this` (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Shape** (delegated). *Ruling:* the recommended pick. The direct `depends-on` links stay as chips,
  and beneath them a read-only block draws the answer as the Tree's *Depends on this* panel does:
  the assets nearest first under *Depends on this* with their count, then *Reachable via routes
  that would break*, listed and not counted. Each asset row names the edge it came through
  (*inside* for containment). *Reasoning:* it is the glossary's own arrangement, and a reader sees
  the whole answer without opening anything. *Reversing:* low, one block in one component.
- **When it reads** (delegated). *Ruling:* on every editor open, as its own read beside `get_asset`.
  If it fails, *Needed by* says *What breaks could not be read: …* and the rest of the editor
  still works. *Reasoning:* the recommended pick; requirements §0 leaves performance for later.
  *Reversing:* low.
- **"The direct chips stay editable".** The editor has never had a control that edits a *Needed by*
  chip. A `depends-on` link is added from the other asset's *Depends on*, and nothing in the editor
  removes one. *Ruling:* the chips stay as they are, the part a link edit changes, and get no new
  control. *Reasoning:* the ticket rules editing out of scope and asks for the direct part to be
  kept, not for an unlink control. *Reversing:* low.
- **Routes landing on the asset** used to be chips taken from `reachable_via`. *Ruling:* they now
  come only from `depends_on_this.routes`, in the read-only block, so no route is drawn twice.
- **The VM's screenshot criterion.** `DependsOnThis.routes` holds only the routes whose target is
  the asset itself (`CONTEXT.md`, *Depends on this*). No route targets the OrbStack VM, so its
  editor shows its 14 assets and no routes. *Ruling:* follow the glossary. The knobas-mockd shot
  shows the routes, and #1553 holds the conflict (routes landing on anything in the closure).
  Reverses no earlier ruling.

## #1448: a run's test summary is declared, and a version bump backfills it (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

**The fork:** declare the test counts on the run kind, which reverses the #961/#947 "not declared" ruling, or strike the test summary from R-9.6 and ADR-0022.

**Ruling:** declare them. This reverses #961/#947 (its §10.8 entry now carries an amendment saying so). ADR-0022 is in force and lists the summary among a run's declared fields; R-9.6 and prototype-6 both draw it; #848 deferred it only because of fixture cost. `KindPaths` gains `tests_failed`, `tests_passed` and `tests_ignored`, and `RunRow` gains one `tests: Option<TestSummary>`. The name `RunTests` already belongs to `run_tests`' answer (#855).

**Further picks inside the ruling:**

- *Backfill, not migration.* TeamCity's cursor goes to version 2. A stored version-1 position reads as unknown, so the next run is a full sync, and the engine does not sweep it because it holds a position. A migration could only have cleared the position, which makes the run a sweeping first sync, or rewritten the same version number in SQL on a single-writer surface. A build older than `builds_per_config` keeps no counts until a later read answers it.
- *mockd serves what the seeded server serves.* That is `failed: 1, passed: 0, ignored: 0` on 1187 and nothing on any other build (deviation 19), because the seeded step reports one test. ADR-0013 and the crate header freeze mockd ("not a deviation"), but the ticket asks for mockd's dataset to carry the counts, and without a known `testOccurrences` key `BUILD_FIELDS` is an `UnknownField` 400 on every mockd test. Deviation 18 (#1004, merge-manager ruling) is the precedent. The fixture log's `41 passed` is story text that neither server counts. The fake IPC carries prototype-6's 41/42.
- *Row copy.* Prototype-6's `tests-mini`: *N failed, M passed* with the failed part in err tone, and the failed part left out at zero (*42 passed*). *, K ignored* shows above zero, as the ticket asks.
- *`rest::TestCounts` stays as it is.* The mirrored counts are read through declared paths on the raw payload, as `agent` is, and nothing would read a wider `TestCounts`. The Tests tab keeps reading its failed count from the build view.
- *Battery.* An absent count is evidence only beside another count that reads. Asked for by name, TeamCity serves all three counts, zeros included, and no `testOccurrences` on a build that ran no tests (measured on teamcity.jetbrains.com 2026.2.1).

**Reasoning:** each pick matches what the real server serves and what the frozen shapes already do (`current_step`'s excuse, the cursor's own "bump when the meaning changes" rule).

**Cost of reversing:** medium. Striking the summary means removing three `KindPaths` fields, one `RunRow` field and a table cell, with a §10.8 entry. Leaving the cursor at version 2 costs nothing.

### Reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus: sign-off before merge (#1448)

**The step:** the ticket's last criterion asks for "Björn's sign-off before merge" on the frozen-surface change.

**Ruling:** signed off, on this evidence: the §10.8 entry matches the diff (three `KindPaths` fields, one `RunRow` field, the cursor version, mockd deviation 19, and no migration, command or module); the adapter, battery, app and component tests are green. On the PR's live runs, `just teamcity-live` passed 12 of 12. In `just teamcity-live-seeded`, 1187 read 1/0/0 and the battery passed on the seeded server; its 5 failures come from the fixture break filed as #1560 (stray configurations on the seeded server) and touch nothing this PR changed. Confirmed by the merge-manager on Opus (below).

## #1447, #1448: merge review of #1558 (Opus merge-manager, 2026-10-21)

### Reserved for Björn, ruled by merge-manager on Opus: sign-off before merge (#1448), confirmed

**The step:** the implementer ruled the sign-off and left it to the merge-manager to confirm.

**Ruling:** confirmed. The deep pass found the frozen surface as the §10.8 entry describes it, with one gap now closed (next ruling). A stored version-1 TeamCity position parses as unknown, so the adapter is handed `Some(cursor)` and still runs a full sync over each configuration's window; `knobas-sync` sweeps only a cursor-less, non-backfill run (`CursorSource::may_sweep` plus the cursor-less check in `run_locked`), so the upgrade run tombstones nothing. The battery's excuse is per record and only where none of the three counts reads, the same shape as `current_step`'s. `RunRow` and `KindPaths` are regenerated, not hand-edited. The seeded live run's five failures are all exact-set or configuration-limit failures from #1560; the two tests this PR changes passed there.

**Cost of reversing:** low before release; the cursor bump is the only part that cannot be taken back without another bump.

### The §10.8 entry names `generated/sources.ts`

**The fork:** the entry listed `KindPaths`' three fields but not that they reach the IPC through `SourceDescriptor.payload_paths`, which the regenerated `app/src/lib/ipc/generated/sources.ts` shows.

**Ruling:** one sentence added to `docs/contract/10.8/1448-run-test-summary.md`, so the entry matches the diff.

**Cost of reversing:** none.

### #961/#947's "not declared" reversal stands

**Ruling:** upheld. The ticket delegated exactly this fork and recommended declaring; ADR-0022 lists the test summary among a run's declared fields, and #848 deferred it on fixture cost only. The #961/#947 entry carries the amendment.

### mockd deviation 19 stands

**Ruling:** upheld against ADR-0013's freeze. Without a `testOccurrences` key mockd answers `BUILD_FIELDS` with an `UnknownField` 400 and every mockd test breaks; it serves only what the seeded server serves (1187 `1/0/0`, nothing elsewhere), which the seeded live run printed. Deviation 18 (#1004) is the same case.

**Cost of reversing:** low, but only together with dropping the field from `BUILD_FIELDS`.

### The backfill reaches the window, not every mirrored build

**The fork:** the ticket asks for counts on "every build the mirror holds"; the version bump re-reads each configuration's `builds_per_config` window.

**Ruling:** accepted. A mirrored build older than the window draws no summary until a later read answers it, and `older_pipeline_runs`, which reads the source live, has the counts. Re-reading every mirrored build by id would cost a request per old build on every TeamCity source at upgrade, for rows that new builds push out of view.

**Cost of reversing:** medium: a one-off by-id walk over the mirror's builds.

### *, inherited* after a fixed list's kind word: kept, follow-up #1564

**The fork:** an inherited select reads *one of staging, prod-dryrun, inherited*, which looks like a third value.

**Ruling:** kept for this PR, because the ticket says *inherited* "stays drawn as it is today"; #1564 (`backlog`) carries the wording, since no fixture has an inherited select.

## #1472: the Kuma adapter logs in only once Kuma listens for the login (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Where the cause lies: in knobas** (Björn delegated this call at triage, 2026-10-21). Kuma 2.5.3's
  `io.on("connection")` awaits `sendInfo` (two `Settings.get` reads) before it registers `login`, and
  socket.io drops an event nothing listens for, with no ack. The adapter POSTed the login straight
  after the namespace `40`. With Kuma's settings cache warm the race is never lost; each cached
  setting expires 60 to 120 s after it was read, and then it is. The live suite runs right after
  `seed-kuma.sh`, whose own login warms the cache; the app's first pause after minutes of quiet hits it
  cold. Evidence: Kuma's log for the audit's two pauses (2026-10-20 20:55:15 and 21:07:59) shows `New
  polling connection` from the host and no `Login by username` line. Replayed on 2026-10-21 against the
  pinned container: the two POSTs sent 2 to 7 ms apart with curl lost the login on 5 of 5 cold attempts
  (each 130 s after the last settings read) and kept it on the one warm attempt; the adapter itself, built on the old order,
  failed 2 of 5 cold pauses of the canary with the audit's exact message, and on the new order acked 4
  of 4 (117 to 360 ms).
- **The fix waits for `loginRequired` (or `autoLogin`) before the login.** *Fork:* wait for `info`,
  wait for `loginRequired`, or resend a login that goes unanswered. *Ruling:* `loginRequired`/`autoLogin`.
  *Reasoning:* Kuma emits it at the end of the connection handler, after every handler is registered;
  `info` is emitted before the registrations and is safe
  only by Node's event-loop ordering; a resend guesses at a timeout and doubles logins against the
  twenty-a-minute limit. A Kuma that stopped sending it trips the existing `CALL_BUDGET` deadline with
  the protocol message, which is the right reading. `CALL_BUDGET` is unchanged. *Reversing:* low, one
  read before the login.
- **The session fake registers its handlers late for every session test**, not for one test alone,
  answering the namespace's `40{…}` on the first read and `info`/`loginRequired` on the second.
  *Reasoning:* that is how the real Kuma always behaves; a fake that answers a login nobody could have
  heard is a claim about Kuma the container contradicts. On the old code every session test runs out
  its budget. *Reversing:* low.
## #1560: Live fixture: seeded TeamCity holds ~94 Witness_Alpha configurations (Sonnet implementer, 2026-10-21)

  fix runs once per bring-up, and a hand deletion leaves the next stray to break the suite again.

  the guard first, since the licence limit bites them before any baseline. *Reversing:* low.

  build the seed did not make, so more than one page of leftovers no longer fails every test.
  *Reversing:* low.

  deauthorises every authorised agent but `knobas-agent`. Two containers from the `issue-690`

  suite certifies one agent; a stray container is outside the repo, so the seed makes it

## #1475: a pasted address opens its item in any form its source declares (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **The pick.** *Ruling:* the descriptor slot, the ticket's recommendation and spec #491's own next
  step. Not the Confluence-only alias column: an alias the Confluence crate stores reaches the
  resolver only through the SPI's `SyncItem` (an SPI change anyway) or through a payload key core
  would have to know by name, which is the per-adapter table §3a forbids. Not copy only: the soak
  missed on forms the source serves. *Reversing:* medium (the slot is additive and `serde(default)`).
- **The slot's shape.** *Ruling:* `UrlForm { kind, template, fields: Vec<PayloadPath> }`, `template`
  relative to the source's base URL with `{}` (one value, form-decoded) and `{*}` (the rest, as
  written). Not regular expressions: a template has no syntax to fail at run time, crosses the WIT
  JSON as plain data, and cannot be written to backtrack. Values are compared on the item's payload
  at declared paths, the way `payload_paths` already declares where a source keeps a fact.
  *Reversing:* medium.
- **Where the base is decided.** *Ruling:* in SQL, `web_url_normalized!` on the configured
  `source_config.base_url` and on the pasted prefix, so `knobas_core::web_url`'s rule keeps its one
  implementation; Rust only splits the string. A reading names its adapter kind, so two instances of
  one adapter answer under their own hosts. *Reversing:* low.
- **The tiny link.** *Ruling:* matched against `_links.tinyui` as Confluence stored it, not decoded
  from the page id: the encoding is Confluence's, and a link knobas composed would be a guess (P5).
  The live run confirms a seeded record carries it and the server serves the page there.
- **Order.** *Ruling:* the stored address wins over a form, then entity id. *Reasoning:* an address
  one item reports as its own is stronger than one that reads as another's form. *Reversing:* low.
- **The WIT.** *Ruling:* no change to `adapter.wit` and no minor version: the descriptor crosses as
  serde JSON, so the field is additive on both sides of an old host or an old component.
  *Reversing:* low (a 1.4.0 that only documents the key).
- **The commit-hint reads** in `sources/crud.rs` share `RESOLVE_URL` and bind no readings: their
  behaviour is unchanged. *Reversing:* low.
- **The live run's TeamCity.** The JVM lock was free but TeamCity was up (21 h, no holder), and the
  guard refuses a second JVM product. The narrow run held the lock, put TeamCity down, ran, and put
  it back up as found.

### Reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus

## #1475, #1480: merge review of #1568 (Opus merge-manager, 2026-10-21)

### Reserved for Björn, ruled by merge-manager on Opus: the §10.8 sign-off (#1475), confirmed

**The step:** the implementer signed the sign-off for `docs/contract/10.8/1475-url-forms-in-the-source-descriptor.md` and left it to the merge-manager to confirm.

**Ruling:** confirmed. The deep pass found the frozen surface as the entry describes it: `SourceDescriptor` gains one `#[serde(default)]` field and its type, every other adapter's descriptor adds `url_forms: Vec::new()` and nothing else, `adapter.wit` is unchanged at `knobas:adapter@1.3.0` (the descriptor is `func() -> json`, and `SourceDescriptor` has no `deny_unknown_fields`), and `RESOLVE_URL` stays one statement: its first arm is unchanged, the second is joined to the reading's own adapter kind and base, and `order by via_form, entity_id` keeps it deterministic with the stored address first. `docs/contract.md` changes only by its index line, and #1448's entry and amendment are intact. Two gaps are closed in the next two rulings.

**Cost of reversing:** medium; a follow-up removing the field, and a Confluence paste in another form misses again.

### The serde default for an external adapter's descriptor is witnessed

**The fork:** the entry and the PR claimed that a component sending no `url_forms` decodes as one declaring none, and no test removed the key. The WASM fixture serialises the current `SourceDescriptor`, so it always sends the key.

**Ruling:** `url_forms_round_trip_and_a_descriptor_without_them_still_decodes` in `knobas-source` removes the key from the wire and decodes it. With `#[serde(default)]` dropped, the test fails. The entry names it among its witnesses.

**Cost of reversing:** none.

### The §10.8 entry spells the order key `via_form`

**The fork:** the entry said `order by form, entity_id`, but the review renamed the column to `via_form`.

**Ruling:** the entry now reads `order by via_form, entity_id` and lists `a_reading_with_no_values_names_nothing` among its witnesses, so it matches the diff.

**Cost of reversing:** none.

### No install-time check of an external adapter's `url_forms`

**The fork:** `knobas-wasm-host`'s `check_descriptor` does not run `url_forms::check`. Only the contract battery does, and an external adapter's author may never run it.

**Ruling:** no check is added here. A form that `check` refuses gives no reading (`UrlForm::read` calls the same rules), a form that names a kind the adapter does not emit matches no item, and a reading is joined only to its own adapter kind's sources. So a malformed external declaration can only miss. It cannot name another adapter's item, and it cannot make install fail. Refusing it at install would turn a harmless miss into a broken adapter.

**Cost of reversing:** low; one call in `check_descriptor` and a `Refusal` variant.

### The narrow Confluence live run is not re-run on the merge head

**The fork:** the dispatch asked for one re-run of `a_pasted_address_opens_its_page_in_every_form_confluence_serves` on the merge head, because the resolver's `$2` is now built differently from how it was built on `1a9f44cb`, where the live run passed. The run queued on the JVM lock and took it after 128 s, once #1560's seeded TeamCity run released it. `live_guard` then refused, because TeamCity was still up with no holder. The dispatch rules out touching TeamCity.

**Ruling:** merge on the live run from `1a9f44cb`. Since that head, the path the test drives changed in two ways. `$2` is now built from a `FormReading` struct with `#[serde(flatten)]` in place of `json!`, and the JSON keys are the same. The SQL column alias is now `via_form`. The gated `url_resolve` tests drive both through `Registry::for_process()`, which holds the real Confluence descriptor, and through the real statement on Postgres. The Confluence descriptor and the live test changed only by `cargo fmt`. So what only the live run can witness has not changed since it passed: a real record holds `id`, `space.key`, `title` and `_links.tinyui`, and the server serves each form.

**Cost of reversing:** low. Once TeamCity is down, run the narrow test on `main`: `live_session confluence` and then the one `cargo test --exact`.

## #1450: Builds pages re-read when their source's sync finishes (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **An *as of HH:MM* line on a run in flight** (delegated). *Ruling:* no. The #853 ruling stands:
  the warn line (`staleLine`) is the run's last-seen, and the page now re-reads when its source's
  sync finishes, so the callout is as current as the mirror. The `sync:state` payload also replaces
  the page's sync status for that source, so the warn line moves with it. *Reasoning:* a second
  clock beside the warn line says the same thing twice. *Reversing:* low, one line in the callout.
- **Polling a run in flight between syncs** (delegated). *Ruling:* no; the pages re-read when the sync ends and at
  no other time. *Reasoning:* polling is a read budget no ruling has granted, and the sync interval
  is the source's own cadence. *Reversing:* low, an interval beside the listener.
- **What "the open tab" re-reads.** *Ruling:* the run page bumps a `rereads` counter the Log, Tests,
  Artifacts tabs and the Overview's chain panel take. Each reads again over what it draws: the
  log's folds, the tests' filter and opened rows, the artifact folders opened stay. A tab's failed
  re-read keeps its last answer. A failed runs re-read on either page keeps the runs and draws the
  page's existing *Runs could not be read* line above them. *Reasoning:* the ticket asks that a
  re-read keep the reader's place; remounting a tab would drop it. *Reversing:* low.
- **The fake's sync-state path.** *Ruling:* no fake change. The component tests fire `sync:state`
  through the pages' new `listen` port, and `fake-tauri`'s bridge already has `emit(event, payload)`
  for any test that drives the fake. *Reversing:* none needed.

## #1449: a run queued on the run page shows on its pipeline (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Store or pending writes** (delegated; (b) recommended). *Ruling:* (a) in the form the dispatch
  named: the shared `tf/queued.svelte.ts` marks (#1424), kind `run`, keyed by pipeline id, written
  by both pages' `queue()`, not a second store. The mark's text is the branch (`""` for the
  default), its base the newest run the page held as the run was queued (the pipeline's own `recent` runs
  before the page's read arrives). A read holds a queued run
  once it carries a run newer than that base, on its branch (any branch for one queued on the
  default), that no change or schedule started; each such run settles one mark, the oldest first
  (`runLanded`). The queue holding or refusing the write drops the mark and toasts, through the
  module's `followWrite`. *Reasoning:* (b) loses the row the moment the write is sent, before the
  mirror holds the build, so it needs a sent-write store anyway, which is (a). The shared module
  already has the follow and the drop-on-read, and the dispatch asked for it where it fits.
  *Known gap:* a write withdrawn in the queue panel leaves its row until a read holds a newer run,
  because `pending_writes` cannot tell withdrawn from sent. Two runs queued before either lands
  settle together once the first is read back. *Reversing:* medium. The marks become a
  derivation over `pendingWrites()` plus a sent-write list.
- **Amends #853.** #853 said a run started from the run page "is drawn *queued* on the pipeline
  page's next read" and that "the page draws no queued row of its own". The first half's premise
  was wrong: the next read is a mirror read and cannot show the run until a sync lands it. The
  pipeline page now draws it from the mark at once. The second half stands: the run page draws no
  queued row.
- **The pipeline page's own queued rows.** *Ruling:* they move to the same marks, so they now
  survive leaving the pipeline and coming back, and they go when a read holds the run, where before
  any re-open dropped them. *Reasoning:* R-9.7 says "appears … as queued at once, never as
  started"; dropping it on a revisit before the mirror holds it was the same gap. *Reversing:* low.

## #1477: a deleted newest TeamCity build, and the stale *Unreachable* (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **On a 404 of the watermark build, the refusal stays, reworded, and names *Backfill*** (Björn
  delegated this call at triage, 2026-10-21). *Fork:* (a) keep #91's refusal, reword it and name
  Backfill as the way out, or (b) fall back to the newest build the run witnessed, or the next-lower
  id, and carry on. *Ruling:* (a). #91 is not reversed. *Reasoning:* when a person deletes the newest
  build, the server's answers are the same as a replaced server's (the watermark answers 404, and no
  build the run saw reaches it), so nothing the adapter can ask tells the two cases apart. A
  fallback would sync on blindly in both cases, and for a replaced server that is the quiet,
  wrong-builds case #91 kept the refusal for. Backfill already gets out of it: it hands the adapter
  no position (`run_backfill`), so the check does not run, and it stores the newest build that
  survived. That is the "reset the cursor" #91 named, and the app has no other control for it. The
  refusal is now one sentence for a reader plus the evidence: *"build N, the last one this source
  synced, is no longer on the server, so syncing stopped; if it was deleted, Backfill on this
  source's page starts over from the newest build. Evidence: `/app/rest/builds/id:N` answers 404
  and no build this run saw reaches it, which is also what a source pointed at a different server
  sees."* The line under *Fetch everything again* now says Backfill forgets where the last sync
  stopped and is for a sync that names it. The contract's #91 amendment ("the same refusal, with the
  message re-worded onto that evidence") still holds, so no amendment. The glossary's *Backfill*
  gains the second purpose. *Reversing:* medium. (b) would be a change to `refuse_a_replaced_server`
  and would reverse #91 by name.
- **A run that ends in `Error` clears a stored `unreachable`, to `unknown`** (Björn delegated this
  call at triage, 2026-10-21). *Fork:* leave `auth_state` alone on `Error` (until now), clear only a
  stale `unreachable`, or write a verdict (`ok`) on every error. *Ruling:* clear a stored
  `unreachable` to `unknown` (detail dropped, `source:health` fired), and touch no other state.
  *Reasoning:* `unreachable` is a claim about the far end, made by an earlier run or by *Test
  connection*. An error run did not witness it again, and as long as the error repeats the sources
  view drew *Unreachable* over the run's own *Failed …*. `unknown` and not `ok`: a protocol error
  does not vouch for the credential (some servers answer a bad token with a login page), and
  `unknown` is already "not tested since something changed". `ok` and `unauthorized` stay: an
  error says nothing about them. Every `Error` counts, not only one where the server answered: the
  health step sees only the outcome, and an error the server never saw (a keychain read, a shutdown
  cancel) is still the run's own outcome, which is what the row should read. The next unreachable
  run sets `unreachable` again. *Reversing:* low, one arm in `apply_health_and_backoff` and
  `config::clear_unreachable`.
- **Test connection still maps `Protocol` to `unreachable`** (`knobas-app` `sources/crud.rs`). That
  is where a stale `unreachable` most often starts, and this ticket left it alone: it is outside
  the delegated picks, and the clear above stops it from outliving the next error run. *Reversing:*
  not applicable.
- **Merge-manager on Opus: every `Error` clears a stored `unreachable`, not only an error the server
  answered** (deep pass, 2026-10-21). *Fork:* keep the implementer's wider clear, or narrow it to
  the errors where the far end answered (`Protocol`, `Moved`) and leave `unreachable` standing
  through a keychain, configuration or database error. *Ruling:* keep it wide. *Reasoning:* the
  ticket asks for the narrow case and the wide rule contains it. An error the server never saw
  leaves the stored `unreachable` no truer: it was not re-witnessed either way, and `unknown` is
  the glossary's "not tested since something changed". On the source page, a stale *Unreachable*
  would sit over a keychain failure that needs a person, which is the worse reading. Nothing
  gates on `unreachable` (the scheduler skips only `unauthorized` and `missing_secret`; backoff
  reads the run log, not the health), so the clear changes no schedule, and the next unreachable
  run sets it again. The write is one guarded `update`, so a *Test connection* landing at the same
  moment loses or wins whole. *Reversing:* low; narrowing needs the `RunFailure` kind on
  `RunResult`, a sync-crate change with no IPC.
- **The launcher strip no longer shows a stale red for an erroring source** (merge-manager, deep
  pass). The strip reads only credential health, so a source whose runs keep ending in `Error` is
  unmarked there, as an error-only source always was. *Ruling:* not this ticket's; filed #1581
  (`backlog`). *Reasoning:* the red it loses was the stale state the ticket removes, and the source
  page reads the run's own *Failed …*. *Reversing:* not applicable.

  witness's own `testenv/desktop-witness/ax.swift`. The four new subcommands (`press-visible`,
  `focus-visible`, `click-at`, `window-id`) go into that file beside the witness's. The
  witness's `press`/`focus` are unchanged, because its drivers count on exactly one match in the
  tree. *Reasoning:* the ticket's recommendation. A mode of the witness would inherit its signed
  bundle and Launch Services steps, which a screenshot does not need. *Reversing:* medium; the
  steps would move into a driver.
- **AeroSpace.** *Ruling:* optional, off by default. `LIVE_SHOT_AEROSPACE=1` fullscreens the
  window by its CG window id, which AeroSpace uses as its own, and is refused when `aerospace`
  is not on PATH. *Reasoning:* the ticket's recommendation; a Mac without a tiling WM needs
  nothing. *Reversing:* low.
- **Locks.** *Ruling:* `just live-shot` always takes the desktop witness's lock
  (`$TMPDIR/knobas-desktop-witness.lock`), so one witness or live-shot runs at a time. It takes
  a product's lock only when `LIVE_SHOT_PRODUCT` names a product it starts through
  `live_session`: the Gitea lock for Gitea, the JVM lock for a JVM product. *Reasoning:* the
  ticket's recommendation. `live_session` already holds the right lock and puts the product
  back. *Reversing:* low.
- **Mouse buttons 3 and 4 as steps.** *Ruling:* `back:<name>` and `forward:<name>`, CDP
  `button: "back"`/`"forward"` at the element's centre. *Reasoning:* they are the names the app
  (`TfShell`, #693) and CDP give them. A fixture that does not `preventDefault` the press is
  navigated back by Chrome itself, so the shot test's fixture prevents it the way the app does.
  *Reversing:* low.
- **What a pointer step can name.** *Ruling:* first the elements `click:` would take, but only
  those with a box. Failing those, the innermost element whose whole text is the name (a table
  row's key cell), so `dblclick:PAY-231` reaches a row that is no button. `click:` itself is
  unchanged. *Reasoning:* the ticket asks for `click:`'s resolution, and rows that open on a
  double-click (`TicketsPage`'s `<tr>`) have no name or test id. The brief forbids adding a
  label to the app to reach one. *Reversing:* low, one branch in `findJs`.
- **How the driver's commands are given.** *Ruling:* a steps file of bash that `live-shot.sh`
  sources after the window is up, with `shot`, `press`, `focus`, `click-at`, `type`, `key` and
  `settle` defined as functions. *Reasoning:* a step can then read the product's `./seed --env`
  (`type "$KNOBAS_GITEA_TOKEN"`), which a step passed on the command line cannot, because the
  product only comes up inside the run. *Reversing:* low.
- **The witness, four runs.** *Ruling:* the slot was used for four `just live-shot` runs, all
  in the foreground and one after another. The first three found driver bugs: the web view was
  blank when the window appeared, a field sat below the dialog's fold, and an `Id` typed after
  ⌘A came out capitalised (the steps file now keeps the default id). Each bug was fixed in the
  driver, not the app. *Reasoning:* the brief says to fix the driver when it cannot find an
  element, and only a run shows that the fix works. *Reversing:* none; this records what ran.
- **Merge-manager: `pick` accepts no ambiguous match, no pin owed.** *Ruling:* the surviving
  mutant (an ambiguous match accepted) is not pinned. `choose` already refuses a count other than
  one without an `n`; the unit test has no window to hold two matches, and a pin would need a
  fixture window the gate does not have. Instead the unit test now blanks `LIVE_SHOT_PRODUCT`
  and `LIVE_SHOT_AEROSPACE` in its dry runs, so an exported variable cannot start a product
  inside a gate. *Reasoning:* the refusal is one guard, read in review; the hazard that mattered
  was the env leak. *Reversing:* low.

## #1564 — how *inherited* is marked, and which fixture parameter carries it

Ruled 2026-10-21 by the implementer (Sonnet).

## #1583 — what tells a withdrawal from a send

Ruled 2026-10-21 by the implementer (Sonnet).

**The fork:** the follower hears `undefined` when a write leaves `pending_writes`, whether it was sent or withdrawn; no IPC carries the difference, and a sent write's mark must stay until the read shows it.

**Ruling:** the signal is client-side: the queue store's `discard` announces a successful withdrawal (`noteWithdrawn` in `write-queue.svelte.ts`), and `markQueued` listens (`onWithdrawn`) for every mark with a write id, following or not. The mark goes quietly, with no toast. No IPC change.

**Reasoning:** the ticket allows no IPC change where a client-visible signal exists. Listening apart from the follower keeps the drop safe if the follower has already left on the same queue read.

**Cost of reversing:** a withdrawal made in another window of the app does not drop this window's mark; it falls back to today's behaviour (until a newer run lands). Removing the hook is two small functions.
## #1501: a ticket's job context is archived while the ticket is done (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **The one-time pass is a startup pass, not a migration.** *Ruling:* `sources::bring_up` runs
  `knobas_core::context::archive_done` after the installed adapters load and before the scheduler
  starts, on every bring-up, with no marker. *Reasoning:* the done-like sets are in the adapters'
  descriptors, which SQL cannot read, so a migration could only add a marker; the statement only
  archives a live context on a done anchor, so every bring-up after the first finds nothing. A
  marker would cost a migration and a §10.8 line for nothing. *Reversing:* low.
- **The pass archives and never revives.** *Ruling:* archive only. *Reasoning:* a source whose
  adapter is not loaded declares nothing, and reviving on that would undo what its last sync run
  decided. Reviving is the sync run's job. *Reversing:* low.
- **The sync run reconciles every context of its source, every run.** *Ruling:* after the saved
  views, inside the run's transaction, off the mirror, over every context anchored on one of the
  source's live items, and not gated on the source declaring a set. *Reasoning:* an incremental
  run that saw a ticket unchanged must leave it as the last run did, which a whole-source
  reconcile does by construction. A changed declaration then takes effect on the next run, and a
  source that stops declaring a set revives what it archived. Contexts are few, so the join is
  cheap. *Reversing:* low.
- **Born archived without a migration.** *Fork:* widen `context_anchor_idx` to cover archived
  rows (a migration that fails on a database already holding two contexts on one anchor), or
  serialise promotes. *Ruling:* `promote` takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(47, hashtext(anchor))` in
  its transaction, in the two-key space that never meets a sync run's one-key lock.
  *Reasoning:* the partial index cannot keep two born-archived contexts apart, and the lock does
  without touching the schema. *Reversing:* low.
- **Which context `promote` answers with.** *Ruling:* the live one, else the newest archived one.
  *Reasoning:* before #1501 an archived context could be followed by a fresh one on the same
  anchor, so an old database may hold several. *Reversing:* low.
- **Which context revives.** *Ruling:* the newest archived one per anchor, and none where the
  anchor already has a live one. *Reasoning:* the unique index allows one live context per
  anchor, and a revive that broke it would fail the whole run. *Reversing:* low.
- **A done job still reaches what its context held.** *Fork:* leave `reach_walk!`'s
  `archived_at is null`, or drop it. *Ruling:* drop it. *Reasoning:* "a reopened done job is
  reading, not working"; with the filter, everything a person added to a job would vanish from
  its page the moment the ticket went Done. `member_ids` already answers about a context whatever
  its state; only the inbox's alert rule and the open jobs ask whether anyone is still working.
  *Reversing:* low, one clause.
- **`promote_context` reads the declarations from the lifecycle's registry.** *Ruling:* the
  command takes `lifecycle.pool()` and `lifecycle.registry()`, as `get_entity` does. *Reasoning:*
  the lifecycle's registry is the process registry the sync engine shares (`Registry::for_process`),
  so it holds the same done-like sets, and opening a job keeps answering once the database is up
  instead of `not_ready` until the engine is. Overruled by the merge-manager on Opus: the
  implementer's version took `sources::state`, which would fail a job page opened during
  bring-up. *Reversing:* low.
- **No WIT change and no contract bump.** *Ruling:* `adapter.wit` stays at
  `knobas:adapter@1.3.0`. *Reasoning:* the descriptor crosses as serde JSON, as #1475 ruled for
  `url_forms`; the field is `#[serde(default)]`, and `convert`'s new test witnesses both an old
  and a new component. *Reversing:* low.
- **Gitea declares no set, as the ticket says.** *Ruling:* empty, with the reason beside
  `ticket_paths()`. A Gitea issue's status is `open` or `closed`, and `closed` is done-like, so
  the body is too narrow there: follow-up #1593 (`ready-for-agent`). The mock adapter declares
  none either, so the demo's finished jobs stay as drawn. *Reversing:* one line each.
- **No event when a run archives.** *Ruling:* the sync run emits no `contexts:changed`.
  *Reasoning:* the views that read the open jobs read them on mount, and the sync crate has no
  event for contexts. *Reversing:* low.
- **`list_contexts` is witnessed through `knobas_core::context::list`.** The command has no inner
  function and is that call alone, so the IPC test reads it there, beside `open_alerts` and
  `inbox_items_inner`. *Reversing:* none.

### Reserved for Björn, ruled by implementer on Opus

- **The §10.8 sign-off** (`docs/contract/10.8/1501-done-statuses-and-the-job-context-lifecycle.md`).
  *Ruling:* signed. The entry matches the diff: one additive `KindPaths` field, the regenerated
  `sources.ts`, `promote_context`'s answer now archived where its anchor is done, the sync run's
  step, the bring-up pass and the reach change. No command, argument, migration or WIT change.
  *Reversing:* a follow-up removing the field and the step; every adapter but Jira declares none.

### #1501, merge-manager (Opus, 2026-10-21)

- **A done job's reach keeps its context's adds.** *Fork:* the implementer's widening of
  `reach_walk!`, which the ticket does not ask for, against #446's inbox rule and the open jobs.
  *Ruling:* confirmed. *Reasoning:* the inbox reads `held_by_any_context!` and the open jobs read
  `list`, and both still skip archived contexts; reach answers about one job by name, as
  `member_ids` does. Without it, archiving on Done would empty a finished job's page. Search's
  `reach:` and the job drawer's parent read share the walk, so the §10.8 entry now names them.
  *Reversing:* one clause.
- **The sync run checks every context of its source on every run.** *Ruling:* confirmed.
  *Reasoning:* the statement joins `knobas.context` (people-made, so small) to `sync.item` by its
  key and writes only the rows that move, so a large mirror costs one indexed probe per context;
  runs of different sources touch disjoint rows, and runs of one source are serialised by its
  advisory lock. *Reversing:* low.
- **`promote`'s advisory lock.** *Ruling:* kept. *Reasoning:* transaction-scoped, so a dropped
  transaction releases it when the pool flushes the rollback; `promote` takes no other lock while
  holding it, and a sync run never takes key space 47, so no cycle. A promote inserts only on an
  anchor with no context at all and a sync run revives only existing ones, so the two never race
  on `context_anchor_idx`. *Reversing:* low.

### Reserved for Björn, ruled by merge-manager on Opus

- **The §10.8 sign-off.** *Ruling:* confirmed, on the entry as amended in review (the lifecycle's
  registry for `promote_context`; the two other `reach_walk!` readers named). *Reasoning:* the
  field is additive and `#[serde(default)]` on both sides of the WIT (`convert`'s test decodes a
  component without it), `adapter.wit` is unchanged, and the entry now matches the diff.
  *Reversing:* a follow-up removing the field and the step.

## #1581 — how the launcher strip reads a source's last run

Ruled 2026-10-21 by the implementer (Sonnet).

**The fork:** the strip holds credential health only. The run's outcome reaches it how, in which words, and for which sources.

**Ruling:** `App.svelte`'s `dialogs` snippet is handed the shell's `sync` rows (`TfShell` already holds them from `sync_status` and `sync:state`), and passes them as `runs` through `Launcher` to `Board`. The strip calls `sourceState` (the source page's reading) per source. A credential state `isActionable` flags keeps its err tone and detail; otherwise a warn reading (a failed run) draws the warn tone with the reading's text (*Failed 30 min ago*). Nothing else of `sourceState`'s output is used: the board knows neither `enabled` nor the role misses, so it passes `enabled: true` and no misses. No IPC change.

**Reasoning:** one reading, no second table of words. `SourceSyncStatus` carries no error text, so the note is the page's *Failed … ago*, not the run's error.

**Cost of reversing:** the snippet argument, one prop and the strip's derivation.

**Known gap:** a paused source whose last run errored is flagged on the strip but reads *Paused* on the page.
## #1485: the scheduler requests a suggestion pass after every OK run (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Where the request is made.** *Fork:* the ticket allows a handle on `SchedulerDeps` beside the `Analyzer`, or a `SyncEvents` decorator like `ArrivalLinks`. *Ruling:* the decorator, `suggestion_pass::SuggestOnSync`, wrapped around `ArrivalLinks` in `sources::bring_up`. It requests on the `sync:state` that ends a run (`running == false`) whose outcome is `Ok`. The emit that starts a run carries the previous run's outcome and requests nothing. *Reasoning:* `knobas-sync` cannot name `SuggestionPass`, which lives in `knobas-app`, so a deps field would need a new trait plus edits to the 35 `SchedulerDeps` literals across both crates' tests. #1501 is working in the same after-run area, and a decorator leaves `knobas-sync` untouched. *Cost:* `emit_state` skips its emit when the source was deleted mid-run or the status read fails, so that run requests no pass. The next OK run requests one, and `similar_text` picks up everything that changed since it last compared. *Reversing:* low. Move the `request()` to `Scheduler::run` beside `analyzer.request()` and add the deps field.
- **Where the one pass is built.** *Ruling:* in `spawn_bring_up`, before `sources::start`, which takes it as a third argument (`BringUp::suggestions`). The same value goes into `AppState`. `tests/it/wiring.rs` reads the source and fails if `SuggestionPass::` appears in bring-up more than once. *Reasoning:* the scheduler starts before `AppState` is installed, so bring-up is the one place that holds both. *Reversing:* low.
- **`test_scheduler` gets no pass.** *Ruling:* the test-only scheduler over the shared IPC test database requests no pass. *Reasoning:* a pass reads the whole mirror and proposes into it, so every test sharing that database would gain proposals. `bring_up` carries the pass, and the new tests run it on a scratch database. *Reversing:* low.
- **`SuggestionPass::passes()` and `idle()`.** *Ruling:* added beside `request()`, mirroring `Analyzer::passes`/`idle`. *Reasoning:* without them nobody can see whether a pass that nobody waits on has run. `passes()` is how the bring-up test tells whether the pass it handed in is the one the scheduler requested. *Reversing:* low.
- **`suggestion pass finished` logs at `info`.** *Fork:* the criterion "`just demo`, plus a few syncs, logs `suggestion pass finished`" cannot pass at the app's default `info` filter, because the line was `debug`. That also means the audit's "no line in the log" evidence never depended on whether a pass ran. *Ruling:* raise it to `info`. *Reasoning:* there is at most one line per OK sync run, the same volume as that run's own `sync started`, and it is the only sign in the log that passes happen. *Reversing:* trivial.
- **Diagram.** The suggestion-pass SVGs lose the tray box. The scheduler's arrow now goes straight to the queue, labelled `SuggestOnSync: request()`, and `detect_suggestions` comes in as the manual caller. The window box is the Proposed links accept/dismiss, and the per-room caps the tray drew are dropped.
- **Merge-manager on Opus: the decorator ruling stands.** *Fork:* uphold `SuggestOnSync`, or move the request beside `analyzer.request()` in `Scheduler::run`. *Ruling:* uphold. *Reasoning:* the ticket's *Key interfaces* names the `SyncEvents` decorator as an allowed seam. `emit_state` is the one `sync_state` caller in the scheduler, and the run's ending is reported to its watchers only after `settle` has emitted, so the new tests cannot read `passes()` before the request. The two runs that ask for no pass are a source deleted mid-run, whose mirror is being purged anyway, and a failed status read, where the database is already in trouble. The next OK run catches up on both. The pass's connection sits outside every pool, so `EmbeddedDb::stop` does not wait for it, and `pg_ctl stop -m fast` ends it at quit. *Reversing:* low, as above.

## #1603 — how `shot-steps.mjs` closes its Chrome (Sonnet implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Fork:** keep `chrome.kill()` (SIGTERM to the main process) and wait for it to exit, or kill harder. **Ruling:** spawn Chrome `detached` (its own process group) and SIGKILL the group from one `closeChrome`, called by `done()`, by SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers and by the process's `exit` event. **Reasoning:** `done()` is synchronous and followed by `process.exit`, so it cannot wait; SIGTERM only reaches the main process, which can ignore it early in start-up, and leaves helpers. The profile is a throwaway temp directory, so a hard kill loses nothing. **Cost of reversing:** low, one function.
- **Fork:** the orphan did not reproduce on this tree (ten runs of `scripts/shot-test.sh`, none left a Chrome), so the old code cannot be shown to leak. **Ruling:** the fix closes the unproven race anyway; `scripts/shot-test.sh` now fails if any process names `--user-data-dir=$fixture`, which would catch a regression that leaks reliably. A mutant restoring the old `chrome.kill()` survives; one making `closeChrome` a no-op dies.
## #1553: Depends on this lists the routes landing on anything that breaks (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **Widen `depends_on_this.routes`, or keep the narrow reading.** *Fork:* the ticket offers both:
  (a) routes whose target is the asset or any asset in its closure, or (b) routes whose target is
  the asset itself, recorded so later audits stop expecting more. *Ruling:* (a). *Reasoning:* the
  panel answers *what breaks if this goes down*. A route landing on a container stops answering
  when the machine holding the container goes down, so leaving it off answers that question
  wrong. The narrow reading also leaves the panel empty for every machine in
  `testenv/estate.json`, because every route there lands on a container. #432 widened **Route**'s
  *reachable via* on that argument. Story 52's purpose, *"so that the number is about assets"*,
  holds: the routes stay beneath the count and outside it. #505's own reasoning for the narrow
  read was about routes **above** the asset (*"a route landing on the VM above still answers
  whatever else that VM holds"*), and those stay out. The glossary entry is amended in the same
  PR, as the ticket's option (a) says, so nothing here contradicts it. *Reversing:* one `where`
  clause, the fake's filter, the glossary amendment and a §10.8 entry.
- **What "the closure" is.** *Ruling:* the asset plus exactly `DependsOnThis.assets`: containment
  and the two link relations, read toward the asset. A route landing on an asset that holds the
  subject, or on an asset only linked *from* it, is not listed. *Reasoning:* the routes then
  follow the same walk as the count, so the two halves of the panel cannot disagree about what
  went down. *Reversing:* low.
- **Order and labelling.** *Ruling:* still by name, with no new field and no change to either
  renderer. *Reasoning:* `RouteRow.target_id`/`target_name` already say where each route lands,
  so a "lands on" column would be a UI choice, not this read's job. The Tree's panel and the
  editor's *Needed by* read the same answer, so they agree. *Reversing:* low.

### #1553: merge-manager rulings (Opus, 2026-10-21)

- **Does the widening contradict spec #491 story 52 or #505?** *Ruling:* no; merged as ruled.
  *Reasoning:* story 52 asks that routes whose target is the asset be listed beneath and not
  counted, and they still are: the new list contains the old one. #505's case for the narrow read
  was a route landing on the VM *above* the asset, which still answers, and
  `a_route_landing_on_what_holds_the_asset_does_not_break_with_it` keeps those out. #432 widened
  **Route**'s *reachable via* on the same argument (every route in the estate lands on a
  container). The ticket offered this option with the glossary amendment. *Reversing:* as the
  implementer's ruling above.
- **Is a route order owed a test?** *Fork:* both new tests sort the ids, so `ROUTES_TO`'s
  `order by r.name` went unwitnessed, and the list a machine shows grew from at most three rows to
  nine. *Ruling:* yes for the backend, no for the fake. The VM test now asserts the routes come back
  in the order the same database sorts their names (`unnest … order by`), not a literal list: the
  names mix cases and `en_US.UTF-8` sorts case differently across platforms. Dropping the
  `order by` fails it (file order comes back). The fake keeps the file's `localeCompare` convention
  (as `assetColumn` and the depends walk do) without a test of its own. *Reasoning:* both readers
  render the IPC order as given, so the backend order is what a user sees. *Reversing:* delete
  one assertion.

## #1513: no built-in adapter reports a credential's expiry (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

The constraint is #1403's grilling ruling: the countdown's date comes from the source itself, never
typed. Each built-in was checked against what its source publishes, not only against its endpoint
set.

- **Ruling: the countdown stays an external-adapter feature; no endpoint is added.** *Fork:* read
  the token's expiry during the health check (Jira and Confluence DC from `/rest/pat/latest/tokens`,
  TeamCity from `/app/rest/users/current/tokens`), or report nothing. *Ruling:* nothing, and spec
  §3's row says so. *Reasoning, per source:*
  - **Jira and Confluence DC.** `/rest/pat/latest/tokens` lists every token of the account, and the
    Atlassian PAT documentation names no field that ties a row to the bearer of the request. The
    date would be the source's, but the choice of row would be knobas' guess, which #1403 rules
    out. A password source has no expiry at all, and its listing could still hold tokens.
  - **TeamCity.** The `Token` schema is `name`, `creationTime`, `value` (shown only at creation),
    `expirationTime`, `permissionRestrictions`: the same listing with the same gap. The client test's
    note "TeamCity exposes no token expiry over REST" was wrong and now says this.
  - **Gitea.** The `AccessToken` schema (`gitea.com/swagger.v1.json`, checked 2026-10-21) is
    `created_at`, `id`, `last_used_at`, `name`, `scopes`, `sha1`, `token_last_eight`. There is no
    expiry to report.
  - **Uptime Kuma.** An API key opens `/metrics` and nothing else (contract §4.2), and no gauge
    carries the key's expiry; the key's settings are on socket.io.
  *Reversing:* medium. A §4.2 read-endpoint row and a §10.8 entry per adapter, mockd's Jira
  subset, and `just jira-live`/`just confluence-live`/`just teamcity-live`. The live suites'
  `secret_expires_at == None` assertions would flip.
- **Rejected: report the expiry when the listing holds exactly one token.** *Fork:* a narrower
  read of the same listings. *Ruling:* no. *Reasoning:* with Bearer auth and
  one listed token, that token must be the one in use, so the date would be honest. But it goes
  silent as soon as the account holds a second token for another tool, which is the usual case.
  No run here has measured whether a PAT may list tokens at all (the live suite lists them with
  the password). That buys a narrow case for a frozen-contract change and three JVM live runs.
  *Reversing:* as above, plus one count check in each adapter.
- **The stale wording is fixed in comments only.** "PAT expiry countdown" becomes "credential
  expiry countdown" in `knobas-sync` (`health.rs`, `config.rs`, a test's doc comment),
  `knobas-source/src/lib.rs` and `knobas-core/src/inbox.rs`, and the IPC mirror is regenerated.
  The Jira and Confluence notes that said "the countdown shows as soon as that endpoint is added"
  now give the reason it would not. The live suites' assertion messages ("PAT expiry needs
  /rest/pat/latest/tokens, which is outside this adapter's endpoint set") are still true and stay
  as they are, so no live suite is owed. `docs/contract.md` still says "PAT expiry countdown"
  (§1, line 53, and §7's P4); it is frozen, and the wording is history there. *Reversing:* n/a.

## #1571: a failed sign-in is an inbox item of its own, routed by its own switch (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **What a failed sign-in is.** *Ruling:* `auth_state` is `unauthorized` or `missing_secret` on an
  enabled source. *Reasoning:* the dispatch asked for the shell's `signInFails` definition, and the
  scheduler skips the same two states. `unreachable` is retried on its own and `unknown` vouches for
  nothing. A disabled source is excluded, as for a credential expiry. *Reversing:* one `in` list.
- **The lifecycle.** *Fork:* how often the item is raised, and what clears it. *Ruling:* once per
  **episode**, where an episode is the run of consecutive failing verdicts. The item is dated at
  the episode's first verdict, so a retry rejected again (or a rejection becoming a missing secret)
  neither moves the row nor brings back an item marked done. **Any** verdict that is not a failure
  ends the episode, and the item leaves by construction. That includes `unreachable` and `unknown`,
  not only `ok`. The next failure is a new episode, and it comes back past the old *done*.
  *Reasoning:* the item then exists exactly while the status strip, the Builds warn line and the
  queued-write toast say the sign-in fails, so no surface contradicts another. *Cost:* an
  `unreachable` verdict between two rejections makes two episodes, so a *done* answered in the
  first does not hide the second. *Reversing:* the trigger's first branch.
- **Where the episode's start lives.** *Fork:* date the item at `auth_checked_at` (no migration),
  add a column that `set_health` writes, or add a column a trigger keeps. *Ruling:* the column
  `auth_failing_since` with a trigger (migration `0055`, §10.8 entry
  `1571-migration-0055-auth-failing-since.md`). *Reasoning:* `auth_checked_at` moves on every
  verdict, so a retry would undo a *done*, and that is once per attempt, not once per episode.
  The trigger keeps the column for every writer of `auth_state` (`set_health`, the restore's
  `missing_secret`, a raw `update`), so no future writer can forget it. `knobas-sync`'s
  `config.rs`, where #1513 is working, is untouched, and the rule's read of the health columns
  is a statement of its own in `knobas_core::inbox`. *Reversing:* medium (a migration dropping
  the column and the function, and a §10.8 entry).
- **The category and its key.** *Ruling:* `failed_sign_in`, keyed `failed_sign_in:<source id>`,
  after `credential_expiry` in `Category::ALL`. *Reasoning:* the name parallels `failed_build`.
  The subject is the source, as for an expiry, because no entity is involved. Placing it next to
  the expiry puts the two source-level switches side by side. *Reversing:* a rename is a §10.8 entry
  plus a rewrite of stored `inbox_state` keys.
- **The switch.** *Fork:* a new switch, or a rename pass over the existing one. *Ruling:* a new
  switch, labelled *A source cannot sign in*, off by default. The `credential_expiry` switch keeps
  #1439's *A source's credential is about to expire*. *Reasoning:* the label is prototype-6's own
  wording, which #1439 removed from the expiry switch because no rejected sign-in fired that
  category. With its own category, the label now names what fires it. Off by default is story 71's
  rule for every kind. *Reversing:* one string and one test line.
- **What the row says and does.** *Ruling:* the reason is `the <name> sign-in was rejected` or
  `no credential is stored for <name>`, without the server's detail. The kind word is *Sign-in*,
  with no kind chip (a credential expiry has none either). The row gets the err dot. It offers no
  source action. *Open source* goes to the source's page in Settings, where *Re-enter* is, and a
  desktop notification's click goes to the same address. *Reasoning:* the two failures ask for the
  same act but get different prompts on the source's page. The detail belongs to that page.
  *Reversing:* low.
- **The inbox re-reads on `source:health`.** *Ruling:* added to the store's subscriptions beside
  `activity:new` and `sync:state`. *Reasoning:* *Test connection* and *Re-enter* settle a verdict
  with no run behind them, so the item would appear or leave only on the next sync. *Reversing:*
  one array entry.
- **A second episode in one session is not announced again.** *Ruling:* unchanged notifier.
  *Reasoning:* the glossary's **Desktop notification** is once per item per session, keyed by
  `<category>:<subject>`. The inbox row comes back for the new episode, and #447 accepted the
  same trade for a monitor that goes down twice. *Reversing:* a per-episode key, which would
  change the key format.
- **No step of the ticket is reserved for Björn.** The §10.8 entries are ratified under the
  2026-10-18 reserved-steps rule, as #1285's were.

## #1585: a source's page names the store its credential is in (Opus implementer, 2026-10-21)

- **How does the frontend learn the store?** *Fork:* the ticket offers telling the frontend which
  store is in use, or having the page say "Stored for this session only" for the memory store; the
  page cannot tell on its own, so either way a fact crosses the bridge. *Ruling:* `AppStatus` gains
  `secrets_in_memory: bool` (§10.8 entry `1585-app-status-secrets-in-memory.md`), and the page says
  *Stored for this session only* when it is `true`, on the credential row and in the Re-enter
  note. *Reasoning:* `app_status` already carries app-level facts (`demo`, the version) and answers
  before the database is up; a per-source field (`CredentialHealth`) would repeat one process-wide
  fact on every row. A bool, not a store name: the frontend has one decision to make, and the
  keychain's name already comes from the platform. *Reversing:* cheap, one field and one line.
- **One decision, not two reads of the environment.** *Fork:* `app_status` could read
  `KNOBAS_SECRET_STORE` again. *Ruling:* `sources::SecretStoreKind` is decided once in `setup`,
  managed, and both the store bring-up and `app_status` read it. *Reasoning:* the report and the
  store cannot disagree, and a test manages either value without touching the process
  environment. `profile.rs` is frozen (§10.8), so the kind is its own managed value, not a
  `Profile` field. *Reversing:* cheap.
- **The keychain line is unchanged for the real store.** It reads "Stored in the macOS keychain"
  on a Mac and "Stored in the system keychain" elsewhere (the user agent decides, as before). Until
  `app_status` answers, or if it fails, the page names the keychain: the store every run but a QA
  run uses. `?fake-secret-store=memory` makes the `?fake-ipc` fixture answer as the memory store
  does.
- **The importer token hint is not this ticket's** (Opus merge-manager, 2026-10-22). *Fork:*
  `ImportDialog.svelte` and `TfImport.svelte` also say an importer token is "Kept in this
  machine's keychain", and that is just as untrue under the memory store. *Ruling:* out of scope
  here, filed as #1615 (`backlog`). *Reasoning:* the ticket names a source's page in Settings ›
  Sources, and the importer is a different surface. `secrets_in_memory` is now there for #1615 to
  read. *Reversing:* cheap.

## #1626: TeamCity per-configuration incremental query and the ceiling below the watermark (Opus implementer, 2026-10-22)

- **Which sources ask per configuration.** *Ruling:* a source with a non-empty `build_type_ids`,
  whether or not it also names projects. A project-only scope keeps the global query, as the
  spec's "an unscoped source keeps the global query" reads for anything without a configuration
  list: a project has no locator dimension in the contract, and asking per configuration of a
  whole project trades one query for as many as it holds. *Reversing:* low, one match arm.
- **Where the per-configuration list comes from.** *Ruling:* the same `/buildTypes` listing a full
  sync reads, filtered by `scope`, not `cfg.build_type_ids` as typed. A configuration the list
  names and the server no longer has is then not asked about, which a `buildType:(id:…)` locator
  on a missing id would otherwise turn into a failed run every poll; step 6 reuses the listing.
  The cost, on every incremental run of such a source, idle ones included, is `/projects` and
  `/buildTypes` (the scope needs the tree) plus one `sinceBuild` query per configuration: three
  requests become four plus one per configuration. (Cost corrected by the merge-manager, which
  found the implementer's "one `/buildTypes` request" short of the `/projects` read.)
  *Reversing:* low.
- **The scoped source's watermark.** *Ruling:* the newest in-scope finished build. A foreign
  finished build is no longer in any answer, so it no longer moves the watermark; that rule kept
  the *global* query from growing, and a per-configuration query carries only its own builds. The
  seeded live test that asserted the server's newest id for a scoped incremental run now asserts
  the scope's. *Reversing:* low.
- **The per-configuration refusal.** *Ruling:* it names Backfill as well, and the configuration.
  The global refusal also says a configuration list keeps it from recurring, the one narrowing
  that now changes the query. *Reversing:* low, a string.
- **The walk reading.** *Ruling:* unchanged: an incremental run reports its walk over the builds
  it listed, and the per-configuration queries before it report none. *Reversing:* low.
- **What ignoring a ceiling below the watermark gives up.** *Ruling:* accepted as the spec states
  it, and written down in `cursor::advance`'s docs: for that one run, the clamp no longer covers a
  build queued after the in-flight poll and still running while a later-queued build finished
  before the finished query. On an incremental run that window is the few requests between the
  two queries; against it stands a re-emission of the same builds on every poll. A ceiling equal
  to the watermark still clamps. *Reversing:* low, one `filter`.
  (Amended 2026-10-24 by #1989: for a source scoped to a configuration list the window is
  `C + 2` requests or more, not a few. See `## #1989` below.)
- **Glossary.** *Ruling:* CONTEXT.md's *Backfill* also names the cap refusal as a case it is the
  way out of. *Reversing:* low.
