- **A board one pass alone holds is kept** (merge-manager, Opus). *Fork:* keep the union, or drop a board the second pass no longer lists. *Ruling:* keep the union. *Reasoning:* a board only the first pass holds is either deleted between the passes or stepped over by the second. A deleted one 404s on its configuration read, which `boards` leaves out, so `sync.rs` delivers it as gone. A stepped-over one reads fine and stays. A board only the second pass holds is one the first stepped over. Neither case needs a rule of its own. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Across two project listings, the earlier project's record wins** (merge-manager, Opus). *Fork:* also order the project listings newest first, or keep them in project order. *Ruling:* keep project order. *Reasoning:* the second-pass-first order picks the newer record inside one listing. A board on two synced projects is held by both listings, and `dedup_by_key` keeps the first project's record, as before this PR. A rename landing between the two project listings is delivered at the next board read. Nothing is tombstoned, and the `after_first_page` fake can't witness it without switching on a page count. *Reversing:* prepend each project's listing in `boards`.
- **Every board read lists twice, upheld** (merge-manager, Opus). *Fork:* list twice only when the read can send `gone`. *Ruling:* every read. *Reasoning:* every board read whose previous cursor holds a view can send `gone`. The only read that can't is the first, where skipping the second pass would save one request, once. The second pass is one page per 50 boards, while each board costs at least three requests (configuration, filter, keys search), so it adds under 1% to a board read. *Reversing:* a flag to `listing`.
- **"None reported gone" read as "no other board", upheld** (merge-manager, Opus). *Reasoning:* the ticket's *What to build* names the harm as a live view tombstoned. Read literally, the criterion would contradict `a_board_deleted_in_jira_is_delivered_as_gone_at_the_next_sync`. The ticket isn't wrong, only loosely worded, so no follow-up. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **No second live run** (merge-manager, Opus). *Reasoning:* after `257f2660`, the full live run's head, the production change is only which pass goes first. Against the seeded Jira both passes return identical records, and no live test renames a board mid-read. The live file's change is the `Probes` merge, and both of its users ran on `9b33e967`. The rebase brought in #2021 alone, which is `knobas-app` only. *Reversing:* one `just jira-live`.

## #2007: a data directory an `initdb` cleanup cut short after `PG_VERSION` left (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **Reproduce on Linux first.** *Fork:* reproduce it, or close the ticket because the order rules both states out. *Ruling:* reproduced. One of the ticket's two states arises, plus a third it did not name. *Reasoning:* a throwaway `ubuntu-latest` workflow (runs 40104881162 and 40107207840, on a branch since deleted) ran PostgreSQL 18.6's `initdb` (the theseus-rs binaries `postgresql_embedded` installs) with knobas's flags on seven filesystems: the runner's ext4, four loop-mounted ext4 with different hash seeds, xfs, btrfs and tmpfs. Each run sent `SIGTERM` once `base/5` existed, then `SIGKILL` at one of eight points: at once, after the first top-level file went, after `postgresql.conf`, after `PG_VERSION`, after every file, after `global/`, after `base/1`, after `base/5`. There were 12 runs per point on the runner's disk and 6 on each other filesystem, plus one run per point with every removal slowed 20 ms under `strace`. PostgreSQL's `rmtree` unlinks the top level's files in `readdir` order and removes the directories only after every file (`src/common/rmtree.c` defers them). Where the filesystem lists `postgresql.conf` or `pg_hba.conf` before `PG_VERSION`, a kill leaves `PG_VERSION` without them, with every directory and `base/1`, `4` and `5` in place. Every ext4 tried and tmpfs list one of them that way, so six filesystems of seven left such a state (ext4b only in the slowed runs). On the runner's disk, 24 of 24 runs killed after the first file went left `PG_VERSION`, `pg_hba.conf`, `pg_ident.conf` and `postgresql.auto.conf`. Main marked that and `initdb` then refused it. ext4d and tmpfs also left `PG_VERSION` with `postgresql.conf` but without `pg_hba.conf`. Main marked that too, and the server will not start without `pg_hba.conf` (*could not load pg_hba.conf*). It starts without `pg_ident.conf` or `postgresql.auto.conf`. xfs and btrfs list `PG_VERSION` before the other files, as APFS does. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **The ticket's second state does not arise from `initdb`.** *Fork:* recover it as well, or close it on the evidence. *Ruling:* closed on the evidence. *Reasoning:* `PG_VERSION` and `postgresql.conf` with `base/` or `pg_tblspc/` gone needs a directory removed before a file, and `rmtree` removes no directory until every file is gone. No kill on any of the seven filesystems left one, at any point. Knobas's own removal of an unfinished directory could leave it: `std::fs::remove_dir_all` recurses into each entry as `readdir` lists it, and on ext4b `global/` went before `PG_VERSION` (folded in; see below). *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Recover the reproduced states, or fail naming the directory.** *Fork:* the dispatch prefers failing unless it can be proved that no server ever ran in the directory. *Ruling:* recover when the proof holds. With `PG_VERSION` and one of `initdb`'s other files (`INITDB_FILES`: `postgresql.conf`, `postgresql.auto.conf`, `pg_hba.conf`, `pg_ident.conf`) gone, the directory is unfinished and is removed only when no `postmaster.opts` exists, `base/` holds nothing but `1`, `4` and `5`, and `pg_tblspc/` is empty. Otherwise it is `Shape::Unrecognised`: kept, never marked, and the launch fails. `initdb` names the directory when it refuses it as not empty. *Reasoning:* every postmaster start writes `postmaster.opts` (the run read it back after one `pg_ctl start`) and nothing in PostgreSQL removes it. `initdb` never writes it, and no kill state had one. `postgres` will not start on a directory with no `postgresql.conf` (*could not access the server configuration file*). So without `postmaster.opts`, no server ever ran in the directory, the `knobas` database was never created, and `base/5` is the `postgres` database `initdb` had just made. The cleanup removes every file before any directory, so a missing `base/` or `pg_tblspc/` with `PG_VERSION` still there remains a doubt and keeps the directory. *Reversing:* one branch in `shape`.
- **A doubt that has lost one of `initdb`'s files stays unmarked.** *Fork:* mark it as `HoldsDatabase` is marked, or keep it unmarked. *Ruling:* `PG_VERSION` with a file gone and a database, a missing `base/`, an unreadable `base/` or a `postmaster.opts` reads as `Unrecognised`, not `HoldsDatabase`. With every file there, a doubt is `HoldsDatabase` and is marked, as #1824 ruled. *Reasoning:* a marker on a directory with no `postgresql.conf` or `pg_hba.conf` keeps a later build from ever recovering it, and the launch fails on it either way. A finished cluster has all four files. *Reversing:* one branch.
- **#1819's "holds a database" fixture without `postgresql.conf`.** *Fork:* keep `a_data_directory_that_holds_a_database_is_never_removed`'s `(false, "base/5")` fixture as it was, which this rule now removes, or give it the mark of a server. *Ruling:* it gets a `postmaster.opts`. *Reasoning:* the fixture claimed that `base/5` alone marks a database. #1985 and this ticket show that a cleanup cut short leaves `base/5` behind. A server having run on the directory is what makes `base/5` a database worth keeping. The fixture still checks that `initdb` refuses such a directory and nothing is removed. *Reversing:* one line in the test.
- **A kill before the cleanup starts.** *Fork:* this state also has `base/5` and no marker: change it, or keep marking it. *Ruling:* kept as #1819 ruled: marked and started. *Reasoning:* a `SIGKILL` right after the `SIGTERM` leaves every file in all 48 such runs, plus the standalone backend's `postmaster.pid`. That backend is still running `CREATE DATABASE postgres`. It reads its input to the end, commits, exits and removes its lock. In 5 of 5 runs the server then started, `pg_database` listed `postgres`, `template0` and `template1`, and `create database knobas` succeeded. The cluster is finished in all but the final `fsync`, and the ticket's criteria are about the states a kill *in the cleanup* leaves. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Knobas's own removal leaves `PG_VERSION` last (fixed in passing).** *Fork:* fix it here, or file it. *Ruling:* `remove_unfinished` unlinks `PG_VERSION` before `remove_dir_all`, except when the data directory is a symlink, which loses the link alone as before. *Reasoning:* `std::fs::remove_dir_all` takes entries in `readdir` order and recurses into each directory as it finds it. A launch killed partway could leave `PG_VERSION` without `base/`, which reads as a database on a volume not mounted, so it would be marked. Once `PG_VERSION` is gone, whatever the removal leaves reads as unfinished. *Reversing:* one call.
- **Test seams.** *Fork:* confirm the seams with Björn first, as the TDD skill asks, or pick them. *Ruling:* picked, as in #1819 and #1985: `EmbeddedDb::start` for what a launch does with the states the kills left (`a_data_directory_an_initdb_cleanup_cut_short_after_pg_version_left_is_initialised_again`, `a_data_directory_a_server_ran_on_that_lost_an_initdb_file_is_kept_unmarked`), and `shape` and `recover_or_mark` for the cases no launch sets up. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. The second run passed `knobas-db`'s 35 `embedded::` unit tests and its 44 `embedded` integration tests on ext4. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Harness noise.** *Fork:* read the odd runs as states a kill leaves, or as the harness's own. *Ruling:* the harness's own, not a finding. *Reasoning:* on ext4b, ext4c and tmpfs, 7 runs ended before the trigger or left only `base/5`. In those runs, the standalone backend from the previous at-once kill was still running and wrote into the directory the next run had just cleared, so `initdb` refused a directory that was not empty. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **`postmaster.opts` as the sign that a server ran** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* uphold the new arm, tighten it, or keep every such directory and fail naming it. *Ruling:* upheld as it stands. *Reasoning:* the paths that leave a real cluster with no `postmaster.opts` were tried. A `pg_basebackup` copy leaves it out, a reader can delete it, and a file-level restore may skip it. Each of those that carries the reader's data carries the `knobas` database, which is under `base/` with an OID of 16384 or more (`FirstNormalObjectId`), or a tablespace under `pg_tblspc/`, so `base/` holding nothing but `1`, `4` and `5` keeps it. A postmaster writes `postmaster.opts` before it starts the startup process, so no server killed during its own start has written to a database without it, and it cannot get that far with no `postgresql.conf` or `pg_hba.conf`. Every knobas build has kept the reader's data in the `knobas` database (`create_database(DATABASE_NAME)` since #2). It connects to `postgres` only to read `data_directory` and `pg_database` and to create `knobas`. So `postmaster.opts` is a second guard. The `base/` and `pg_tblspc/` checks are what keep the reader's data, and they are the same checks #1824 already made with `PG_VERSION`. *Reversing:* one condition.
- **#1819's fixture lost a direction** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* accept the `postmaster.opts` on the `(false, "base/5")` fixture alone, or launch a `knobas` database too. *Ruling:* add `(false, "base/16384")` with neither `postgresql.conf` nor `postmaster.opts`. *Reasoning:* the change is right for `base/5`, but after it no launch test kept a `knobas` database that had lost its config and had no `postmaster.opts`. Only `shape`'s unit test covered that. With the new fixture, dropping the `base/` check from the new arm fails `a_data_directory_that_holds_a_database_is_never_removed` (tried). *Reversing:* one fixture.
- **The throwaway Linux workflow** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* n/a, a check. *Ruling:* gone. *Reasoning:* `issue-2007-linux-repro` is not on origin, and none of origin's five branches has `.github/workflows/issue-2007-linux-repro.yml`. The diff touches nothing under `.github/`. GitHub still lists the workflow as registered, as it does `windows-locale.yml`, but with no file on any branch it cannot run. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **A copy caught partway** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* tighten the new arm against a `cp -R` or `pg_basebackup` into `data/` caught partway, or accept it. *Ruling:* accepted. *Reasoning:* a copy that has `PG_VERSION` and `base/1`, `4` and `5` but not yet a config file or `base/16384` reads as unfinished and is removed. What is lost is the half-made copy, never its source. The `base/1`, `4` arm from #1824 already removes a copy caught before `base/5`, and a copy into the data directory of a profile knobas is launching on is the reader's own race. *Reversing:* one condition.
- **The kill before the cleanup starts is marked** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* uphold the implementer, or hold it to the ticket's "None is marked as finished". *Ruling:* upheld. *Reasoning:* the criterion is "either comes back from a launch or fails with a message naming the directory. None is marked as finished". This state comes back: 5 of 5 servers started on it and created `knobas`. The marker is the one a finished `initdb` gets, because the cluster is finished. "None is marked" is about the states that cannot come back. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **A kept directory that still has `postgresql.conf` fails without naming itself** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* fix it here or file it. *Ruling:* filed as #2025. *Reasoning:* `initialise` skips `initdb` there, and a failed `pg_ctl start` reports `pg_ctl`'s output alone (`embedded postgres: Command error: stdout=waiting for server to start.... stopped waiting`, witnessed on a cluster with `pg_hba.conf` removed). The server's reason is in `start.log`. No reproduced kill leaves that shape, so #2007's criteria hold. The cause covers every failed server start, five calls of `postgresql.start()`, and the fix changes an error the app shows, which fails the fit test. *Reversing:* n/a.

## #2025: a failed embedded server start names the data directory and the server's reason (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **How the error reads.** *Fork:* keep `DbError::Embedded` and rewrite its text, or a variant of its own; one line or the log as it is. *Ruling:* `DbError::ServerStart { data_dir, reason, source }`, shown as one line: `embedded postgres at <data_dir> did not start: <reason>`, with `postgresql_embedded`'s error kept as its `source`. *Reasoning:* the boot screen (`app/src/lib/shell/Booting.svelte`) prints the message in one `<p>` that wraps and folds line breaks into spaces, under the heading *knobas cannot start its database*, so a multi-line log would run together. The `embedded postgres` prefix stays, so the line opens as it did. A failed restart reads *the database server stopped while knobas was running and did not start again: embedded postgres at … did not start: …* (`crates/knobas-app/src/lib.rs`). No caller matched on `Embedded` for a start, and `DbError` crosses no IPC: the app sends `to_string()`. The boot screen's code is unchanged. *Reversing:* one variant and its `#[error]` string.
- **What the reason is.** *Fork:* the `FATAL` line whole, or from `FATAL:` on. *Ruling:* the text after `FATAL:`, with whitespace collapsed. Witnessed on PostgreSQL 18.6: *could not load /…/data/pg_hba.conf*. *Reasoning:* the log line prefix (timestamp and pid) and the severity word tell the reader nothing the sentence before them doesn't. *Reversing:* one slice.
- **Only this start's lines.** *Fork:* the last `FATAL` in `start.log`, as the ticket words it, or the last one this start wrote. *Ruling:* this start's. `start_server` takes the log's length before `pg_ctl start` and reads only what came after. A log shorter than that was replaced in between, and is read whole. *Reasoning:* `pg_ctl -l` appends, so the file keeps every earlier start's lines. A start that failed without a `FATAL` would otherwise report an earlier start's reason as its own. The `Lock::Cleared` retry follows a start that wrote its own `FATAL` about `postmaster.pid`. *Reversing:* one line.
- **No `FATAL` line.** *Fork:* the ticket's "the whole short log", but how short, and what for a long one. *Ruling:* the last five non-empty lines this start wrote, joined with `; `: all of a short log, the end of a long one. `pg_ctl`'s own output when the start wrote nothing. *Reasoning:* `lc_messages` comes from the environment (#2013 fixes only collation and ctype), and some translations rename the `FATAL` label, so the fallback has to read on its own. Five keeps the line short; no fixture reaches this case, so the number is a judgement, not a measurement. *Reversing:* one constant.
- **Seams.** *Fork:* the TDD skill asks the user to confirm seams, and none is there. *Ruling:* `EmbeddedDb::start` and `restart`'s error text, one test per start site, plus a unit seam on the log reader. *Reasoning:* "this start's lines only" cannot be isolated by a real start: each failure in reach writes its own `FATAL` last. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **The offset is witnessed by a real start after all** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* leave "this start's lines only" to the unit seam, as the seams ruling above says, or find a real failure that writes no `FATAL`. *Ruling:* witnessed: `start_reason::a_start_without_a_fatal_line_never_reports_an_earlier_starts_fatal`. *Reasoning:* a lost `global/pg_control` makes the postmaster write *could not find the database system* to stderr, so into `start.log`, with no `FATAL` label. After a first start's `pg_hba.conf` `FATAL`, reading the log from 0 reports that one; the test dies on that mutant. The seams ruling's "cannot be isolated by a real start" held for the failures the implementer had in reach, not for this one. *Reversing:* one test.
- **How the reason reads on the boot screen** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* uphold the one line, or reshape it. *Ruling:* upheld, with one fix: the fallback joined a sentence the postmaster wraps over a line ending in a comma as `",;`, and now reads it on (`", but could not open file …`). *Reasoning:* `Booting.svelte` renders the message as text in a wrapping `<p>`, so nothing in it is markup and a long path stays in the window. The `pg_hba.conf` case names the directory twice, once in the prefix and once in the server's sentence, which costs a line and says nothing wrong. *Reversing:* one `replace`.
- **Nothing secret reaches the reason** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* filter the reason, or take the log as it is. *Ruling:* as it is. *Reasoning:* the reason is the server's own output from this start, or `pg_ctl`'s, which `DbError::Embedded` already showed. The settings passed at a start are `listen_addresses`, `fsync`, the durable settings and `max_connections`; the superuser password lives in `<root>/.pgpass`, is never a server argument, and the server logs no password at start. The default `log_line_prefix` carries no user. A value from `postgresql.conf` is quoted only in a `LOG` line about an invalid setting, which a `FATAL` follows, so it reaches the reason only through the five-line fallback under a locale that renames `FATAL`, and that file is `initdb`'s. *Reversing:* a filter in `start_reason`.
- **A taken port reports the `FATAL` alone** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* add the `LOG` line before the `FATAL` (*Address already in use*), or keep to the ticket's "the last `FATAL` line". *Ruling:* the ticket's. *Reasoning:* the reason then reads *could not create any TCP/IP sockets*, which names the cause class; the ticket asks for the `FATAL` line, and `restart`'s doc names the taken port as one cause. *Reversing:* one branch in `start_reason`.

## #2028: the adapter SDK, one crate with the WIT bindings and the SPI types (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **Which trait an adapter implements.** *Fork:* `knobas_source::Source` itself, run in the guest under a small executor, or a trait of the SDK's own in `Source`'s shape. *Ruling:* the SDK's own, `knobas_adapter_sdk::Adapter`: `Source`'s methods in the trait's order and with its defaults, synchronous, over the same SPI types, plus `new(Instance)`. *Reasoning:* every call into a component blocks, and `Source` is `async_trait`, takes a `dyn Sink + Send` and has no constructor, while the WIT resource is built from an instance for each call. Implementing `Source` would need an executor in the guest and a second trait for the constructor. Most of `Source`'s doc comments are about the battery and the engine, and they stay with `Source`: `Adapter` points at them. *Cost of reversing:* low. The methods map one to one, and the glue is one file (`glue.rs`).
- **The crate's name and version.** *Fork:* the workspace version with the interface in build metadata (`2.0.0+knobas-adapter.1.3.0`), or the interface version itself. *Ruling:* `knobas-adapter-sdk`, `version = "1.3.0"`, the WIT package's. A test holds the version to `wit/adapter.wit`'s `package` line. *Reasoning:* the ticket asks for "the crate's version names the interface version it targets". Cargo ignores build metadata when it resolves a dependency, so an author could not ask for `^1.3` with it. The release step bumps `version.workspace` crates only, so this crate's version moves only with the WIT. *Cost of reversing:* one line, plus the test.
- **Where the WIT lives.** *Fork:* move `adapter.wit` into the SDK, copy it there, or have the SDK read the host's file. *Ruling:* it stays in `crates/knobas-wasm-host/wit/`, and the SDK's `generate!` reads it as `../knobas-wasm-host/wit`. *Reasoning:* moving it changes the frozen file's path in every §10.8 entry that names it, and a copy can drift. A git dependency on the repository checks out the whole tree, so the relative path resolves for an author too. The crate is not publishable to crates.io as it stands, and the workspace is `UNLICENSED` anyway. *Cost of reversing:* a move and two paths, when the standard is published.
- **The fixture's 1.0.0 build.** *Fork:* keep hand-written 1.0.0 bindings in the fixture beside the SDK, or let the SDK build against 1.0.0. *Ruling:* the SDK's `v1_0` feature, with `wit-1.0.0/` moved into the SDK unchanged. Under it, `Adapter` has no `translate_query` or `download` and `Sink::walked` reports nothing. *Reasoning:* the battery holds the host to the 1.0.0 component as well, and the ticket asks for the fixture to be built on the SDK. Two copies of the glue would be the hand-written conversions the ticket removes. The feature's doc says an adapter has no use for it. *Cost of reversing:* low.
- **The fixture's reads stay JSON.** *Fork:* rewrite `builds.rs` and the views as typed SPI values, or decode the JSON literals into the SPI types. *Ruling:* decode, with one helper (`decoded`) that panics on a literal that does not decode. *Reasoning:* the bytes the battery and the app's external-adapter tests hold stay the same. The decode is not a WIT conversion, and a typed rewrite of about 250 lines would change no behaviour. *Cost of reversing:* that rewrite.
- **A config that is not JSON.** *Fork:* hand `Instance::config` over as text, or as a `serde_json::Value`, and what a text that does not parse becomes. *Ruling:* a `Value`, and `null` for text that does not parse. *Reasoning:* the host writes the config from a `serde_json::Value`, so the case cannot arise from a knobas host, and every adapter reads its config as a value first. *Cost of reversing:* low.
- **What the battery cannot see** (a check). The mutant that makes `Sink::item` swallow the host's error survives the host battery, because the host remembers a refused item and fails the sync itself (#1198's `swallow_sink` hold). The SDK's unit test `a_sink_error_returned_as_it_came_reaches_the_host_unchanged` covers the conversion. Nothing that runs natively can call the import.

### #2028 review rulings (merge-manager, Opus, 2026-10-24, PR #2037)

- **A sink's refusal reaches the adapter, and now a test sees it.** *Fork:* leave `Sink::item`'s error unwitnessed, since the host's hold masks it, or witness it where the host does not mask it. *Ruling:* the SDK hands it to the adapter (as it did), and the fixture logs every refusal a sink answers at `warn` before it returns or swallows it. `host::the_component_hears_the_sink_s_refusal_of_an_item` and `reads::the_component_hears_the_sink_s_refusal_of_a_download` read that line, so the mutants that make `Sink::item` or `DownloadSink::write` drop the host's error now fail. *Reasoning:* an author wants the error: it stops the walk and the network reads behind it, and `?` returns it as it came. The host failing the call whatever the guest answers is right for the engine, but it leaves the guest half untested; the component's log is the one channel the host does not override. `DownloadSink::write` had the same unwitnessed shape, so the class is fixed, not the instance. *Cost of reversing:* the helper and two tests.
- **The relative WIT path for a git dependent.** *Fork:* a doc note, or a test that builds an adapter outside the repository against the SDK by git. *Ruling:* a doc note in the crate doc, and the build witnessed once by hand: a `cdylib` crate in a scratch directory with `knobas-adapter-sdk = { git = "file:///Users/dev/Projects/knobas", rev = "11e1ceb7" }`, the repository's toolchain file and lockfile, built for `wasm32-wasip2` in 22 s with no other dependency. *Reasoning:* the path resolves for the reason the implementer gave (a git checkout is the whole tree); the export macro from another crate is already witnessed on every gate by the fixture, which has no `wit-bindgen` of its own. A test over a git dependency needs a committed revision and a registry the build may not reach offline, so it cannot run on a working tree under the gate. The note also says the dependency must keep the crate's name, since `runtime_path` names `knobas_adapter_sdk`. #2033 names the dependency line an author writes, so the automated build belongs with it if it wants one. *Cost of reversing:* a `just` recipe that does what the hand check did.
- **The moved 1.0.0 world is the same file.** *Check:* `crates/knobas-adapter-sdk/wit-1.0.0/adapter.wit` is blob `ad3a95b8`, the blob `crates/knobas-wasm-fixture/wit-1.0.0/adapter.wit` had on `main`, and git records a 100 % rename. Nothing else in the tree named the old path.
- **The `generate!` options and the blanket `Guest` impls stand.** *Check:* `pub_export_macro` with `export_macro_name` makes `export_world!` reachable as `$crate::bindings::export_world`; `runtime_path` through `__private` lets the expansion resolve `wit_bindgen::rt` in a crate that does not depend on `wit-bindgen`; `extern crate self` makes the same paths resolve inside the SDK. The three blanket impls (`source`, `query`, `downloads`) are of the SDK's own traits, so coherence holds, and `Adapter: Sized + 'static` gives the resource rep what wit-bindgen asks.

## #2031: an external adapter's install and update are shown, then confirmed (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **A check-only command or a dry run on `install_adapter`.** *Fork:* the ticket leaves it to the implementer. *Ruling:* two check-only commands, `preview_install_adapter(manifest)` and `preview_update_adapter(kind)`, each answering a new DTO; `install_adapter` and `update_adapter` keep their answers. *Reasoning:* a dry-run flag would give one command two answer shapes. The update needs a preview too, and its answer has to carry what is installed beside the release, which no install answer holds. §10.8 entry `2031-an-adapter-install-and-update-are-shown-then-confirmed.md`. *Reversing:* two commands and three DTOs.
- **The confirm is held to what was shown.** *Fork:* install whatever the release is when *Install* is pressed, or hold the install to the preview. *Ruling:* held. `install_adapter` and `update_adapter` take the hash the preview answered, and refuse another (`invalid`). Nothing is written. (The merge-manager widened the hash from the artifact's to `confirm_sha256`, below.) *Reasoning:* "latest release" and a local manifest can both move between the preview and the press, and story 21 is about deciding to trust the code that lands. Without the pin, the reader could confirm one artifact and get another. *Reversing:* the argument and one check.
- **Which updates ask.** *Fork:* the ticket body says an update "whose hosts or roles differ" shows what changed, and the criterion says one that "widens". *Ruling:* any difference in hosts, role names or limits opens *Update <name> to <release>?*. A release that asks for the same as the installed one switches at once after its check, as *Update* did before. A change in a claim's reads only is not a difference. *Reasoning:* a narrowing is a change the reader may want to know about before it switches. A memory or deadline limit that moves changes what the adapter may do on the machine. The reads a role names are about the shell's surfaces, not about trust. *Reversing:* the `updateChanges` rules in `tf/settings/adapter-preview.ts`.
- **How install is drawn.** *Fork:* prototype-6 draws no install. Options were an inline step in *Add a source* or a dialog over it. *Ruling:* the field's button reads *Install…* (*Checking…*, then *Installing…*) and opens *Install <name>?* over *Add a source*, with *Cancel* and *Install*. It shows Version (version · tag or *no release*), From, Roles, Hosts and Limits in the `tf-facts` list, and the line *It runs with no disk and no keychain. Nothing is installed until you press Install.* A refusal stays the note under the field and opens nothing. *Reasoning:* the same shape as *Uninstall…* and *Uninstall <name>?* on the same page. A dialog keeps the *Add a source* draft as it was, and its *Cancel* means what *Cancel* means everywhere. The sandbox line is ADR-0028's own guarantee. *Reversing:* one component.
- **Copy no design names** (the ticket asks for prototype-6's words, and it has none here). *Ruling:* the words above, the update dialog's *This release changes what <name> may do:* list (*It may newly reach …*, *It no longer reaches …*, *It newly claims …*, *It no longer claims …*, *Each call may take …, was …*, *Each call may use … MiB of memory, was … MiB.*), *<name> stays on <release> until you press Update.*, and the limits line *<deadline> per call (asked for|the default), <n> MiB of memory (asked for|the default)*. The deadline is spelt by `secondsLabel`, as a run's length is. Roles use `roleWord`: a built-in role in the shell's words, a custom role by its full name, as the health line names it. Hosts use the install note's words, now `adapter-preview.ts`'s `reach`. *Reversing:* strings in one module.
- **A refused update preview is recorded.** *Fork:* record the refusal on the row only when `update_adapter` runs, or already at the preview. *Ruling:* at the preview. It records the same `refused` or `failed` check that `update_adapter` would. *Reasoning:* after this change, a release the checks refuse never reaches `update_adapter`, so the row's *Update to … refused, still on …* line would otherwise never be drawn. *Reversing:* one call.
- **Interface version not drawn.** *Fork:* add it to the facts or leave it out. *Ruling:* left out. *Reasoning:* the ticket lists name, version, roles, hosts and limits. A version this knobas cannot host is refused before the preview, so the reader has no decision to make about it. *Reversing:* one row.
- **Seams.** *Fork:* the TDD skill asks the user to confirm seams, and none is there. *Ruling:* the IPC seam (`sources::install` and `sources::installed`, the commands' bodies, with the fixture component and the local forge) for "nothing written" and the pin. *Settings* through its ports (`TfSettings.test.svelte.ts`) for the dialogs. The pure module for the words. *Reasoning:* the brief's seams for this area, as #1202 and #1209 used them. *Reversing:* n/a.

### #2031, merge-manager (Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **The pin covers the manifest's hosts and limits.** *Fork:* hold the confirm to the artifact's hash, as the branch did, or to everything the reader was shown. *Ruling:* to `confirm_sha256`, a SHA-256 over `[artifact_sha256, hosts, limits]`, which the preview answers and `install_adapter` and `update_adapter` take as `sha256`; a release it does not match is `InstallError::ReleaseChanged` (`invalid`). *Reasoning:* the hosts and limits live in the manifest, not in the artifact, so a manifest rewritten between the preview and the press (a local file, or a release re-published under its tag) around the same artifact installed a host the reader never saw, and an update with no visible difference switched to it without a dialog. Story 21 is about exactly that list. The kind, the versions and the roles need no place in the hash: the static checks hold the manifest's kind and version to the artifact's descriptor, and the roles are the descriptor's. *Cost of reversing:* one function and one field.
- **Which updates ask, and narrowings shown.** *Check:* the implementer's ruling stands. The criterion's "widens" is a floor; asking on any difference in hosts, role names or limits, and naming a narrowing as one, never hides a widening. A release that differs only in its code switches without a dialog, as the ticket asks (hosts or roles), and the switch is still held to the checked release.
- **The dialog copy stands.** *Check:* *Install <name>?* and *Update <name> to <release>?* have the shape of *Uninstall <name>?* beside them, the buttons are *Cancel* and the verb, *Checking…* and *Installing…* end in an ellipsis as the shell's other running labels do (*Cloning…*), and *It runs with no disk and no keychain* is ADR-0028's own sentence. The convention line now also says when an update asks, which the first wording left out.
## #2034: Forgejo's commit listing ignores `since=` and `until=` (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **Which date Forgejo's `until=` reads.** *Fork:* the test is wrong, or the adapter is. *Ruling:* both. Forgejo 17.0.0 does not filter on `since=` or `until=` at all, so the test's assumption is Gitea's alone, and the adapter had a bug on it. *Reasoning:* measured against both pinned containers on `tidewater/payout-service` main. Gitea 1.27.3 answers `until=` and `since=` inclusively on `created`. Forgejo (`17.0.0+gitea-1.22.0`) answers both commits for every `since=` and `until=` it was asked. The sources agree: Forgejo v17.0.0's `GetAllCommits` declares no `since` or `until` and calls `CommitsByRange(page, pageSize, not)`, while Gitea v1.27.3 passes both to `git log --since/--until`, and its `created` is `Committer.When`. The adapter already dropped commits outside the window client-side, so the result stays correct. The page cap was where it broke: a catch-up re-reads from the head everything it delivered above its window, and once that fills `MAX_COMMIT_PAGES` the leg stops having examined nothing, resumes where it began, and the commit mirror stands still on every later run. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **How a catch-up reads past the cap.** *Fork:* a page hint in the cursor, as `pulls_catching_up.page` has, or read on in the same run. *Ruling:* read on. A walk capped while its last page held commits above the window that the leg had not met before opens another walk at the next page. *Reasoning:* the cursor stays as it is. The "new to the leg" condition keeps a server that repeats its first page stopping at the cap as before (`a_commit_catch_up_over_a_server_that_repeats_its_first_page_stops_at_the_cap`). The cost is that on Forgejo each catch-up run re-reads what the catch-up delivered before it, which grows with the catch-up's depth. A hint would remove that, but it changes the cursor. The live witness is `a_commit_catch_up_reads_past_a_page_cap_of_commits_the_server_lists_above_it`, which pushes 1,100 commits to a scratch repository. *Reversing:* one match arm, a closure and the per-leg set of commits above the window.
- **How the live test tells the forges apart.** *Fork:* an environment variable from the recipe, or the server's own answer. *Ruling:* `GET /api/v1/version`. Forgejo reports `17.0.0+gitea-1.22.0`, Gitea a bare `1.27.3`. *Reasoning:* the server decides, so a run pointed at the wrong forge cannot pass by the variable it was given. *Reversing:* one line.
- **Where the Forgejo run is written down.** *Fork:* the implementer brief or the recipe's comment. *Ruling:* both, one line each. *Reasoning:* the brief is what an implementer reads, and the recipe comment is what a reader of `just gitea-live` sees. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Test seams.** *Fork:* confirm them with Björn, as the TDD skill asks, or pick them. *Ruling:* picked: `Source::sync` over `sync_moving`'s fake, with an `ignores_bounds` mode standing for Forgejo, and the live listing itself. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. The fake's mode is a claim about Forgejo, and the live run checked that claim. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **The read past the cap holds** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* uphold the `Capped if passing_above` arm, or bound it further. *Ruling:* upheld as it is. *Reasoning:* the arm needs an upper bound (`passing_above` is only set by a commit above `window.upper`), so a full sync and every leg walked from its head take the old path, and on Gitea, where `until=` holds, only the boundary second's commits are ever above the window and they sit on the first page, not the twentieth. Each further walk needs the last page to hold a commit above the window the leg has not met, so the walks per leg are bounded by the branch's history: a server that repeats page 1, or one that answers its last page for every page past the end, stops at the next cap. A push of 50 or more commits between two page reads can make page 20 repeat page 19 on Forgejo; that run stops as before and the next continues, so it costs a run, never a stall. A force-push that re-dates the branch makes every commit "above"; the leg then reads the branch to its end and finishes, as Gitea's `until=` would have it. An empty repository returns before any walk (`repo.empty`). *Reversing:* one match arm.
- **The cost on Forgejo goes to the backlog** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* fix the re-read in this PR, or file it. *Ruling:* #2039, `backlog`, as the implementer filed it; its body named the arm by its draft name `overhead` and now says `passing_above`. *Reasoning:* the fix it names is a page hint in `CommitsCatchUp`, a cursor change on the frozen surface the fit test keeps out of a passing fix, and the cost only arises on Forgejo after a single push larger than `commits_per_repo`. A stall for good is a wrong mirror; a re-read is a slower right one. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **The Forgejo-run rule covers every `gitea-live` run** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* keep the implementer's "a test you add or change", or the whole class. *Ruling:* the class: whenever an implementer runs `just gitea-live`, it runs `just gitea-live forgejo` once as well, in `docs/agents/implementer-brief.md` (*Live suites*) and the recipe's comment. *Reasoning:* the cause is that no gate runs the Forgejo form, and the adapter stall this PR fixes was code under a test, not a new test; an implementer runs `gitea-live` only when its change exercises it, so the rule costs one Forgejo run (174 s here) exactly where it can find something. The brief's own *Live suites* bullet is the line an implementer reads before a live run, and the ticket asked for the line there, so it lands in this PR rather than a docs-only one. *Reversing:* one sentence.
- **The deep catch-up test cleans up by name, not by `Litter`** (merge-manager, Opus) *Fork:* a `Drop` guard for the scratch repository, or remove it before and after. *Ruling:* before and after, as `repositories_gitea_refuses_pull_requests_for_do_not_end_a_full_sync` does. *Reasoning:* the removal at the end runs before the assertions, so only a panic in the setup or the sync itself skips it, and the next run's removal at the start clears that. The live suites take the Gitea lock and run with one thread, so nothing else sees the repository while it stands. *Reversing:* a guard struct.
- **Overlap with #2030 (PR #2043)** (merge-manager, Opus) *Ruling:* no shared code; one textual conflict. *Reasoning:* `git merge-tree` of this head with #2043's (8568ba08) conflicts only in `docs/contract.md`, where this PR edits §4.2's Gitea read-endpoints row and #2043 the write-endpoints row beneath it; the PR merged second keeps both rows. `live_gitea.rs`, the rulings file and `test-inventory.txt` merge cleanly. *Reversing:* n/a.
## #2030: writes a source's credential cannot make are drawn enabled (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)
## #2030: Gitea's views draw the writes its token cannot make disabled, saying why (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **How Gitea is asked what the token may write.** *Fork:* the repository's `permissions`, the token's scopes, or a probe. *Ruling:* a probe. A view that offers writes sends `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/branches` and `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues` with the body `{}`, once each and only for the scope categories its writes fall in. Gitea refuses each for the scope (403 `token does not have at least one of required scope(s)`) or for the body (422), and changes nothing. *Reasoning:* `permissions` describe the account, not the token: a `read:repository` token of the admin reads `{"admin":true,"push":true,"pull":true}` (measured on Gitea 1.27.3). Gitea's token listing takes basic auth, so a token cannot read its own scopes. Gitea checks the scope of a route's category before it reads the body, so an empty body is refused for the scope or for itself. Measured on Gitea and witnessed on Forgejo by `a_token_that_may_only_read_is_offered_its_writes_disabled_saying_why`. *Reversing:* `crates/knobas-source-gitea/src/view/grants.rs`.
- **When it is asked.** *Fork:* at test-connection or sync, as the ticket suggests, or when a view is drawn. *Ruling:* when a view is drawn, after the view knows which writes it offers. *Reasoning:* an answer kept from a sync would need a column (a migration) and would go stale when the token is replaced. A view is live already (ADR-0020 rule 1). The cost is one round trip after the draw, and one or two requests, for a view that offers writes; a view with no writes asks nothing. No cache: the adapter is built for each call. *Reversing:* the call in `view::draw`.
- **Disabled or absent.** *Fork:* per op, as the ticket leaves it. *Ruling:* every refused write is drawn disabled with the reason. A diff's line comments (`Commenting` carries no reason) are left out, and the review actions beside them say why. *Reasoning:* a token can be replaced and an account can be given push, so the reader can reach the state where the write is enabled (ADR-0020 rule 4, the #701 ruling). *Reversing:* `SourceView::refuse_writes`.
- **The token's reason replaces the adapter's.** *Fork:* keep a reason the adapter drew (a mirror, a conflict), or replace it. *Ruling:* replace. *Reasoning:* whatever else the reader fixes, the token still cannot make the write. *Reversing:* one condition in `refuse_writes`.
- **The wording.** *Fork:* the ticket's *This token cannot write: it has read:repository only*, or the scope it lacks. *Ruling:* *This token cannot write: it lacks the write:repository scope* (or `write:issue`). *Reasoning:* the scope it lacks is what a new token must have. `knobas-http` reads the scope refusal as `Unauthorized`, which carries no message, so the token's own scopes would need a change to the HTTP crate. *Reversing:* `grants::reason`.
- **An account that may not push.** *Fork:* leave it to the ticket's token case, or read the branch probe's other 403 too. *Ruling:* read it, for the writes that push only (`create_branch`, `delete_branch`, `commit_file`, `merge_pull_request`): *This account cannot push to this repository*. The issue probe's other 403s are no verdict. *Reasoning:* measured with a seeded person's write-scoped token on the admin's public mirror: the branch probe answers 403 *user should have a permission to write to a repo*, and the issue probe 422. A reader may still comment and review, so nothing else is disabled. *Reversing:* `grants::pushes`.
- **The Code page's header and compare page.** *Fork:* leave *New branch…* and *Create pull request* as the shell draws them, or take the source's answer. *Ruling:* the header reads the repository's whole view for its toolbar's `create_branch`. The compare page takes the branch view's `create_pull_request` reason it already reads. *Reasoning:* both were drawn enabled whatever the source said: the header's *New branch…* on a mirror too, which the repository's toolbar draws disabled. It costs one more view read per repository page. The compare page now also disables *Create pull request* for a branch with *No commits ahead of main*, which is the source's answer for the same action. *Reversing:* `TfRepo.svelte`, `TfRepoCompare.svelte`.
- **The other adapters.** *Fork:* fix each here, or list it. *Ruling:* listed in #2040. *Reasoning:* outside Gitea's views a write is drawn from the template `write_ops` by a shell surface (the inbox, the ticket detail, stand-up, time), so the fix needs an answer per instance, with a reason, across IPC: a §10.8 entry. TeamCity's own views need its permissions read, and no TeamCity write is safe as a probe: `POST /app/rest/buildQueue` with a build type queues a build (measured; the build the probe queued, and the one TeamCity re-added when it stopped, were deleted and `Ledger_Deploy_Staging`'s counter put back to 523). Kuma has no cause. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **A pull request's view for a `read:repository`-only token.** *Fork:* fix it here, or file it. *Ruling:* filed as #2042. *Reasoning:* it is a read lost to a narrower read scope, not a write drawn enabled, and it changes what the *Conversation* tab draws. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Test seams.** *Fork:* confirm the seams with Björn, as the TDD skill asks, or pick them. *Ruling:* picked: `SourceView::refuse_writes` (unit), Gitea's `Source::view` over the wiremock fake, the mounted repository page, and `live_gitea` on both forges. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Merge-manager review (Opus, 2026-10-24).**
  - **The empty-body probe is safe to send to a reader's server.** *Fork:* keep the probe, or fall back to drawing writes enabled. *Ruling:* keep it. *Reasoning:* read in the source of Gitea 1.19, 1.21, 1.24 and `main` and of Forgejo's `forgejo` branch: `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/branches` and `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues` run `bind(api.CreateBranchRepoOption{})` and `bind(api.CreateIssueOption{})` before `repo.CreateBranch` and `repo.CreateIssue`. `bind` answers 422 and stops the chain on a failed validation, and `new_branch_name` and `title` are `binding:"Required"` in every one of those versions. Everything ahead of `bind` only checks (the scope, `reqToken`, `reqRepoWriter`, `mustNotBeArchived`, `repoAssignment`). Forgejo's quota check sits after `bind`. Webhooks and notifications fire from the handlers, which a refused body never reaches. Gitea `main`'s new audit log (`services/audit`) records through the same notifier (`NewIssue`, `NewPullRequest`, …) plus account events, and has no entry for a refused request. Neither forge rate-limits its own API. A token has no scopes before 1.19, so there the probe reads 422 or the account's 403. A proxy's or WAF's 403 page reads as the scope refusal (`client::forbidden_refusal` reads a body that is not Gitea's envelope as the token's). The write is then drawn disabled with the scope reason, and the same proxy would refuse the write itself. `live_gitea` now counts both repositories' branches, issues and pull requests around the probes, on both forges. *Cost of reversing:* drop the `grants::narrow` call in `view::draw`.
  - **A probe on every draw, no cache.** *Fork:* keep the per-draw probe, or keep the token's scope answer per token for the process, as `GiteaSource::viewer` keeps the login. *Ruling:* per draw. *Reasoning:* at most two requests on a view that already makes five to twenty, and they go through the client's limiter like the reads. A process-wide cache would keep a proxy's passing 403 page as the token's scope until restart. *Cost of reversing:* a map beside `viewers()`, keyed on `viewer_key` and the category.
  - **The Code page's extra whole repository view.** *Fork:* keep the read, or take *New branch…*'s answer from something lighter. *Ruling:* keep it. *Reasoning:* only a whole view carries the toolbar, and the button must be drawn disabled before it is pressed (criterion 1). The read is the one the repository's detail makes when it opens, once per Code page opening and not per tab. A failed read leaves the button as before. *Cost of reversing:* the one `entityView(id, null)` in `TfRepo.svelte`.
  - **#2042 is in v3, not folded.** *Fork:* v3 or outside it, fold or file. *Ruling:* v3, a native blocker of #2027, and left as its own ticket. *Reasoning:* story 10 says a read-only Forgejo token "still gives me Code", and a pull request's view falling back to the mirror breaks that. Folding it takes a degraded discussion read with new *Conversation* tab copy, a check of the sync's discussion read and a live witness on both forges. That is past the fit test's 100 lines, and the copy is Björn's to judge. *Cost of reversing:* the milestone and the blocker link.
  - **#2040 is outside v3.** *Fork:* v3 or outside it. *Ruling:* outside, no milestone. *Reasoning:* story 10 names a read-only Forgejo token in Code, and #2030 covers that with #2042. #2040 covers the other adapters and the shell surfaces (inbox, ticket detail, stand-up, time, docs). It needs an answer per instance across IPC (a §10.8 entry) and TeamCity's permissions read: new work, not a gap in v3's stories. *Cost of reversing:* set the milestone.
  - **Rebase against #2041 (#2034).** *Check:* a trial merge of #2041's head into this one conflicts only in `docs/contract.md`. #2041 edits the Gitea *read endpoints* row and this PR edits the *write endpoints* row below it. The resolution keeps both rows as each PR wrote them. `live_gitea.rs`, `test-inventory.txt` and this file merge cleanly. #2041's `client.rs` change is a doc comment on `commits`. Nothing else overlaps.
## #2032: saved views name their ticket system, not Jira (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **Where the shell gets the name.** *Fork:* read it off the group (`Jira boards` less ` boards`), work it out in the shell from the source list and the adapter registry, or have the backend send it. *Ruling:* the backend sends it, as `SavedViewSource.system` (§10.8 entry `2032-…`), by the same `knobas_sync::saved_views::declared` that names the group. *Reasoning:* the ticket rules out telling a synced group by its name, and taking the system out of the group's name is the same reading of a string. Working it out in the shell would be a second copy of `declared`'s rule, which needs the source's adapter kind and a loaded registry on every row. The row already comes from the backend, and the backend already has the registry. *Cost of reversing:* one field and its mirror.
- **When the adapter is gone.** *Fork:* what `system` is for a source whose adapter is not compiled in or declares no saved views. *Ruling:* the source's display name, else its id. *Reasoning:* such a view is not live (its source cannot sync), so this is rarely seen, and the reader's name for the source is the best word left. *Cost of reversing:* one `map_or`.
- **What makes a group synced, and where it sits.** *Fork:* a group is synced when all its views come from a source, when any does, or when its first does. Where several systems' groups go. *Ruling:* when any view in it has a `saved_view_source`. Synced groups come after every group of your own, one ticket system at a time in the order its first view sits, boards before filters. *Reasoning:* "any" keeps today's drawing for a reader who typed a synced group's name on a view of their own. Sorting by system keeps each system's boards and filters together, and boards before filters is the order prototype-6 and #878 drew for Jira. *Cost of reversing:* the sort in `groupViews`.
- **Copy with no ticket system, or with two.** *Fork:* prototype-6 has one sentence, naming Jira, for the list's foot and for a view of your own. *Ruling:* with one system, prototype-6's words with its name filled in. With two or more, the names are joined (*the Jira and Kestrel sources*, *Jira and Kestrel never see it*). With none, *A ticket system's boards and favourite filters come in at every sync.* and *Kept in knobas. No source sees it.* *Reasoning:* the systems are the ones the listed saved views come from (`savedViewSystems`), so with no saved view there is nothing to name, and *Jira* would be wrong for a reader without Jira. Two own-view tests whose harness has no saved view now expect *No source sees it.*; every test with a Jira view expects the same words as before. *Cost of reversing:* two branches in the markup.
- **Boards and filters' name.** *Fork:* the source's views' `system`, or the adapter's declaration. *Ruling:* the declaration, `savedViewSystem` in `tf/settings/boards.ts`, restating `declared`. *Reasoning:* the section is drawn for an adapter whose schema declares it, before any view has synced. Its words ("The next Jira sync…") need a name even then, and the page already holds the descriptor. The fake Jira adapter now declares `jira_view` with `system_name: "Jira"`, as the real one does, so the fake page still reads *Jira* and not *Jira Data Center*. *Cost of reversing:* one prop.
- **The fake second ticket system.** *Fork:* give the fake Gitea a saved view, or add a source. *Ruling:* a source and an adapter of a made-up system, Kestrel (`kestrel`, *Tidewater Kestrel*), with one Kanban board *Ops triage* (the OPS tickets) under *Kestrel boards*. It claims the ticket-system role with no optional reads, so it offers no editable copy. *Reasoning:* the fake Gitea claims only what the real adapter does, and no real Gitea adapter has saved views. A made-up name makes no claim about a real tool. *Cost of reversing:* two fixture entries.
- **Seams.** *Fork:* the TDD skill asks the user to confirm seams, and none is there. *Ruling:* `ticket_views::list` for `system` (one integration test, with a source whose display name differs); `groupViews`, `savedViewSystems`, `systemsWords` and `savedViewSystem` as pure rules; `TicketsPage` and `TfSettings` mounted for the words; the house rule over the files. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. *Cost of reversing:* n/a.
- **The two no-view sentences stand** (merge-manager, Opus). *Fork:* keep *A ticket system's boards and favourite filters come in at every sync.* and *Kept in knobas. No source sees it.*, or name the ticket-system adapters a reader has before any view syncs. *Ruling:* keep them. *Reasoning:* the TF conventions let copy leave prototype-6 where the PR says why, and it does: with no saved view listed, the shell has no system to name, and *Jira* would be wrong for a reader without Jira. Both sentences keep prototype-6's shape (the foot still ends on *Choose which*; *No source sees it* stands where *Jira never sees it* stood), and both are true for every reader. Reading the adapters' declarations on Tickets would add a read the page does not make today for a case with nothing in it. *Cost of reversing:* two branches in `savedViewsFoot` and `ownViewKept`.
- **Kestrel in the fake stays** (merge-manager, Opus). *Check:* the seventh fake source reaches only `?fake-ipc`. The demo profile (`--demo`) is the real server on its own database and reads no `fake/` module; no crate `include_str!`s `fake/sources.ts` or `fake/ticket-views.ts`; no test pins the fake's source count (`fake-tauri.test.ts` counts relative to the list it reads). Kestrel claims the ticket-system role, so `fakeRoleScope("ticket-system")` now names it, and the fake Jira's `jira_view` joins that role's kinds through its saved-view frame, as `role_scope` answers on the server. *Ruling:* no change. *Cost of reversing:* two fixture entries.
## #2042: a pull request's view for a token without `read:issue` (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **Which failures of the discussion read degrade.** *Fork:* every failure, as the labels read takes any, or the scope refusal only. *Ruling:* the scope refusal only (`Unauthorized` with its 403, `knobas-http`'s reading of Gitea's scope sentence). A 5xx, a timeout or a 404 still fails the view. *Reasoning:* a scope refusal is a fact about the token that no retry changes, and the rest of the view is readable on it. Any other failure is what the view reports today, *Showing the mirror* and why, and a tab drawn without its comments over a blip would read as a quiet discussion. *Reversing:* the match in `PullView::comments`.
- **What *Conversation* draws.** *Fork:* an empty tab with the line, or the reviews under it. *Ruling:* the reviews under the line. The count is what the tab lists. *Reasoning:* Gitea serves the reviews from the pull request (`/pulls/{n}/reviews`, the `repository` category), so the token reads them. The line says comments are missing, so the reviews do not read as the whole discussion. *Reversing:* `conversation` in `view/pr.rs`.
- **The wording.** *Fork:* Gitea's own sentence, or a sentence naming the scope. *Ruling:* *This token cannot read this pull request's comments: it lacks the read:issue scope*. The labels: *This token cannot read this repository's labels: it lacks the read:issue scope*, and *This token cannot read its organisation's labels: it lacks the read:organization scope*. *Reasoning:* it follows #2030's *This token cannot write: it lacks the … scope*. `Unauthorized` carries no message, so the scope comes from the route's category (`grants::READ_ISSUE`, `grants::READ_ORGANIZATION`), the same way #2030 names a write's. *Reversing:* `grants::unread`.
- **An organisation's labels refused for the scope.** *Fork:* offer the repository's own labels and leave the organisation's out, or disable *Add label…* naming the scope. *Ruling:* disable it, naming `read:organization`. *Reasoning:* a list without the organisation's labels, with no line saying so, would look like the whole list. *Reversing:* one arm in `label::read`.
- **Whose reason *Add label…* gives on a token that may not write issues.** *Fork:* the read's or the probe's. *Ruling:* the probe's, *This token cannot write: it lacks the write:issue scope*, as #2030 rules (the token's reason replaces the adapter's). *Reasoning:* `write:issue` includes `read:issue` in Gitea, so a token refused the labels read for `read:issue` is refused the write too, and the write scope is the one a new token needs. The read reason shows only where the probe gives no verdict. The live test asserts the probe's reason. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **The sync's discussion read.** *Fork:* change it, or check it. *Ruling:* no change. `sync::discussion` already reads a 403 as repository-scoped (`client::is_repo_scoped`), warns, and mirrors the pull request without its discussion. The issue listing's 403 is skipped the same way. *Reasoning:* witnessed by a full sync on a token minted with `read:repository` and `read:user` in `a_token_that_may_not_read_issues_reads_every_view_but_the_discussion`, on Gitea and Forgejo. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **The sweep.** *Fork:* fix the discussion read alone, or every view read a scope can refuse. *Ruling:* every one; only the discussion read failed a view. Every read a Gitea view makes, grouped by Gitea's scope category: `issue` covers the discussion (fixed here) and the repository's labels (they already degraded, and now name the scope). `organization` covers the organisation's labels (same). `user` covers `GET /user` for the viewer (`GiteaSource::viewer`, already `None` on any failure). Every other read is `repository`: the repository, its contents and README, branches, compares, commits, a commit's diff, pulls, a pull request's reviews, its review comments, its diff and commits, statuses, and branch protections (already `unless_refused`). The live test reads every view and the PR's tabs on a `read:repository` token and compares them with the seed's token. `reachable_transitions` reads an issue, but only for a ticket, which this token never mirrors (its issue listing is refused too). *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Test seams.** *Fork:* confirm them with Björn, as the TDD skill asks, or pick them. *Ruling:* picked: Gitea's `Source::view` over the wiremock fake, and `live_gitea` on both forges. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **An organisation's labels that fail otherwise** (fixed in passing). *Fork:* keep the reason *Could not read this repository's labels* for a failed organisation read, or name the organisation's. *Ruling:* name them: *Could not read its organisation's labels: …*. *Reasoning:* the repository's labels were read; the reason named the wrong read. *Reversing:* the fallback in `label::read`.
- **A proxy's 403 on the discussion read** (merge-manager, Opus). *Fork:* tell a proxy's 403 from Gitea's scope sentence before degrading, or degrade on both. *Ruling:* both degrade, and the doc on `grants::is_scope_refusal` now says so. *Reasoning:* `forbidden_refusal` keeps a 403 without Gitea's envelope as `Unauthorized`, the conservative guess #722 rules for writes, and `Unauthorized` carries no message, so the two can only be told apart by a change to `client.rs`'s reading or to `SourceError`, which #722 and the frozen contract hold. #2030's probe already reads that 403 as a scope refusal. A proxy that refuses only `/issues/` routes would get a *Conversation* line naming the wrong cause over the reviews. Before this PR it got *Showing the mirror* for the whole view. Every 403 carrying another Gitea sentence (a permission refusal) still fails the view, as `a_discussion_gitea_fails_to_serve_fails_the_view` pins. Gitea and Forgejo send the same scope sentence on the versions the live suites pin (the live premise asserts it on both). An older Gitea whose sentence lacks it gets the view failing as before, never a wrong line. *Cost of reversing:* a message on the reading in `client.rs`, and its tests.
- **The live suites after `20644ee5`** (merge-manager, Opus). *Check:* from `git diff 20644ee5 94af7128`, every change after the live runs is a move (`muted_line` to `view/rows.rs`, `is_scope_refusal` pulled out of `unread` and `refusal_of` unchanged in behaviour), a fake test, docs, or the fallback *Could not read its organisation's labels*, which no live test asserts (`live_gitea.rs` asserts only the scope sentence at its line 6463). *Ruling:* the claim holds; the live suites were not run again.
- **The seed token a `just gitea-live forgejo` run leaves in Forgejo** (merge-manager, Opus). *Fork:* delete the seed token when the recipe stops Forgejo, or keep it. *Ruling:* keep it. *Reasoning:* `seed-forgejo.sh` is `seed-gitea.sh` pointed at Forgejo, so the token is the worktree's seed state under #684's rule: minted once under the worktree's own name, recorded in its `seed-state-forgejo.json`, and reused while it authenticates. A teardown delete would leave that file holding a dead token between runs (`./seed --env-forgejo` would print it, #1377's class) and re-mint on every run, and it would make Forgejo's lifecycle differ from Gitea's, whose token stays because Gitea stays up. What outlives its owner is one token per worktree that ever seeded, on both forges (49 on the shared Gitea today, all on one page of its listing). These are localhost test containers, and `gitea_seed_token` already reads every page. The live suite's own tokens (`knobas-live-2042-*`) are deleted before it asserts and again at the next run's start; none is left on Gitea. *Cost of reversing:* a delete step in `live_session`'s teardown for `forgejo`.
## #2035 and #2036: `check.yml` red on ubuntu, whole-tree guards and shellcheck (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **Which shellcheck side moves.** *Fork:* pin the runner to the Mac's 0.11.0, or the Mac to the runner's 0.9.0. *Ruling:* the runner moves up to 0.11.0. *Reasoning:* Homebrew ships only the current release, so a Mac cannot hold 0.9.0 without a hand-built binary. 0.11.0 is the newer parser, and it splits the indirect-call case out of SC2317 into SC2329, which is the false positive the runner raised on `desktop-witness-test.sh:1031`. The recipe's docker fallback already named `koalaman/shellcheck:v0.11.0`. *Reversing:* one line, `shellcheck_version` in the justfile.
- **How the runner gets the pinned version.** *Fork:* an install step in each workflow, or the recipe enforcing the version. *Ruling:* the recipe. `just shell` runs a local binary only when `shellcheck --version` says `shellcheck_version`; otherwise it runs the pinned image, and with neither it stops and names both versions. `testenv.yml` runs `just shell` in place of its own copy of the discovery. *Reasoning:* the version is then named once, `check.yml` still restates nothing of the gate, and a Mac whose `brew upgrade` moves ahead gets the image or a message rather than silent drift. Both runs on the branch pulled the image in about a second (testenv 40124504405, check 40124502573). *Reversing:* a few lines in the recipe.
- **The scripts.** *Fork:* change the lines 0.9.0 flagged, or only what the pinned version reports. *Ruling:* only what 0.11.0 reports, which is nothing. The three `SC2015` disables from #1713, whose comments said 0.9.0 flags the line and 0.11.0 does not, are removed. *Reasoning:* a disable or a rewrite for a version no gate runs is noise. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Faster, a bigger budget, or both.** *Fork:* the dispatch prefers fast guards to a raised timeout. *Ruling:* both. `browser-globals` asks the checker only about candidates (a confusing name that is not a member or a key), gives it only the files that have one, and parses the lib files once for both its programs. `nullish-fallback` leaves the tests out of its roots as well as its walk. Each whole-tree guard's timeout is then `wholeTreeBudget()` (`app/src/lib/shell/test-budget.ts`): the machine's test timeout (below) plus 100 ms per `.ts` and `.svelte` file under `app/src`, 69.5 s on the Mac today. *Reasoning:* the cheaper scans cut the work (below), but a type-checking scan still grows with the tree, and the runner's speed moved 1.6 times between runs on the same day. A per-file budget keeps the pass off the tree's size, and a guard that hangs still fails. *Reversing:* one module and two call sites.
- **A test timeout for the machine (#2044, folded in).** *Fork:* the branch's second run went red on two launcher-chain tests at 15 s, the class filed as #2044: fix it here, or per test, or leave it. *Ruling:* here. `testTimeout` is `TEST_TIMEOUT_MS`: 15 s times eight over the core count, never less than 15 s. Eight is the threads `just check` runs at once, four vitest workers beside four rustc jobs. The Mac keeps 15 s, and the two-core runner gets 60 s. `hookTimeout` scales the same way from Vitest's 10 s, after `test-setup.ts`'s `afterEach(resetStores)` passed 10 s on the runner (40130991453). The TfCode 1,200-row test's own 60 s, added on the way, is dropped as covered. *Reasoning:* one rule for every test, set by the machine rather than by being CI, so `check.yml` still restates nothing. Per-test budgets would chase the next test to cross. The slowest unit tests measured on the runner took 11 to 17 s, a quarter of the new budget. *Reversing:* one constant.
- **Which tests are the class.** *Fork:* every test that walks `app/src`, or the two that type-check it. *Ruling:* the two. *Reasoning:* the regex walkers (`house-rules`, `a11y`, `test-suffix`, `test-resets`, the `fake-seed` scan) read the files and match text, and none took more than 2.3 s on the runner (house-rules' dev-harness test, 2.2 s in 40124502573). One walk shared between test files is not possible anyway: vitest isolates each file's modules. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **One program for both guards.** *Fork:* share a program, or keep two. *Ruling:* two. *Reasoning:* they read different trees. `browser-globals` reads tests too, `.svelte` script blocks only, with `lib` and `noResolve`. `nullish-fallback` reads the app under `tsconfig.json` with svelte2tsx. Sharing would mean merging the two files and changing what each guard sees. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Siblings that kept the run red (fixed in passing).** *Fork:* fix them here, or file them. *Ruling:* fixed. `merge-tail-lock-test.sh` initialised its bare origin with git's default branch, which is `master` on ubuntu-latest, so three `gated` checks failed there (hidden on main behind the shellcheck failure). `check.yml`'s timeout goes from 30 to 60 minutes: the cargo half took 12 minutes on the last green run, 26 on main's red one, was cut off at 30 on the branch's first run and took 40 on its second (rust-cache saves only from a green run). *Reasoning:* each blocks the green Linux run the PR needs, and each is a few lines. *Reversing:* one line each.

## Björn's #2035 ruling in the standing texts (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **The milestone reviewer's Linux run.** *Fork:* drop the step, or replace it. *Ruling:* replace it with one `just check` on current `origin/main`, and have the reviewer name the missing Linux opinion in its verdict. *Reasoning:* the ruling says a step that says `gh workflow run check.yml` takes the local `just check` in its place. The local run is not a Linux opinion, so the gap goes in the verdict for Björn to see. *Reversing:* the old sentence is kept in the new one, behind `gh workflow enable check.yml`.
- **The `testenv.yml` counterpart.** *Fork:* `just check` alone, or `just check` plus the workflow's compose and port steps. *Ruling:* `just check` plus the compose and port steps. `just check` runs `just shell`, the workflow's first check. `docker compose ... config -q` and `testenv/check-ports.sh` run in no recipe, so `docs/development.md` names them. *Reasoning:* with `just check` alone, a compose or port-map change would go unchecked until the workflow comes back. *Reversing:* n/a.
- **Descriptive mentions left alone.** *Fork:* reword every line that names `check.yml` or `testenv.yml`, or only the ones that tell an agent to dispatch or rely on them. *Ruling:* only those. The justfile and `scripts/gate-slot.sh` comments (`justfile:489`, `:834`, `gate-slot.sh:116`, `:120`), `test-inventory-conditional.txt:3` (CI), the workflow files and `docs/contract.md:428` (frozen) say what the workflows do when they run, and that is still true while they are disabled. *Reasoning:* the change stays docs-only, and the lines go back to being current the moment the workflows are enabled. *Reversing:* n/a.

## #2040: what a source's credential cannot write, asked before a write is drawn (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-24)

- **The split.** *Fork:* every adapter and every surface the ticket lists in one PR, or a first slice. *Ruling:* the SPI and the IPC read, TeamCity's answer, TeamCity's own view, and the shell surfaces that draw TeamCity's writes (the inbox's *Re-run*, the Builds frame's *Run…*, *Run on*, *Re-run*, both *Run again…* and the parameters' *Change…*). Jira, Confluence and Gitea issues are follow-ups, one per adapter, each owning its adapter's answer and the surfaces that draw its writes. *Reasoning:* the dispatch allows the split. A surface wired to an answer no adapter gives yet cannot be witnessed live, and TeamCity is the adapter the ticket measured. *Cost of reversing:* none; each follow-up adds its adapter's `refused_writes` and calls `askRefused` from its surfaces.
- **The shape of the answer.** *Fork:* a per-instance list of refused ops, new fields on each surface's DTO (`InboxEntry.actions`, `PipelineSettings`), or one batched per-entity read. *Ruling:* one command, `refused_writes(asks: Vec<WriteAsk>) -> Vec<RefusedWrite>`, each ask an op on an entity, each refusal with its reason. *Reasoning:* every permission model the ticket names is scoped below the instance (a TeamCity project, a Jira project, a Confluence space, a Gitea repository), so a per-instance answer would be wrong for half the entities. A field on a mirror read would turn the inbox's database read into a network read and make it wait on the slowest source. A separate read is asked after drawing, so a surface never waits for it, and batched, so the inbox asks once. *Cost of reversing:* one command and one SPI method (§10.8 `2040-refused-writes`).
- **A default on the SPI method.** *Fork:* no default, as ADR-0006 asks of `view` and `reachable_transitions`, or a default that answers nothing. *Ruling:* a default. *Reasoning:* nothing refused is the right answer for every adapter whose credential cannot be narrower than the adapter (mock, Uptime Kuma), and a default keeps `knobas:adapter@1.3.0` and every WASM guest unchanged. Nothing refused draws as today, so a missing override can only leave a write enabled, which is the state the ticket starts from. *Cost of reversing:* an override per adapter.
- **TeamCity: which permission each write needs.** *Fork:* the role names or the permission ids. *Ruling:* the permission ids from `GET /app/rest/users/current/permissions`, read with no locator: `run_build` for `run_build`, `trigger_build` and `rerun_build`, `edit_project` for `set_parameter`. *Reasoning:* measured on 2026.1.3 (#2040): a `PROJECT_VIEWER` holds `run_build` and not `edit_project`, and the parameter `PUT` is refused 403 for want of the right to edit the configuration. A custom role is a set of permissions, so the ids hold for it too. *Cost of reversing:* `grants::needs`.
- **TeamCity: where an assignment holds.** *Ruling:* an assignment holds when it is `isGlobalScope`, or names `_Root`, the configuration's project or any of its ancestors (`/app/rest/projects`, read as the sync reads it). *Reasoning:* a role given on a project holds in its subprojects, as the ticket warns. *Cost of reversing:* `Grants::refusal`.
- **TeamCity with per-project permissions off.** *Check:* measured on the seeded 2026.1.3 server, 2026-10-24. Its `perProjectPermissions` is `false`, and then every role is global: a user given `PROJECT_ADMIN` on `Payout` alone is answered `edit_project` with `isGlobalScope: true`, for `Payout` and `Ledger` alike, under every `project:` locator. With them on, the same role answers `isGlobalScope: false` and `"project": {"id": "Payout", …}`, names only the project it was given on, and a parameter `PUT` on `Ledger` is refused 403. *Ruling:* read the answer as it is in both modes. *Reasoning:* it is what the server enforces. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **The live test turns per-project permissions on.** *Fork:* witness the project-scoped shape only on wiremock, or turn the server's per-project permissions on for one test. *Ruling:* turn them on, through `PUT /app/rest/server/authSettings`, and put them back from a `Drop` guard; the test asserts they are back. *Reasoning:* the project-scoped shape is the claim the fake makes about TeamCity, and the seeded server cannot answer it otherwise. The suite holds the JVM lock, so no other run sees the setting. *Cost of reversing:* drop `PerProject` and the second half of the test.
- **No verdict.** *Ruling:* a permissions or projects read that fails, a project listing with a further page, and an entity whose project cannot be read each refuse nothing. In the app, an entity no configured source owns, a keychain or build failure, and an answer about a write nobody asked about refuse nothing too. In the shell, a rejected read refuses nothing. *Reasoning:* the ticket's direction: never refuse a write on a guess; the source still refuses it at write time. *Cost of reversing:* one branch each.
- **The wording.** *Ruling:* *This TeamCity user cannot run builds in Payout: it lacks the Run build permission* and *This TeamCity user cannot change the settings of Payout: it lacks the Edit project permission*. *Reasoning:* it names what to fix, in the shape #2030 gave Gitea (*it lacks the write:repository scope*). The project is named by its name, else its id. *Cost of reversing:* `Permission::reason`.
- **Disabled or absent.** *Ruling:* disabled with the reason, as `aria-disabled` and the reason as the title, the way #2030 drew the Code page's *New branch…*; a press opens nothing and queues nothing. *Change…* is drawn disabled too, rather than hidden. *Reasoning:* ADR-0020 rule 4: the user can be given the permission, so the reader can reach the state where the write is enabled. *Cost of reversing:* the components' attributes.
- **When it is asked.** *Ruling:* once per inbox ask set (a refresh that changes no row's writes asks nothing again), once per pipeline on the pipeline page and on the run page, and on every draw of a configuration's source view. No cache. *Reasoning:* the answer is live like a view (ADR-0020 rule 1), and #2030's merge-manager ruled against a per-token cache for the same reason: a replaced credential must show at once. A view draw costs two more requests (permissions, projects), sent after the configuration's, since the adapter has no runtime of its own to join them on. *Cost of reversing:* a map beside the source.
- **`PipelineSettings.parameter_write_op`.** *Fork:* have TeamCity answer `None` there for a user who may not edit, or leave it. *Ruling:* leave it; the Builds frame asks `refused_writes`. *Reasoning:* `None` carries no reason, so the parameters would lose *Change…* without saying why. *Cost of reversing:* one field.
- **`?fake-ipc`.** *Ruling:* the fake refuses nothing. *Reasoning:* every fake source's credential is the demo's, which may write. *Cost of reversing:* one handler.
- **Test seams.** *Fork:* confirm the seams with Björn, as the TDD skill asks, or pick them. *Ruling:* picked: TeamCity's `Source::refused_writes` and `Source::view` over wiremock, `sources::crud::refused_writes` over a fake source, `askRefused`/`refusalOf`, the mounted inbox, pipeline and run pages, and `live_teamcity_seeded.rs` with a minted `PROJECT_VIEWER`. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. *Cost of reversing:* none.

## #2040, merge review of #2051 (merge-manager, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **The SPI default.** *Fork:* no default on `Source::refused_writes`, as ADR-0020 gives `view` and the contract gives `reachable_transitions`, or the implementer's default that answers nothing. *Ruling:* keep the default. *Reasoning:* ADR-0020's "no default implementation" is stated for `view`, and the contract's for `reachable_transitions` because an empty answer there is a wrong answer (a workflow with no moves left). Here an empty answer is no verdict: the write is drawn as before, and the source still refuses it at write time. So a missing override costs what the ticket starts from and no more. Neither text asks every new `Source` method to have no default, and `pipeline_settings`, `undeclared_reason` and the run reads already have one. `knobas_sync::progress::Observed` forwards no defaulted method and narrates sync runs only, so the IPC read never goes through it. *Cost of reversing:* an override in every `impl Source for` in the tree.
- **WASM guests.** *Fork:* a WIT change so a guest can answer, or no verdict for now. *Ruling:* no verdict for now; no WIT change, no follow-up. *Reasoning:* `knobas:adapter@1.3.0` binds unchanged and a guest draws its writes as before. The first guest whose credential can be narrower than its adapter needs a minor WIT bump with an import beside `view`, and that guest's ticket owns it.
