Filing it now would be a ticket no guest asks for. *Cost of reversing:* one WIT function and the host's forwarding.
- **TeamCity's ancestry, and per-project permissions off.** *Check:* `Grants::refusal` holds an assignment that is global, on `_Root`, on the project or on any project in `ProjectTree::path`, which stops at `_Root` and at a project the listing does not name. With per-project permissions off, TeamCity answers every assignment `isGlobalScope`, and that is read as global. *Ruling:* right as written. *Reasoning:* a role given on a project holds below it, and with the setting off the server enforces every role globally, so the read matches what a write would meet. A viewer cannot be refused for an ancestor it cannot see: a role on a project makes the project visible. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **Any failure refuses nothing.** *Ruling:* right. *Reasoning:* the ticket rules out sending a write to find out. Refusing on a failed read would disable every TeamCity write on a transient error and give a reason that is not true, while the write's own refusal at write time still says why. The cost is a write drawn enabled that the source refuses after it was queued, which is today's behaviour. *Cost of reversing:* one branch each.
- **The live test's per-project toggle.** *Check:* `PerProject` is a `Drop` guard running through `knobas_live_cleanup::Cleanup`, on a thread and runtime of its own, so it puts the setting back on a pass and on a panic; a panic in the cleanup while unwinding goes to stderr, not an abort. It is dropped before `MintedViewer`, and a failed `PUT` turning the setting on still puts it back. A **killed** run reaches no `Drop`. The seeded TeamCity keeps its volume, and the test recorded the setting it found as the server's own, so a killed run would have left per-project permissions on for every later run. *Ruling:* fixed on the branch (*Fixed in passing*). The test puts the setting off first, as it removes a leftover viewer first, and asserts it off at the end. *Reasoning:* the seed leaves the setting off (measured 2026-10-24), and nothing else turns it on. *Cost of reversing:* `PerProject::off_if_left_on`.
- **The view's section reads.** *Check:* `64d08973` reads the grants only for the whole view and for the *Parameters* section. The toolbar is drawn only for the whole view, and *Parameters* is the one section with an editable value. *Ruling:* right. It touches the adapter crate after the live run at `f7460212`, so `just teamcity-live-seeded` ran again on the merge head.

## #2059: the status bar follows the sources that exist (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **The signal.** *Fork:* a backend event when a source is removed (a new §10.8 surface), or a frontend signal. *Ruling:* frontend. The shell re-reads its source list whenever the health store's membership changes. *Reasoning:* Settings already re-lists the sources after Remove, Uninstall and Add source and hands the store the new membership (`Health.replace`, the one operation that removes a row, #148). The store is the shell's and Settings' one shared instance, so the bar's list goes stale exactly when that membership changes. *Cost of reversing:* one `$derived` and one effect in `TfShell.svelte`.
- **The shell's `source:health` re-read.** *Fork:* keep it beside the new signal, or drop it. *Ruling:* drop it. *Reasoning:* its comment said that adding or removing a source changes its health reading first, and that premise was the bug: a removal sends no `source:health`. A reading for a source the store did not hold changes the membership, so the new signal catches that case. A reading for a source the store already held changes neither a name nor a role. *Cost of reversing:* one `listen`.
- **A restore counts as a membership change.** *Ruling:* after a restore, Settings re-lists the sources (`TfBackupSection`'s `onrestored`). *Reasoning:* the ticket lists restore among the paths. A restore only lands in a knobas with no data, so it brings sources and removes none, and until now the bar showed none of them until a restart. *Cost of reversing:* one prop.
- **Test seams.** *Ruling:* picked, since the loop runs unattended: the mounted shell over a real health store, and the mounted Settings over a real health store for each removal path. *Cost of reversing:* none.
## #2053: what a Confluence credential cannot write (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **The read.** *Check:* measured on the seeded Data Center 9.2.21, 2026-10-25, with a minted user. `/rest/api/space/{key}/permissions` (and `/permissions/user/{key}`) answer 403 to anyone but an administrator, and `?expand=permissions` on a space answers 500. A space has no `operations` expansion on Data Center, and a page's `operations` name `read`, `update`, `delete` and a `create` that a user with *Add page* is not answered, never a comment. `POST /rpc/json-rpc/confluenceservice-v2/getPermissions` with `["<key>"]` answers the user's own space permissions: `["view"]` for a viewer, `["view","modify","comment"]` for `confluence-users` on ENG, and the same over a personal access token with no XSRF header. *Ruling:* `comment` needs `comment` and `create_page` needs `modify` in the page's space, from `getPermissions`; `update_page` needs `update` among the page's operations. *Reasoning:* it is the one read Data Center gives an ordinary user, and it is a read. A page's `update` also says what its edit restrictions allow: a page restricted to the admin drops `update` for a user whose space permissions still say `modify` (measured). *Cost of reversing:* `grants.rs`.
- **The remote API.** *Fork:* depend on the JSON-RPC service, which Atlassian deprecates, or answer only what REST tells. *Ruling:* depend on it, and read its absence as no verdict. *Reasoning:* without it no comment or page create can be judged. A server whose remote API is off, or a later Confluence without it, fails that read, so its comments and creates are drawn as today and its edits are still judged from the page's operations. *Cost of reversing:* the `space_permissions` read.
- **Cloud.** *Check:* the ticket asks for the Cloud form to be measured too. The adapter refuses the Cloud flavor when it is built (`ConfluenceConfig`, #284), and no Cloud instance is seeded. *Ruling:* not measured; the answer is Data Center's. *Cost of reversing:* none until a Cloud dialect exists.
- **Which entity a create is asked about.** *Ruling:* the parent page, the entity `CreatePage` names, and its space. *Reasoning:* `WriteAsk` asks a create about the container its payload names, and every surface that offers a page has its parent at hand. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **The wording.** *Ruling:* *This Confluence user cannot comment in Engineering: it lacks the Add comment permission*, *… cannot add pages to Engineering: it lacks the Add page permission*, *… cannot edit pages in Engineering: it lacks the Add page permission*, and for a page its restrictions close, *… cannot edit SEPA payout retry design: the page's restrictions leave it out*. Where the space's permissions cannot be read, *… cannot edit SEPA payout retry design*. *Reasoning:* the names Confluence's space-permissions screen uses, in #2040's shape. *Cost of reversing:* `grants::refusal`.
- **No verdict.** *Ruling:* a page that cannot be read refuses none of its writes; a space whose permissions cannot be read refuses no comment or create in it. `refused_writes` never errors for Confluence. *Reasoning:* the merge-manager's #2051 ruling (a failed read refuses nothing), per entity, so one deleted page does not wipe the inbox's other answers. *Cost of reversing:* one branch each.
- **Reads in turn.** *Fork:* ask each page and space side by side (a `futures` dependency) or in turn. *Ruling:* in turn, each page once and each space once. *Reasoning:* a docs page asks one page; the inbox a handful; the client's rate limit serialises them anyway. *Cost of reversing:* one `join_all`.
- **The publish-target pickers.** *Fork:* draw the refusal only on each dialog's primary button, or in the shared `PublishTargetPicker`. *Ruling:* the picker asks about every hit and the chosen parent; a refused hit is drawn disabled with the reason and cannot be picked, a refused chosen parent (Settings' stored one) says why and announces no target, so *Publish*, *Save* and *Move N notes* stay disabled. Stand-up's *Publish to Confluence* asks about the stored target's page itself. *Reasoning:* one place for three dialogs, and the reader sees which pages are closed before picking. *Save* in Settings is not a Confluence write, but it sets where every later publish goes, and each would be refused. *Cost of reversing:* the picker's ask.
- **New page's *Under*.** *Ruling:* the dialog asks about the parent as it changes and draws *Create page* refused. *Reasoning:* *Under* can name another space than the page it opened from. *Cost of reversing:* the dialog's ask.
- **The inbox.** *Check:* a Confluence mention's row carries `comment` among its actions, but the inbox draws only `rerun_build` of a source's ops inline (`tf/inbox/inbox.ts`, `INLINE_OPS`), so it draws no Confluence write. *Ruling:* no change there. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **The live witness.** *Ruling:* the test mints a user and a private space it may only view (`POST /rest/api/space/_private`, then the space-permission `grant`), asks through the user's own personal access token, and deletes the token (its `204` checked), the space and the user from a `Drop` guard, the space and the user each checked gone; a killed run's are deleted by the next before it mints. *Reasoning:* the seeded space grants `confluence-users`, so a viewer of it needs the seeded permissions changed; a space of its own leaves the seed as it was, and the same user then witnesses the writer's case on ENG. *Cost of reversing:* the test.
- **Test seams.** *Ruling:* picked: `grants::refused` over a fake of its two reads, `live_confluence_seeded.rs` for the reads themselves, and the mounted Docs reader, *New page*, stand-up, Settings › Standup and Settings › Notes. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. *Cost of reversing:* none.

## #2053, merge review of #2057 (merge-manager, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **The JSON-RPC dependency.** *Check:* `getPermissions` goes through `ConfluenceHttp::rpc`, and any failure there (an error answer, a non-2xx, HTML or another shape) is an `Err`, which `grants::refused` keeps as `None` for that space. With the remote API off, or gone in a later Confluence, comments and creates are no verdict and drawn as before. An edit is still judged from the page's operations, with the reason that names no permission. The `modify` = *Add page* mapping is the remote API's own spelling of `EDITSPACE`, and the seeded 9.2.21 measured it both ways (`confluence-users` with *Add page* on ENG answers `modify`, a View-only user does not). *Ruling:* right. The implementer's ruling said this; the code and contract did not, so the module doc of `grants.rs` and contract §4.2's Confluence read row now say it. *Cost of reversing:* prose.
- **Settings' *Save* refusing a stored parent.** *Fork:* refuse, or only warn. *Ruling:* refuse, as the PR does. *Reasoning:* *Save* in *Change…* writes only the publish target. While the stored parent is refused, the only thing *Save* could save is that same stored value again, which changes nothing. The warning (`role="alert"`) is drawn either way, *Cancel* keeps the stored target, and a parent that is no verdict stays savable. Warning only would let a refused hit be saved too, so every later publish would be refused after it was queued, which is the behaviour #2053 exists to remove. *Cost of reversing:* the picker's `announce`.
- **The picker's cost.** *Check:* each distinct set of hits is one `refused_writes` call. In it, every hit is one page `GET` (up to 20, in turn) and each distinct space is one `getPermissions`. Spaces are cached within a call, not across calls, and the adapter is built afresh for each call. `find()` searches on every keystroke, so typing sends overlapping rounds. A dropped answer's reads still run. *Ruling:* acceptable for this PR, filed as #2063 (backlog). *Reasoning:* the picker opens rarely and the reads are plain GETs. Coalescing them is a timing change across three hosts' tests, or an unmeasured adapter read, and either one fails the fit test. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **The trait doc.** *Ruling:* `Source::refused_writes` no longer names which adapters answer. It says that an adapter whose credential can be narrower overrides it, and that one that does not override it answers nothing, which stays true as #2052 and #2054 land. *Cost of reversing:* prose.
- **The live run's head.** *Check:* `git diff eba61ff7..bac1af67 -- crates/` changes only `rustfmt` layout and doc comments, in `grants.rs`, `http.rs` and the live test. *Ruling:* the implementer's run covered bac1af67. My fixed-in-passing change to `grants.rs` changes what the page read decodes, so `just confluence-live` ran again on the merge head.
- **Fixed in passing.** These came from the Spec review. A page answered without `operations` was read as *no edit* and refused, though the module calls whatever cannot be read no verdict. A *Save section* stayed live in an editor opened before the refusal landed, or reopened by *Edit and resend*. The tree's *New page* was judged by the open page while it opens on the shown space. Each is fixed with a test that fails without it. *Ruling:* fixed on the branch. *Cost of reversing:* one guard each.
- **The live witness of the surfaces.** *Check:* the criterion asks for the surfaces witnessed on `just confluence-live`. The live test witnesses the adapter's answer through the minted viewer's own token, #2051's IPC tests witness the wire, and the component tests witness the drawing. *Ruling:* satisfied, in #2040's shape. *Cost of reversing:* none.
## #2056: one window-size step before every desktop-witness driver and live-shot (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **AeroSpace: detected, not switched on.** *Fork:* take live-shot's opt-in `LIVE_SHOT_AEROSPACE=1` into the witness, or detect AeroSpace. *Ruling:* detect it: when `aerospace list-workspaces --focused` answers, the window is fullscreened by its CG window id, whatever its width. `LIVE_SHOT_AEROSPACE` is gone, and live-shot runs the same step. This replaces the #1483 ruling *AeroSpace: optional, off by default*. *Reasoning:* an opt-in is what failed: the witness had none, and live-shot without the flag shot at whatever size the tiling gave. On a Mac without AeroSpace the probe costs one failed command. Fullscreening a window that is already wide enough keeps it from being resized while a driver runs, and the fullscreen ends with the window, so Björn's layout and workspaces are untouched. *Cost of reversing:* low; one branch in `witness_window_size`.
- **Without AeroSpace.** *Ruling:* a window narrower than the minimum is widened through a new `ax resize`, keeping its height; a refused resize is reported, not fatal, and the size read afterwards decides. *Reasoning:* other window managers may refuse or undo a resize, and the refusal below names the size either way. *Cost of reversing:* low.
- **The minimum.** *Ruling:* 1241 points wide, no height minimum. `desktop-witness-test.sh` reads it from the `@media (max-width: …)` block in `tickets.css` that hides `.tf-preview`. *Reasoning:* the preview is drawn above 1240 px, and on macOS the window is as wide as its web view. No driver reads anything a height hides. *Cost of reversing:* one constant.
- **The capture driver's path to the job.** *Fork:* reach PAY-231 by a path no breakpoint hides, or keep the Tickets preview. *Ruling:* keep the preview. *Reasoning:* the size step guarantees the preview is drawn, and the README records that ⌘K does not reach `PAY-231` on the demo profile. A second path would be a driver change no failure asks for. *Cost of reversing:* a driver step.
- **live-shot refuses below the minimum too.** *Ruling:* yes; it shares the step. *Reasoning:* the ticket asks for one step for all of them, and a shot below the breakpoint is not what a reader of Tickets sees on a normal window. *Cost of reversing:* a flag on the step.
## #2052: what a Jira user may not write, read from `mypermissions` (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **Measured first.** *Check:* on the seeded Jira 10.3.24 (Server), 2026-10-25. `GET /rest/api/2/mypermissions?projectKey=PAY` answers 75 keys, each `{"id","key","name","type","description","havePermission"}`; the four this adapter needs are `ADD_COMMENTS` (*Add Comments*), `TRANSITION_ISSUES` (*Transition Issues*), `WORK_ON_ISSUES` (*Work On Issues*) and `CREATE_ISSUES` (*Create Issues*). Adding `&permissions=…` changes nothing: the same 75 come back. An unknown project answers 404. The seeded projects' scheme (*Default software scheme*, 10000) gives every one of the four to `applicationRole`, any user with Jira Software access. A user minted without application access cannot sign in at all (401 on `myself`, then 403), and stays 403 after being given access within the same minute.
- **The project, not the issue.** *Fork:* `issueKey=` per ticket or `projectKey=` per project. *Ruling:* `projectKey`, from the key's prefix for a ticket and from the entity for a create. *Reasoning:* Jira answers a permission given through issue data (*Reporter*, *Current Assignee*) as held when the user meets it on any issue of the project, so a project answer can only refuse less than an issue answer, never more; and it is one read per project rather than per ticket on a busy day. *Cost of reversing:* `grants::refused`'s grouping and the query parameter.
- **`projectKey` alone.** *Fork:* the ticket's `&permissions=ADD_COMMENTS,…` or nothing more. *Ruling:* nothing more. *Reasoning:* the pinned WADL declares no `permissions` parameter on the resource, and the adapter sends only what it declares (`api.rs`, mockd's allowlist); measured, the filter changes nothing on Data Center. *Cost of reversing:* one query pair.
- **The wording.** *Ruling:* *This Jira user cannot comment in PAY: it lacks the Add Comments permission*, and *log work*, *move tickets*, *create tickets* for the other three, each naming the permission as Jira's permission scheme names it. *Reasoning:* #2040's shape, and the name is what an administrator finds on the scheme page. *Cost of reversing:* `grants::NEEDS`.
- **No verdict.** *Ruling:* a project whose read fails refuses nothing in that project and leaves the others answered; an op none of the four, a permission the answer leaves out, another source's entity and a key that is not one refuse nothing. *Reasoning:* #2040's rule, never refuse on a guess. *Cost of reversing:* one branch each.
- **The Rust `log_work` gates stay.** *Fork:* make `worklog::takes_a_worklog`, `takes_a_worklog_for` and `suggest::logging_namespaces` ask `refused_writes`, or leave them reading the template. *Ruling:* leave them. *Reasoning:* they answer whether a source takes worklogs at all (whether the entity is a ticket), and each answers by leaving something out: no draft, no row in *Log all*, no suggestion. Answering a refused credential there would hide the write rather than draw it disabled, against ADR-0020 rule 4, and would turn three database reads into network reads. The surfaces they feed draw the refusal instead: the draft's *Log*, the Day's *Log…* and *Log all*'s rows. *Cost of reversing:* a `refused_writes` call in each, and a reason to carry.
- **The ad-hoc suggestion** (`drafting.svelte.ts`, the ticket's `:132`). *Ruling:* unchanged. *Reasoning:* it re-targets a block onto a ticket, which is local; the write it leads to is the worklog draft's *Log* or *Log all*, both of which now draw the refusal. *Cost of reversing:* an ask in `offerAdHoc`.
- **The inbox.** *Ruling:* nothing to change. *Reasoning:* its rows draw one source op inline, `rerun_build` (`inbox.ts`' `INLINE_OPS`), which #2040 already gates for any source; no Jira write is drawn there. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **The status select.** *Ruling:* a refused move draws the select with only where the ticket stands, `aria-disabled` and the reason as its title, not `disabled`. *Reasoning:* `disabled` takes the title's tooltip away in WebKit and the focus with it; with no other option nothing can be picked, and the pick is guarded too. *Cost of reversing:* the attributes.
- **Start work's move.** *Fork:* draw the step with the reason and let *Run all steps* queue it, or skip it. *Ruling:* draw it with the reason, and *Run all steps* skips a refused, not yet settled move, which runs the flow on past it as *Skip* does (`start_work::skip`). *Reasoning:* a refused write is never queued (#2040); the other steps still run. *Cost of reversing:* one branch in `runAll`.
- **The comment box.** *Ruling:* *Comment* is `aria-disabled` with the reason as its title and beside it; the box keeps what was typed. It asks about `comment` for any source, so Gitea issues draw the same once #2054 answers. *Cost of reversing:* the attributes.
- **Create ticket.** *Fork:* hide a refused project, disable its option, or keep it pickable and disable *Create ticket*. *Ruling:* keep it pickable; picked, *Create ticket* is `aria-disabled` with the reason, and the reason stands above the fields. The dialog asks about every project it draws, so the run page and Standup both get it. *Reasoning:* a native option shows no title, and another project of the same list may take the ticket. *Cost of reversing:* the dialog's attributes.
- ***Log all*'s rows.** *Ruling:* a refused row is drawn unticked, its box `disabled` with the reason as its title, the reason under the key, and it is never sent. *Reasoning:* an `aria-disabled` checkbox still toggles, and the dialog sends what is ticked. *Cost of reversing:* the row's attributes.
- **The live witness.** *Fork:* a minted user without application access, or a minted user with it on a narrowed copy of a project's scheme. *Ruling:* the second, on OPS: the copy gives *Add Comments*, *Work On Issues* and *Create Issues* to `jira-administrators` alone, OPS is put on it for one test, and `Narrowed`'s `Drop` puts OPS back, deletes the copy and the user, and checks each; the next run first puts back a killed run's, on PAY's scheme (the seed makes both from one template). *Reasoning:* measured above, every seeded write is held by any Jira Software user and a user without access cannot sign in, so no user is refused anything without a scheme of its own. OPS holds one seeded ticket, whose `updated`, status, comments and worklogs, and the project's issue count, witness that nothing was written; NARROW, the first choice, holds no issue (its probe is deleted again). No suite reads OPS's permissions, and the suite holds the JVM lock. *Cost of reversing:* the test and its guard.
- **Test seams.** *Ruling:* picked: `grants`' unit tests, `Source::refused_writes` over a canned-bytes stub that records every request line (mockd serves no `mypermissions` and is frozen), the mounted job, conversation, start work, worklog draft, Day, *Log all*, run page and Standup, and `live_jira_seeded.rs`. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. *Cost of reversing:* none.
## #2052, merge review of #2058 (merge-manager, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **`Narrowed` on a pass, a panic and a killed run.** *Check:* the guard is built before the scheme copy is made, so a panic anywhere after it (the copy, the `PUT`, the mint, an assertion) unwinds through its `Drop`, which hands `unnarrow` to `knobas_live_cleanup::Cleanup` with OPS's own scheme id and checks each restoration (OPS's scheme, no copy left, the user 404). A killed run reaches no `Drop`; the next run's `Narrowed::new` calls `unnarrow` with no id first, which reads PAY's scheme (the seed makes both software projects from one template, measured both on *Default software scheme* 10000), puts OPS back if it differs, deletes any copy by name and the user, and checks the same three. `just jira-live` runs the suite `--test-threads=1`, so no other test of it meets OPS narrowed or the minted user, and the session removes Jira with its volumes afterwards. *Ruling:* right as it stands.
- **Start work's skipped move.** *Check:* *Run all steps* skips a refused move through `start_work::skip`, which settles it and runs the steps before and after it; the row then reads *skipped*. The reason under the row was hidden once the step was settled, so after the click the reader saw *skipped* and not why, although the reader had not chosen the skip. *Ruling:* fixed on the branch (*Fixed in passing*): the reason stays until the move succeeded. *Cost of reversing:* the condition.
- **`Source::refused_writes`' doc line.** *Check:* it said Jira answers nothing until #2052, which this branch makes false. #2057 (Confluence), merged while this was under review, rewrote it adapter-neutral (*an adapter whose credential can be narrower overrides it with a read of its own grants*), which is true for Jira too; this branch's own rewrite was dropped in the rebase. The §10.8 entry `2040-refused-writes.md` keeps its "until #2052, #2053 and #2054": it records what #2040 shipped. *Ruling:* nothing more to change. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **Cloud's form of the read.** *Check:* the ticket asked to measure Cloud's `mypermissions` if the adapter's Cloud flavor differs. the adapter refuses `flavor: cloud` at build time (`config.rs`; `source.rs`, `the_cloud_flavor_is_refused_at_build_time`), so no Cloud source reaches `refused_writes`. *Ruling:* nothing to measure; Cloud, which requires `permissions=`, is for the ticket that implements the flavor.
- **No §10.8 entry.** *Check:* no IPC, SPI method, DTO or migration changes; the adapter's new read is recorded in contract §4.2's Jira read row, as TeamCity's was in #2051. *Ruling:* right.
- **The live run.** The refactor after `87f4b047` (`NEEDS` as a struct of `WRITE_OP_*` constants, `issue_project`) touches the adapter crate the suite exercises, so `just jira-live` ran again on the merge head.
## #2054: Gitea writes outside its views answer refused_writes from the scope probes (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **A probe where the SPI said "read, never probed".** *Fork:* follow the ticket (answer from the probes #2030's views send) or the doc on `Source::refused_writes` and #2040's §10.8 entry (an adapter answers from a read and never sends a write to find out). *Ruling:* the ticket, and the doc and the entry now say an adapter never finds out with a write that *could change anything* (§10.8 `2054-gitea-refused-writes`, with an amendment line on #2040's entry). *Reasoning:* the rule was written for TeamCity, whose only candidate probe queues a build. Gitea has no read of a token's scopes, and #2030's merge-manager ruled its empty-bodied creates safe from the forges' source; the live test counts branches, issues and pull requests around them on both forges. The ticket is the contract and the doc comment is not a spec or an ADR. *Cost of reversing:* the override in `source.rs`.
- **Where the probe lives.** *Ruling:* `crates/knobas-source-gitea/src/grants.rs`, holding the categories, the probe, its reading and the reasons; `view/grants.rs` keeps `unread`, the read scopes and `narrow`, which now calls it. *Reasoning:* the ticket asks for one probe shared by both callers. *Cost of reversing:* a file move.
- **Repositories in turn, not side by side.** *Fork:* probe each repository the asks name concurrently, or one after another. *Ruling:* one after another; within a repository the two categories still go side by side. *Reasoning:* the crate has no `futures` dependency and a `JoinSet` needs `'static` borrows; every surface asks about one entity or one picked project, so a second repository is rare. *Cost of reversing:* a dependency and a `join_all`.
- **What is answered.** *Ruling:* an ask for an op the descriptor template declares, on an id this source issued; anything else is not answered and sends nothing. A probe that meets neither measured answer is no verdict. *Reasoning:* the SPI doc's "only for ops it declares", and #2040's no-verdict rule. *Cost of reversing:* one filter.
- **Create ticket: where it is asked.** *Fork:* at the *Create ticket* buttons (`TfRunTicket`, `TfStandup`), or in the one create-ticket dialog. *Ruling:* in `TfCreateTicket`, for the picked project, each time the pick changes; *Create ticket* in the dialog is drawn `aria-disabled` with the reason as its title, and a press files nothing. *Reasoning:* the buttons open the dialog before any project is chosen, and the projects come from several sources, so only the picked project has an answer. One place covers both surfaces, and a Jira project gets the same answer once #2052 lands. *Cost of reversing:* one effect and the button's attributes.
- **The status select.** *Fork:* `disabled`, or `aria-disabled` with the reason as its title. *Ruling:* `aria-disabled` and the title, and the select offers no other status, so opening it picks nothing; a pick is ignored. *Reasoning:* the shape #2040 gave buttons, which keeps the control focusable so its reason is reachable, and an empty offer is how the select already draws a workflow it could not read. *Cost of reversing:* the select's attributes.
- **The comment composer.** *Ruling:* the box stays editable; *Comment* is drawn `aria-disabled` with the reason, and a press queues nothing and keeps the words. *Reasoning:* the reader may want to keep a draft while a token is replaced. *Cost of reversing:* the button's attributes.
- **The inbox.** *Ruling:* no change. *Reasoning:* the inbox draws only `rerun_build` inline (`INLINE_OPS`); a Gitea row's *Approve* and *Comment* sit behind *Review*, which opens the pull request's view, and #2030 already narrows that. The inbox asks `refused_writes` for every inline op it draws, so an inline Gitea write added later is answered without a change here. The ticket says "only if an inline write is added there". *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **Seams.** *Fork:* confirm the seams with Björn, as the TDD skill asks, or pick them. *Ruling:* picked: `Source::refused_writes` over wiremock (`tests/it/grants.rs`), the mounted job page (`TfJobTalk.test.svelte.ts`), the run page's and Standup's dialog, and `live_gitea.rs` with two minted tokens on Gitea and Forgejo. *Reasoning:* the loop runs unattended. *Cost of reversing:* none.

The implementer's *Create ticket: where it is asked* ruling above is superseded by #2058's, which asks about every project the dialog draws. `Source::refused_writes`' doc now names no adapter (an override finds out as the paragraph above it allows), and the shell helper's doc names Gitea beside Jira and Confluence. *Cost of reversing:* none; the dropped commits are in the PR's history.

## #2050: a saved view's query is a declared path (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **Which reads become declared paths.** *Fork:* declare every key the projection reads (`kind`, `id`, `columns`, `keys` and `query` too), or the four the ticket names. *Ruling:* the four: the query (`source_query`, required), the board type, the sub-query and the sprint (optional). `kind`, `id`, `columns`, `keys` and `query` stay the frame's own shape, which the module doc of `knobas_sync::saved_views` states. *Reasoning:* the four are Jira's own words (`jql`, `type`, `sub_query`, `sprint`) and are what the ticket's instances list. The frame keys carry no source's name, and declaring them would change their shape rules (a board id is a number, columns an array of objects) for no reader. *Cost of reversing:* a field each, plus clause 6 rows.
- **The field names.** *Ruling:* `source_query`, `board_type`, `sub_query` and `sprint`, the names of the `sync.saved_view` columns and the `SavedViewSource` fields they fill. *Reasoning:* `source_query` is the name #1285 gave the query so it would keep no Jira word, and `KindPaths` already has `sprint_state`, which is a ticket's and not a view's. *Cost of reversing:* a rename across the mirror.
- **Optional paths in the minimum.** *Fork:* name only the required query in the minimum, or name the optional three as well. *Ruling:* `KindMinimum` gains `optional_paths`, empty everywhere but the saved view's. They are never refused for being missing, and their names are held to `KindPaths`' keys. *Reasoning:* story 2 says a role's minimum is written down as its paths, and the projection reads these three. *Cost of reversing:* one field.
- **Rows already mirrored.** *Ruling:* no re-sync and no migration. *Reasoning:* Jira's declaration names the keys its payloads have carried since #877, so the next run of an existing source projects every view to the same row, and a reader keeps their views and their settings (the upsert is keyed on the entity id). A declared string is read trimmed, so a JQL with leading or trailing blanks loses them, and a blank one becomes the empty query. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **Where the battery holds it.** *Ruling:* in two places. Clause 10's role check refuses a ticket-system claim whose saved-view kind declares no `source_query`, naming the path. Beside the Builds frame's checks, the battery refuses any kind on the `saved_view` frame that declares none, claimed or not. *Reasoning:* the projection keys on the frame, not on the claim, so a source that emits saved views without claiming the role is projected too. *Cost of reversing:* one assertion.
- **The role data check (#1199).** *Fork:* have `role::data` weigh the saved view's query on the records too, or leave it to required kinds. *Ruling:* leave it. It weighs required kinds only, as before; the battery's clause 6 still weighs every declared path. *Reasoning:* a miss there stops the shell drawing the role, so a view whose query never resolved would cost a source its Tickets surface for an optional kind. *Cost of reversing:* a loop over `optional_kinds`.
- **The sprint's shape.** *Ruling:* an object (`Wanted::Object`, `Shape::Object`), read as the first declared candidate that is one. *Reasoning:* the shell draws its `name` and `end_date`, and the projection already kept only an object. *Cost of reversing:* one arm each.
- **The words for a view with no query.** *Ruling:* the source line drops the colon and the code (*Kestrel decides which tickets, from the Scrum board Customs flow, active sprint Sprint 9. Read again at every sync…*). View settings draws no query block, and says *knobas reads it again at every sync* in place of *runs its query at every sync*. A sub-query with no query still shows, after the colon. *Reasoning:* prototype-6's sentence with the clause it no longer has taken out. With no query there is no query for knobas to run. *Cost of reversing:* the `savedViewQueries` helper.
- **The fake's second ticket system.** *Ruling:* fake Kestrel's saved-view kind declares `source_query` at `filter.text` and `board_type` at `layout`, and no sub-query or sprint. Its view keeps its query and board type and carries neither of the others. The fake Jira adapter declares the real adapter's four paths. `fake-tauri.test.ts` holds every fixture saved view to what its adapter declares. *Reasoning:* with the path declared, the backend can give Kestrel's query, and a required path is what a real second system would declare. The no-query drawing is witnessed by the component tests. *Cost of reversing:* two fixture lines.
- **The sync test's Jira.** *Ruling:* `tests/it/jira_views.rs`'s fake Jira declares Jira's four paths, spelled in the test. The Jira descriptor's unit test pins the same four, and `knobas-app`'s `jira_views_ipc.rs` projects under the real descriptor. No assertion of an existing test changed; the non-Jira test's adapter moved to a `FORGE` constant that declares its own paths. *Reasoning:* `knobas-sync` does not depend on the Jira adapter. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **Test seams.** *Ruling:* picked, since the loop runs unattended: `role::check`, the battery's behaviours, `run_once` over a scratch database, the Jira descriptor, the mounted Tickets page, and the fake's handlers. *Cost of reversing:* none.

### #2050: merge-manager's review (Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **`UPSERT_VIEWS`' declared reads against rows already mirrored.** *Check:* Jira declares `jql`, `type`, `sub_query` and `sprint`, the keys `crate::views` writes. `declared_string!` takes the first non-blank string, trimmed; the old reads took `->>` untrimmed. Jira's `type` is `scrum`, `kanban`, `simple` or null, and its `sub_query` was already non-blank or null, so only blanks around a JQL or a sub-query differ. The sprint is still the object or none. *Ruling:* the implementer's "no re-sync, no migration" stands. The upsert rewrites every column and `last_read` at every sync, nothing compares a row with its last version, `is_new` and `hidden` live on `knobas.ticket_view`, which the projection does not write, and `sync.saved_view.query` (what the keys were read with) is untouched. So a row an older build synced keeps its view and settings, and the trim shows nowhere but in the drawn query. The §10.8 entry now names all three trimmed strings. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **Could the frame check refuse a source that installs today?** *Check:* the battery's frame check runs only in an adapter's own tests (`contract::battery`). At install and at an update's check, `manifest::check` runs `role::check` (clause 10). `load_installed` and a restore's reinstall go through `install::load_one`, which runs no role check. No adapter on main but Jira uses the saved-view frame: the WASM fixture and the adapter SDK don't. *Ruling:* no break on upgrade. An external adapter installed before this change keeps loading; its views draw no query until it declares one. A new install or update of one that lacks `source_query` is refused by name, which is what a frozen minimum's §10.8 entry is there to announce. The entry now says so. *Cost of reversing:* none.
- **The ADR-0029 edit.** *Fork:* a change to Björn's decision, or a clarification. *Ruling:* a clarification, inside an agent's authority. ADR-0029 already rules that every role requires its read side through declared paths, and that `role::MINIMUMS` is the normative list, amended by its §10.8 entry. The edited bullet describes the role's shape, as #1224 and #1225 edited it on 2026-10-19 (`f2bfdc72`). Spec #1192's stories 2 and 7 and ticket #2050 ask for this path. *Cost of reversing:* one clause of a sentence.
- **The frame's fixed keys stay undeclared.** *Ruling:* agreed. None of `kind`, `id`, `columns`, `keys` or `query` names a source, and the ticket's criterion is "no key named after Jira". The old module doc counted `query` as Jira's, but the shell never reads `sync.saved_view.query`. An adapter author could find these keys only in `knobas_sync::saved_views`' module doc, so `Frame`'s doc now names them beside the declared paths (*Fixed in passing*). *Cost of reversing:* a field each, if a source's own shape ever needs one.

## #2065: a pull request's tabs draw the source's muted lines where it put them (implementer, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **What a muted line is.** *Fork:* any muted row with no entity, as the ticket words it, or the whole block `view::muted_line` writes. *Ruling:* an untitled `entities` block with at least one row, every row muted, with no entity and no chip. *Reasoning:* a muted row with no entity is also the note a cut list ends on (Gitea's `rows::left_out`, inside the commit list), and TeamCity's muted test is a muted row with no entity but the chip `muted`. Taking single rows would pull the cut note out of *Commits* and change a tab no ticket asked to change. *Cost of reversing:* `linesOf` in `tf/pr/pr.ts`.
- **The unread checks in *Ready to merge?*.** *Fork:* take Gitea's *Checks could not be read* line out of the checks everywhere, or keep it as *Ready to merge?*'s checks line. *Ruling:* the Overview tab draws it as a line, not a row of the *Checks* table. *Ready to merge?* still draws it in the checks' place when the overview has no checks and its first list is a line, as `checksLine` has since #841. *Reasoning:* the ticket keeps lines out of the checks and draws them as lines. The side panel's checks line is a line, drawn as the source wrote it, and dropping it would leave the panel silent about checks it could not read. *Cost of reversing:* `checksPlace` in `pr.ts`.
- **An empty tab beside a line.** *Ruling:* *No comments yet.* and *No commits.* are drawn only when the tab holds nothing at all, line included. *Reasoning:* the ticket's first criterion. A line says why the tab holds nothing, so the empty sentence would contradict it. *Cost of reversing:* one condition each in `TfPr.svelte`.
- **The fake's read-only pull request.** *Ruling:* `mock:fx-rates#88`, not a new corpus row. Its *Conversation* opens on Gitea's line with jonas's approval under it, and every write is drawn disabled with the write scope `grants.rs` names. *Reasoning:* a new row would move the counts other fixtures and tests read. A token with `read:repository` and `read:user` can write nothing, and #2043 draws those writes disabled, so a fake that offered them would not be that token. *Cost of reversing:* `READ_ONLY_PR` in `fake/views/pulls.ts`.
- **The sweep.** *Ruling:* `tf/repo/repo.ts`'s `viewRows`, which took the first `entities` block of a repository's *Branches* and *Commits*, now takes every `entities` block in order. *Branches* already draws a row with no entity and no meta as a note, and *Commits* draws it dimmed, as both draw a cut list's note. Named safe: `run.ts`'s `rowsOf` already takes every list, `branchOptions` and `branchStanding` pick rows by entity id, `TfItem` draws every block, and the diff readers (`files.ts`, `TfRepoCommit`, `TfRepoCompare`, `TfRepoFiles`) read a diff or file block from sections no adapter writes a line into. *Cost of reversing:* one line.
- **Test seams.** *Ruling:* picked, since the loop runs unattended: the mounted pull request page (`TfPr.test.svelte.ts`), `viewRows`, and the fake's `entity_view` handler. *Cost of reversing:* none.

## #2065 review: PR #2066 (merge-manager, Opus, 2026-10-25)

- **`linesOf`'s definition.** *Fork:* tighten it further (no url, no meta) or keep it. *Ruling:* keep it. *Reasoning:* both `muted_line` callers (`checks.rs:67`, `pr.rs:339`) match it. Gitea's real checks block is titled *Checks* and its rows carry a chip, so no check is taken for a line. TeamCity's muted test carries the chip `muted`, so it stays in its list, and *Tests* is read through `run_tests`, not `linesOf`. The one row it can take is a Gitea commit list whose every record failed to parse, so the block holds only its cut note (`pr.rs:217`). That note is then drawn as a dim line, not a dim row, and loses nothing, because the commit table never drew a note's link either. *Cost of reversing:* one condition in `linesOf`.
- **The gate-scope comment rewrap (`testenv/desktop-witness-lib.sh:586`).** *Fork:* keep the directory pin on `app/src/lib/shell` to be safe, or accept the rewrap. *Ruling:* accept. *Reasoning:* no `testenv/*.sh` reads a file under `app/src/lib/shell`. The only mention was this comment, and `test-witness.ts` reads `testenv/desktop-witness/drivers/`, not the other way round. It is a vitest file, so `check-front` runs it when it changes, and a driver change sits under `testenv/` and takes the full gate. After the rewrap, the pins `gate-scope.sh` computes hold no directory under `app/src`. *Cost of reversing:* re-wrapping one comment line.

Both tabs already draw a row with no entity as a note. A text filter could hide such a line, but only on a section that does not exist yet. *Cost of reversing:* a `linesOf`-style split in `TfRepo`.
